changes_bullets: `FaceRoute` GAINS THE THREE PIECES ZENOH HOLDS, no more and no fewer. `tokens` (wire id -> resolved keyexpr) is the token twin of `subs` and the same stored form the receiving endpoint keeps in its own `peer_token_table`. `local_tokens` (advertised keyexpr -> the id that advertisement carried) is zenoh's `face_hat.local_tokens` and is load-bearing rather than bookkeeping: the receiver keys its token table by the declared id, so a retraction can only be the ordinary id-only form if something remembered the id. `token_interests` is the GATE -- zenoh's `remote_interests` filtered by `options.tokens() && i.matches(res)` (hat/router/token.rs `propagate_simple_token_to`), which is the ROUTER hat's rule and deliberately not the CLIENT hat's broadcast-to-every-face, because a face that never asked has no liveliness subscriber to fire.

`record_declare` GAINS THE TWO ARMS AND FEEDS NO ROUTE CACHE. A `DeclToken` resolves through the source face's aliases, is recorded first-declaration-wins (mirroring the endpoint registry's `Entry::Vacant`, since rebinding an id would make the later id-only retraction name a keyexpr the token was never declared on), and is then advertised. An `UndeclToken` looks the id up FIRST and falls back to the `ext_wire_expr` the retraction carries -- the same two-step in the same order as R311y769's fix on `liveliness_subscriber.rs`, because a sourced retraction is identified by KEYEXPR with `id == 0` and a table that only ever looked the id up would discard every one of them. Neither arm bumps `subscriptions_changed`: a token is not a destination, so the Push route cache is untouched.

`record_interest` ANSWERS THE TOKENS KIND, and the `!body.su()` early return becomes a `!wants_subscribers && !wants_tokens` one. `dump_current_tokens` sends the tokens held on other faces stamped with the soliciting interest_id, and the ADVERTISED ID follows upstream's `make_token_id` exactly: 0 for a CURRENT-only interest, allocated-and-remembered otherwise. That distinction is not cosmetic -- a CURRENT-only interest has no future to retract into, while a CURRENT+FUTURE one must be retractable by id later. ONE Final still closes the whole interest however many kinds it named, which is upstream's single post-dump `if mode.current()` block.

`remove_face` RETRACTS WHAT THE DEPARTED FACE HELD, deduplicated by keyexpr, which is zenoh's `close_face` draining `hat_face.remote_tokens` into `undeclare_simple_token` (hat/router/mod.rs:541-544). `propagate_token_forget` emits nothing while ANY face still holds the same keyexpr -- upstream's `simple_tokens(res)`-is-empty guard -- and picks between two shapes: the id-only retraction when `local_tokens` remembers an id, and the SOURCED one-shot (id 0 plus the keyexpr in an `ext_wire_expr`) when the face has a matching non-aggregate interest it was never declared to. The second arm is reachable by a real shape rather than defensive: pico's `z_liveliness_declare_subscriber` sends FUTURE alone when history is off (net/liveliness.c:202), so such a face never receives a declaration for a token that predates it.

Round 1838.decision_summary:
THE STAR ROUTER LEARNS THE LIVELINESS PLANE, and the reason it is allowed to is the same test that forbade the queryable one. Two atoms carried the clause -- `liveliness-subscriber` ("the RouteTable does not route the token plane at all ... a dropped face leaves its tokens permanently alive, where zenoh's close_face drains and undeclares them") and `routing-routes` ("no liveliness-token routing") -- and R311y802 had just spent a round disproving a residual of exactly that shape, so the first thing this round did was try to disprove this one. It does not disprove. R311y802's argument was about MESSAGE KINDS: `RouteTable::observe` dispatches Declare, Push and Interest and nothing else (routing.rs:397-405), so a queryable advertised from there would invite a `Request` no arm could answer, and the empty dump is truthful. The liveliness plane PASSES that test rather than escaping it -- a `DeclareToken` IS the delivery to a liveliness subscriber, an `UndeclareToken` IS the retraction, a TOKENS `Interest` IS the ask, and every one of those is a kind this table already dispatched. So the hole was real: `record_declare` matched only the keyexpr and subscriber arms and a token fell through to the catch-all, which means a liveliness subscriber behind a wz `--router` read an EMPTY world however many holders shared that router, and a holder that dropped stayed alive in every observer forever.

The other thing checked before writing code was WHICH SUBSTRATE. `routing-token-tables` describes a token plane that is already built and already pico-witnessed, and it would have been easy to read the shared clause and conclude the work was done. It is a different forwarder: `--router-hat` builds `RouterForwarder`, `--peer` builds `LinkstateForwarder`, and both got their token planes in R311y509. `--router` builds `RoutingForwarder` over `RouteTable`, and that one had nothing. Reading each substrate's own code rather than the clause is what separated them, which is the rule two atoms naming one residual has cost this workspace before.

The retraction half is the item R311y802 left in its own carry: it closed the router-generated retraction on the subscriber and queryable planes and recorded that the liveliness plane had no witness for it. It has one now, and the driver is the one that round found -- kill the foreign process rather than stopping it politely, because a peer that says nothing is the only way to make the ROUTER produce the withdrawal.

Round 1839.decision_summary:
FIVE DECLARATION BODIES LEARN TO READ AN EXTENSION CHAIN THEY WERE THE ONLY
IMPLEMENTATION IGNORING, and the clause that named it in four atoms understated
what it cost. `declare-keyexpr`, `declare-subscriber`, `declare-token` and
`declare-final` each carried a residual filed as LATENT: "the generated
Decl<X> decoder does not skip a Z-flagged body ext chain ... zenoh's writer
never sets the bit, so there is no current exposure". Picking it was the y801
rule -- one implementation closing a clause four atoms share beats a deeper
single-atom residual -- and it was what remained after y801 closed the ext_qos
clause those same four shared.

The first half of the clause is right and was verified on both upstreams by
direct read. Every declaration body carries `Z` at header bit 7 meaning "an
extension chain follows", and both upstreams consume it UNCONDITIONALLY: zenoh
loops `extension::skip` / `skip_all` per body (zenoh-codec/src/network/
declare.rs:319 DeclareKeyExpr, :377 UndeclareKeyExpr, :452 DeclareSubscriber,
:826 DeclareToken, :255 Final) and pico calls `_z_msg_ext_skip_non_mandatories`
/ `_z_msg_ext_decode_iter` at the same five sites (src/protocol/codec/
declarations.c:181-191, :192-200, :259-267, :301-309, :314-321). Neither 1.5.0
WRITER sets the bit on any of them, so wz emitted the same bytes as before and
still does; this is the forward-compatibility half of the contract, and wz was
the only one of the three implementations without it.

THE SECOND HALF -- "no current exposure" -- IS WHAT THE ROUND CORRECTS. A
DECLARE batch is a run of self-delimiting records with no per-record length
prefix, so record N+1 is found only by having fully decoded record N; wz's own
`parse_frame_payload` header says exactly that. An unconsumed chain therefore
does not fail its own record. It leaves the cursor mid-message, the next
`decode_one_record` reads the ext header byte `0x21` as a network MID
(`0x21 & 0x1F == 0x01`, which is no N_MID), and the WHOLE REMAINDER of the
frame is absorbed as one `NetworkMessage::Unknown`. The cost is every record
after the Z-flagged one, silently. `passive.rs:2718-2724` had already written
that failure mode down for its own fixture without anyone connecting it to the
five bodies that could produce it.

THE SCOPE WAS MEASURED RATHER THAN INHERITED FROM THE CLAUSES. The four atoms
name four codecs; the actual population is FIVE, because `declare-keyexpr` owns
two bodies and `undecl_kexpr` is the one Undecl_* body without a chain -- its
three siblings all have one because their SOURCED form rides an `ext_keyexpr`,
and this body simply has no ext of its own to have prompted the same work. Two
of the five did not model bit 7 AT ALL: `decl_kexpr.scxml` and
`decl_final.scxml` declared no `Z` flag, so there was no accessor to have
ignored. DeclFinal is additionally the `Declare` variant's CATCH-ALL body, so an
unknown declaration kind decodes through it -- and wz ABSORBS an unknown
declaration where both upstreams reject the whole message, which makes wz the
implementation for which consuming that chain changes an outcome rather than
tidying one.

Each new test in `wz-session-core` `network_message.rs` therefore puts an ordinary `Declare(UndeclKexpr id = 42)` AFTER the Z-flagged record and asserts THAT survives with its id intact, which a desynchronised cursor cannot produce. One per body (decl_subscriber, decl_token, decl_kexpr, undecl_kexpr, decl_final), one for an UNKNOWN declaration MID through the DeclFinal catch-all, and one round-trip. The decl_subscriber fixture is the only MULTI-entry chain (first entry sets its own `Z`), so a decoder consuming exactly one entry fails there and passes every single-entry sibling.

Round 1840.decision_summary:
THE LAST UNWIRED ACCEPTOR SCHEME IS WIRED, and the residual that named it was
shared by EIGHT atoms of which SEVEN had already paid it without the registry
hearing about it. `transport-link-{quic,quic-datagram,tls,ws,unixsock,vsock,
unixpipe,serial}` each carried one clause in the same words -- "a primitive NOT
wired into accept_locator" -- and picking it was the y801/y804 rule again: one
implementation closing a clause many atoms share beats a deeper single-atom
residual.

THE FIRST WORK WAS MEASURING WHICH OF THE EIGHT STILL HELD, and the answer was
one. Reading `bind_locator`'s whole match (session_open.rs) rather than the eight
clauses shows every scheme dispatched: ws at R311y374, tls at R311y375, unixsock
/ vsock / unixpipe at R311y378-380 (multi-client at y392), udp at R311y381-382,
quic at R311y401, quic-datagram at R311y408. Each clause was ACCURATE WHEN
WRITTEN and went stale when that scheme's own wiring round landed; the cited
`session_open.rs` line numbers no longer name the arms they name. That is the
debt-47 shape -- a registry reason outliving the code it describes -- and it is
recorded on all seven rather than left to be re-derived. udp is the one atom that
had already noticed, at R311y382.

SERIAL WAS THE ONE STILL HOLDING, and its clause was right: `accept_serial` had
NO production caller. `bind_locator`'s `AnyLocator::Serial` arm returned a typed
`Unsupported` reading "serial accept is a tty open (accept_serial), not a listen
bind; unwired" -- a true observation used as a reason not to wire it. The seam
does not require a listen queue, only a `BoundListener` that can accept, and two
non-socket siblings had already established that (unixpipe's FIFO rendezvous, the
udp demux). So a `serial/<dev>#baudrate=<n>` LISTEN STRING reached nothing: the
only route to a wz serial acceptor was to hand-compose `DialedLink::Serial`,
which is exactly what both the wz<->wz PTY e2e and the foreign pico witness did.

UPSTREAM SUPPLIED THE SHAPE, INCLUDING THE PART THAT LOOKS LIKE AN OMISSION.
zenoh's serial listener creates NO port at bind either -- `new_listener` records
the endpoint and its accept task opens the device (zenoh-link-serial/src/
unicast.rs:321-373, the `receive` helper opening `ZSerial` then `accept()`ing at
:436-453) -- so `BoundListener::Serial` holding a `SerialListener` and opening
the tty per-accept is parity rather than an approximation of it. Upstream also
gates re-accept on the previous link having dropped (`is_connected`,
unicast.rs:430-433), i.e. ONE live link per tty, which is why wz's acceptor is
the first `supports_mesh_multi_peer == false` since R311y404 rather than a
mesh-capable one that happens to yield a single face.

THE ACCEPT IS SPLIT, AND THAT IS THE ONE PLACE THE OBVIOUS WIRING WOULD HAVE BEEN
WRONG. `accept_serial` is open-tty-plus-Responder-handshake in one call, and the
handshake half BLOCKS until the peer sends `INIT` (retrying on `RESET` the way
`_z_connect_serial` does, serial_protocol.c:255-280). Calling it from
`accept_raw` would put an unbounded peer-controlled wait on the accept path. So
`accept_raw` runs only the local tty open and `AcceptedLink::handshake` runs the
handshake -- the same deferral tls and quic use for their crypto, reached here
for a different reason: this is the only accept in the enum that completes
before any peer has arrived.
verification_bullets: SEVEN DAMAGE PROBES, each run one at a time against the real lane command, and the map is per-clause rather than global. P1 restores the pre-round `Unsupported` bind arm: all FOUR new tests red and the two pre-existing hand-composed ones stay GREEN -- that is the measurement that the transport tests prove nothing about the seam, not an argument that they do not. P2 inlines the Responder handshake into `accept_raw` (the obvious wiring): reds exactly the two tests whose peer is SILENT, which is the deferral clause itself. P3 removes the `armed` gate so a second accept re-opens the device: reds only the parking test. P4 and P5 flip the `BoundListener` / `AcceptedLink` mesh predicates independently: each reds only the test that asserts its own twin. P6 points `interceptor_link` at `InterceptorLink::Tcp` and P7 renders the address as the log word: each reds only the bind test, at the advertised-locator round-trip and the address assertion respectively.

THE FOREIGN WITNESS WAS RUN AND THEN FALSIFIED, not merely re-pointed. A real zenoh-pico `z_pub` built with `Z_FEATURE_LINK_SERIAL` establishes over a serial link against wz's LISTEN STRING and its Put is delivered byte-exact: 2 passed in 22.22s, both locator shapes (`#config` and `?metadata#config`). Under P1 the same two legs fail at `accept_endpoint` with `Unsupported { "listen/accept is wired only for tcp; probe: serial accept unwired" }` -- so the foreign green is a claim about the seam and not about the tty.

THE DISCRIMINATORS ARE PLACED WHERE A WRONG IMPLEMENTATION SHOWS, not where the feature is visible. The bind test binds a device that DOES NOT EXIST, because a bind that opens the tty would `NotFound` there and that is the only thing separating "records an endpoint" from "opens the device". The deferral test gives the accept a peer that has written NOTHING, because a handshake-inline accept cannot return. The parking test asserts the second accept neither succeeds NOR fails but does not complete at all, because all three outcomes are implementable and only one is right (an `Ok` puts a second fd on a live tty; an `Err` re-arms the R311y382 F2 throttle spin). The advertised locator is checked by PARSING IT BACK to the endpoint it was bound from, the R311y470 lesson, because that string is flooded to peers.

THE POPULATION WAS READ, NOT ASSUMED: 5 passed / 0 filtered out frag-off and 6 / 0 frag-on, on a file whose gate is `transport-link-serial` -- the zero-population trap has fired twice in this workspace on exactly this shape.

COUNT GUARDS WERE MEASURED BEFORE THE PUSH, MECHANICALLY. All 90 count-guarded `cargo test` invocations in run-ci.sh were resolved against the four new test names, by package selection and by target filter: exactly the two C1t `--test serial_pty_e2e` lines can select them (every other guarded run names a different `--test` target or is `--lib`, which cannot reach an integration target), and there is no guarded run over wz-runtime-tokio with no target filter at all. Both were moved in this commit.

C1bz first read 187 against a budget of 190, and chasing the missing two found a real defect: `SerialListener` had been placed BETWEEN `BoundListener`'s doc comment and its `pub enum`, so the enum's documentation silently re-attached to a `#[cfg]`-gated struct and vanished from the default build, taking its two `accept_bound` private-link findings with it. The struct moved below the enum, the count read 189, and the honest budget move is the ONE link the round genuinely removed. The three-way difference was established by running rustdoc against HEAD and against the working tree and diffing the error SETS, not by reasoning about which links the diff deleted -- that reasoning had produced the wrong answer.

carry_forward_bullets: THE GAP THAT LET IT THROUGH IS NAMED AND NOT CLOSED: no local step in R311y804 ran clippy over the crate it changed. `cargo check --all-features --all-targets` was run and passes on this byte; the lane that fails is `cargo clippy ... -D warnings`. FOUR JOBS FAILING ON ONE TARGET IS A PROPERTY OF THE JOB LAYOUT worth remembering when reading a red: the count of red jobs is not the count of problems. Nothing measures how many lanes share a compile target, so the next multi-job red will have to be read the same way -- by reproducing one lane and re-running the others.
changes_bullets: THE FIX IS ONE ATTRIBUTE plus the reason for it. `#[allow(clippy::identity_op)]` on `a_z_flagged_decl_kexpr_does_not_swallow_the_next_record` (wz-session-core/src/network_message.rs), with a comment recording that the OR spells a MID and a flag rather than an arithmetic identity, that the lint is correct and the intent is not what it measures, and which round shipped it.
Round 1841.decision_summary:
R1839'S HOSTED RUN WAS RED IN FOUR JOBS AND THE CAUSE WAS ONE LINE. The failing
steps were Layer C1bf (wz-runtime-tokio --all-features clippy), C1h
(wz-session-core arbitrary-subset composability matrix), C1ax (routing-namespace)
and C1bn (passive-dissection RUN) -- four jobs, four lanes, and every one of them
compiles `wz-session-core`'s lib TEST target under `-D warnings`. The finding is
`clippy::identity_op` on a hand-assembled fixture byte R1839 added:
`0x00 | 0x80, // DeclKexpr MID 0x00 | Z`.

THE LINT IS RIGHT ABOUT THE ARITHMETIC AND WRONG ABOUT THE INTENT, so the byte
stays and the lint is silenced at that one test. The `<MID> | 0x80` spelling is
what makes the group of six Z-flagged fixtures readable -- each names its
declaration MID and then sets bit 7 (`0x06 | 0x80` DeclToken, `0x01 | 0x80`
UndeclKexpr, and so on). DeclKexpr's MID is 0x00, which makes the OR an identity;
collapsing it to a bare `0x80` would leave exactly one fixture in the group not
saying which body it is, and that fixture is the one whose whole point is that
`decl_kexpr.scxml` did not model bit 7 at all.

THE ATTRIBUTION IS EXACT AND SO IS THE GAP IT NAMES. R311y804 ran Layer C1, Layer
B, Layer F, C1bz, `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo check -p wz-session-core
--all-features --all-targets` before pushing -- `cargo check`, not `cargo
clippy`, so a clippy-only finding in a test target was outside everything it ran.
The four hosted jobs are not four problems; they are four lanes that happen to
compile the same target with the same flag, which is why the payoff is one line
and not four.
verification_bullets: MEASURED IN THAT ORDER, WHICH IS THE FALSIFICATION. Layer C1bf reproduced the hosted red locally BEFORE the change (`error: this operation has no effect --> network_message.rs:862:13`, `could not compile wz-session-core (lib test)`); after the change C1bf, C1h, C1ax and C1bn all pass -- 69s / 61s / 64s / 51s. Removing the attribute restores the red, which is what running the lane before the fix established rather than asserted.

ALL FOUR RED LANES WERE RUN, not just the one whose name says clippy. Confirming that C1h / C1ax / C1bn recover from the same one-line change is what turns "four jobs, one cause" from a plausible reading of the step names into a measurement.

carry_forward_bullets: TWO OF THE THREE RESIDUALS ARE STILL OPEN AND ARE NOW THE ATOM'S WHOLE REMAINDER: the open path returns after the FIRST locator that reaches Established (session_open.rs:4435-4453) where pico, in peer mode, opens locator[0] and adds every remaining one via `_z_new_peer` (session.c:174-186); and there is no retry / backoff / exit_on_failure at all (`DialConfig` carries per-scheme cert material and nothing else, session_open.rs:262-274, against zenoh's `period_init_ms` / `period_max_ms` / `period_increase_factor`). The first is the LARGER of the two and it is what `StaticConfigError::ListenWithConnect` is waiting on -- gaining a `_z_new_peer` analog converts that refusal into pico's `Z_FEATURE_UNICAST_PEER == 1` arm, listen at index 0 and the connect tail behind it, which is why `StaticConfig.locators` is a list holding one entry rather than one string.

THE LISTEN ARM IS TOKIO-ONLY, DELIBERATELY AND NOT SILENTLY. `resolve_static_config` is pure and reaches the MCU profile through `wz-runtime-coop`'s existing `pub use wz_session_core::scout_static` re-export, so the RESOLUTION composes on both; what is tokio-only is the accept half it dispatches to, because `wz-runtime-coop` has no accept seam of its own here. Nothing measures whether a coop consumer would want one.

DEBT 70 COST THIS ROUND TWO DETOURS AND IS STILL OPEN: `bx` routed to pc3 and refused for a missing `actionlint`, twice, and every remote run here had to be pinned with `--host pc2`. The refusal message does not name that escape hatch.

THE FIRST TEST RUN OF THIS ROUND WAS VACUOUS AND WAS CAUGHT BY READING THE COUNT, NOT THE STATUS: `cargo test -p wz-session-core --lib scout_static` WITHOUT `--features scouting-static` selects zero tests and exits 0, because the whole module is gated. It ran for twelve minutes on a build machine before the gate was noticed. Nothing warns about a filter that matches nothing outside the `_runci_guarded_test` helper, which is exactly the property that helper exists to assert.
changes_bullets: THE PURE RESOLUTION, in crates/wz-session-core/src/scout_static.rs: `StaticRole{Open,Listen}` with `forces_peer_mode()`, `StaticConfig{role, locators}`, `StaticConfigError::ListenWithConnect`, and `resolve_static_config(listen, connect)`. No-alloc capable like the synth it wraps (the error carries no owned string, unlike the alloc-gated `ScoutingModeError`), generic over `S: AsRef<str>` so AP feeds `&[String]` and the MCU feeds `&[&str]`, and `Debug` is hand-written because `BoundedVec` derives nothing on either backing.

`StaticConfig.locators` is a LIST for the listen arm too, holding exactly one endpoint today. pico places listen at index 0 and appends the connect tail as additional peers, but only under `Z_FEATURE_UNICAST_PEER == 1`; keeping the field a list is what makes gaining a `_z_new_peer` analog an append to the tail rather than a change to this type.

THE WIRING, in crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_open.rs: `open_session_static_config(listen, connect, params, cfg, accept_cfg, ..)` resolves first, forces `whatami` to `Peer` when the role says so, and then either accepts (`accept_endpoint` -> `accept_and_open_session`) or runs the existing first-Established-wins dial loop. `open_session_static` is now that same function called with `listen: None`, not a second copy of the loop, so the two cannot disagree about what a static config means.

`OpenError::BadStaticConfig(StaticConfigError)` -- a new `scouting-static`-gated variant, raised BEFORE any socket is touched and kept DISTINCT from `NoReachableLocator`, which means the config was coherent and the peers were not there.

ELEVEN TESTS: eight in `scout_static.rs` (one per resolution arm, plus listen trimming, blank-listen hygiene, the all-blank-connect divergence, and the peer-mode flip on its own) and three in `wz-runtime-tokio/tests/static_scout_open.rs` (a real wz<->wz session whose accepting half comes up from `listen=` alone and is checked for the peer announce; the refusal; the blank-listen fall-through).
`LISTEN_PAIR_BUDGET` (20s) bounds both listen-test pairs, added because the P4 probe measured the un-bounded form HANGING rather than failing.

Layer C1k's two count guards moved in the same commit -- `scout_static` 7 -> 15, `static_scout_open` 6 -> 9 -- and the lane's header comment now names the listen half it covers. The mechanical sweep of all 191 guarded invocations against the new test names found no other collision.
Round 1842.decision_summary:
A `listen=` STATIC DEPLOY HAD NO SEAM AT ALL, AND WZ ALREADY OWNED EVERY PIECE
IT NEEDED. The `scouting-static` atom's registry entry names three residuals
against zenoh-pico; the round's first work was measuring how many still hold,
and unlike R311y805 -- where seven of eight had already been paid off by their
own wiring rounds -- ALL THREE still held. The one closed here is `no listen=
handling`. `wz-session-core::scout_static` synthesised a locator list from
`deploy.connect[]` and knew no other input, so `open_session_static` could only
ever DIAL, while `wz-runtime-tokio` has carried a complete accept path
(`accept_endpoint` -> `accept_and_open_session`) since R311qa. The gap was never
the accept half. It was that the static-mode CONFIG RESOLUTION did not know the
word `listen`.

THE SHAPE OF THE FIX IS PICO'S OWN, INCLUDING WHERE IT REFUSES.
`resolve_static_config(listen, connect)` reproduces all four arms of
`_z_locators_by_config` (vendor/zenoh-pico/src/net/session.c:87-118): connect-only
is `StaticRole::Open` over the connect list; listen-only is `StaticRole::Listen`
over the one endpoint; NEITHER is `Open` over an empty list, because pico returns
`_Z_RES_OK` with an empty svec there and falls through to scouting -- a fact this
transform reports rather than a verdict it renders; and BOTH AT ONCE is
`StaticConfigError::ListenWithConnect`, which is not wz being conservative but
pico's own `_Z_ERR_GENERIC` under `Z_FEATURE_UNICAST_PEER == 0` (session.c:107-108).
wz IS that build shape -- it has no `_z_new_peer` analog -- so refusing is parity,
and refusing loudly is the point: honouring one half and dropping the other is how
a deploy comes up listening on a locator nobody dials.

THE ROLE CARRIES A SECOND EFFECT THAT IS EASY TO SHIP HALF OF. pico's listen arm
does not only place an endpoint; it inserts `mode=peer` OVER whatever the config
said (session.c:96, :110), because pico's default is `Z_WHATAMI_CLIENT`
(session.c:122) and a client does not accept. `StaticRole::forces_peer_mode()` is
a method rather than a second field precisely so the two cannot drift apart, and
the e2e asserts it separately: the acceptor's params are set to `Client` on
purpose, so a wiring that bound the socket and skipped the overwrite still
reaches Established and still fails.

THE DAMAGE PROBE FOUND SOMETHING THE TESTS DID NOT CLAIM. Disabling the
blank-listen hygiene turned `static_blank_listen_still_dials_the_connect_list`
from a failure into a run that NEVER RETURNED: both listen tests pair an inline
acceptor with an initiator inside one `join!`, and an initiator that errors out
without connecting leaves the acceptor parked in `accept()` with nothing left to
wake it. A hang is a worse diagnostic than a failure at every layer that reads
it, so both pairs now bound their own wait, and the probe that found it now
fails in 20.00s -- the budget's own number -- instead of hanging.
verification_bullets: THE THREE RESIDUALS WERE RE-MEASURED BEFORE ANYTHING WAS WRITTEN, against the code and against `vendor/zenoh-pico/src/net/session.c` directly rather than against the registry note. All three still hold, which is what makes this a different shape from R311y805, where the same first step found seven of eight already paid. The measurement also dated the note: it cites `session_open.rs:3675-3711` for the first-Established-wins loop, which lives at :4435 today -- debt-47's signal for the fourth time, path and symbol right, line wrong.

LAYER C1k PASSES AT 15 AND 9 (73s), up from 7 and 6. The guards are EXACT counts, so the lane would have redded on the new tests alone; the mechanical sweep of all 191 `_runci_guarded_test` invocations in run-ci.sh against the new test names found these two and no others, run BEFORE the push rather than after a hosted red.

FIVE DAMAGE PROBES, EACH FAILING EXACTLY ONE TEST PER TARGET AND NAMING IT. Disabling the Listen arm in `open_session_static_config` takes only `static_listen_accepts_a_dialing_peer_and_announces_peer_mode` (2.25s) and leaves all 15 unit tests green, which is the wiring proof. Forcing `forces_peer_mode()` to false takes `listen_forces_peer_mode_and_open_does_not` and that same e2e -- WHILE THE SESSION STILL ESTABLISHES, so the whatami claim is not riding on the Established assertion. Dropping the refusal takes `resolve_listen_with_connect_is_refused_not_silently_halved` and `static_listen_with_connect_is_refused_before_any_socket`. Removing the blank-listen filter takes `resolve_treats_a_blank_listen_as_absent` and `static_blank_listen_still_dials_the_connect_list`. The baseline was re-run after every restore and returned 15/9 both times.

A SIXTH PROBE WAS DISCARDED RATHER THAN REPORTED. Nulling the resolved `listen` did not fail tests, it failed to COMPILE (`error: unused import: StaticRole`), and a compile failure fails every test at once, which proves nothing about which test catches what. It was replaced by the wiring probe above, which compiles.

THE BASELINE E2E FINISHES IN 0.00s AND THAT IS NOT EVIDENCE OF ANYTHING, in either direction. The probes are what settle it: the same file takes 2.25s under P1 and 20.00s under P4, so the fast green is a fast green and not an empty one.

CLIPPY WAS RUN THIS TIME, which is the gap R311y806's carry named and did not close: `-p wz-session-core` and `-p wz-runtime-tokio`, `--all-targets` under both `--features scouting-static` and the C1bf `--all-features` arm, all with `-D warnings`. All four rc=0. R311y804 ran `cargo check` and shipped a clippy-only red to four hosted jobs; `cargo check` does not look at lints.

`cargo fmt --all --check` clean, and it found two real hits first -- an import group my insertion split, and a comment block that rustfmt re-anchored as a trailing comment of the line above. Layer C1bz over both changed crates passes with its budgets UNMOVED (wz-session-core 273, wz-runtime-tokio 189), which is the expected reading: every new item is `scouting-static`-gated and so absent from the default-feature rustdoc the budget measures.

carry_forward_bullets: `scouting-static` IS DOWN TO ONE RESIDUAL, and it is the multi-peer one: wz returns after the FIRST locator that reaches Established, where pico in peer mode opens locator[0] and then adds every remaining configured locator to the SAME unicast transport's peer list via `_z_new_peer` (`vendor/zenoh-pico/src/transport/manager.c:177-207` — open socket, `_z_unicast_open_peer` over the existing link, `_z_transport_peer_unicast_add`). Measured this round rather than assumed: it is a MULTI-PEER TRANSPORT, not N sessions, which is a different shape from both `accept_loop`'s N held faces and `transport-multilink`'s N links into one peer. It is also what `StaticConfigError::ListenWithConnect` waits on — gaining the analog turns that refusal into pico's `Z_FEATURE_UNICAST_PEER == 1` arm.

DEBT-47 NOW HAS TWO MEASURED SHAPES IN ONE REGISTRY ENTRY, one round apart: R311y807 found a clause citing a line number that had moved, and this round found a clause whose mechanism claim was simply wrong. The second is the one no path-and-symbol checker reaches, because a clause that says "wz has no X" names nothing to resolve. Nothing measures that class, and nothing proposed here does either.

THE SWEEP THAT CLEARED THE COUNT GUARDS IS OVER-INCLUSIVE BY CONSTRUCTION and that is the right direction, but it should be said out loud: it splits quoted labels into tokens, so `"C1m default"` matched a test named `..._default_retries`. Four candidates, four false positives, each dismissed by reading the invocation. A sweep that under-reported would have shipped a red.

`exit_on_failure` REMAINS UNWIRED BY DECISION, not by omission — it is a process-lifecycle choice for the host that owns the loop, and upstream's own single-link connect arm does not read it either. If a wz host ever wants it, the decision belongs to that host's round, not to this seam.
changes_bullets: `StaticConnectRetry{policy, timeout_ms}` in crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_open.rs — zenoh's `connect.retry` block plus its `connect.timeout_ms`, with `retries()` naming upstream's two-zero disjunction once. The schedule is NOT re-implemented: `policy` is the crate's existing `RetryPolicy`, so a fix to the growth arithmetic cannot land on the reconnect supervisor and the router auto-reconnect and miss this arm.

`StaticDeploy{listen, connect, retry}` carries the `connect: {}` block as one value, with `connect()` / `with_listen()` / `with_retry()`. This REPLACES two of `open_session_static_config`'s parameters rather than adding a third, which drops it from 8 arguments to 7 and retires the `#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]` R311y807 had to add. The next knob from that config block now lands in the struct instead of the signature.

The dial arm gained the retry loop: a fresh `RetryPeriod` per locator (matching `peer_connector_retry` building its period on entry), a `sleep(next_ms())` between attempts, and the walk pinned to the current locator while it retries — upstream's behaviour, stated in the doc comment as upstream's rather than left to look like an oversight.

The whole walk is wrapped in `tokio::time::timeout` when `timeout_ms` is a positive value, and NOT wrapped when it is zero or absent — upstream skips the wrap on zero too, which is why a zero is never turned into an instantly-elapsed bound here.

SIX TESTS in wz-runtime-tokio/tests/static_scout_open.rs: one per zero-rule, one for the zenoh peer default, a peer that does not exist when the dial starts and binds 150ms later, the SAME fixture with the retry omitted (which must fail), and the connect-timeout bound.
The bound test carries its own `tokio::time::timeout` — written before a probe demanded it, because R311y807 measured this exact hazard one round earlier.

Layer C1k's `static_scout_open` guard moved 9 -> 15 and the lane comment names the retry half. A mechanical sweep of all 191 `_runci_guarded_test` invocations against the six new names raised four candidates, all four false positives: `default` and `timeout` occur only inside quoted LABELS (`"C1m default"`, `"C1n reassembly timeout"`) whose commands target other crates and other `--test` files.
Round 1843.decision_summary:
THE CLAUSE SAID WZ HAD NO RETRY. WZ HAD THE WHOLE SCHEDULE AND TWO CONSUMERS.
`scouting-static`'s third residual read "no retry/backoff/exit_on_failure",
citing zenoh's `period_init_ms` / `period_max_ms` / `period_increase_factor`.
Reading the tree instead of the note found
`crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/retry_period.rs` — a transcription of
`ConnectionRetryConf` / `ConnectionRetryPeriod`
(`commons/zenoh-config/src/connection_retry.rs:31-107`) carrying exactly those
three fields and the return-then-multiply order of `next_duration`, already
shared by the client reconnect supervisor and the router peer auto-reconnect,
with `WzConfig::connect_retry` holding a policy since R311y786. What was
missing was not a mechanism but a THIRD consumer: the static-open dial never
read one.

THAT IS A DIFFERENT DEFECT FROM A STALE CLAUSE, and it is the one debt-47's
second shape names. A stale clause points at code that has moved; this clause
pointed at a capability that exists and called it absent. No path-and-symbol
checker would have caught it, because the clause names no symbol at all — it
is a negative claim about the whole tree, and only reading the tree refutes it.
R311y807 met the first shape twice in the same registry entry (a line number
that had moved); this is the second, in the entry's next sentence.

THE FIX IS A WIRING, NOT A SECOND SCHEDULE. `StaticDeploy{listen, connect,
retry}` now carries zenoh's `connect: {}` block as one value, and
`open_session_static_config` selects between the two arms
`connect_peers_single_link` has (`zenoh/src/net/runtime/orchestrator.rs:345-370`):
no retry is one attempt per locator then fall through — what wz had, and
upstream's own arm — while a retry re-attempts the CURRENT locator on its
growing schedule and does not advance past it. That pin is upstream's, not a
shortcut: `peer_connector_retry` loops until its endpoint connects and then

counter to export; that is a residual, not a rename.

AN ACCEPTOR-ROLE RE-HANDSHAKE REUSES ITS NONCE, AND NOTHING TODAY REACHES IT. Round 1849.decision_summary:
THE ACCEPTOR'S COOKIE PROVED SOMEONE HAD ONCE SEEN AN InitAck, NOT THAT THIS
INITIATOR HAD. `session-unicast-accept` has carried the clause since it was
written and it was still literally true: `generate_cookie_hmac_sha256` took
`(key, peer_zid)` and nothing else, `send_init_ack_with_cookie` minted from
that pair, and `cookie_valid` re-derived the same pair at OpenSyn. The
function's own test asserted the determinism as a property. So the 16 bytes an
acceptor demanded back were a pure function of the deploy key and the claimed
zid — constant for the life of the process. An observer who captured ONE
OpenSyn echo could send InitSyn(zid=X) then OpenSyn(that cookie) and reach
`Established`, forever, having proved nothing about reachability. That is the
whole property the anti-amplification cookie exists to establish.

zenoh's answer is a per-handshake random nonce: `prng.gen()` into the cookie,
the value kept in the acceptor's own link state, and an OpenSyn whose echoed
nonce differs rejected as "Unknown cookie"
(`unicast/establishment/accept.rs:362` and `:500-503`). wz now holds the same
invariant in the shape wz's cookie already had. zenoh ENCRYPTS a structured
cookie so its acceptor can be stateless and read the nonce back out; wz's
cookie is 16 opaque MAC bytes and the acceptor is not stateless (that is this
atom's own separate, untouched residual), so the nonce is folded into the MAC
input and remembered in a slot rather than carried on the wire. The wire is
byte-unchanged and the initiator is unaffected: it echoes an opaque field.

THE ORDER OF THE MAC INPUT IS A CORRECTNESS TERM, NOT A STYLE. `peer_zid` is
1..=16 bytes on the wire, so `zid || nonce` is an ambiguous encoding — a
2-byte zid whose nonce begins `03` and a 3-byte zid ending in `03` concatenate
to the same bytes, and two distinct handshakes would share a cookie. The
fixed-width nonce goes FIRST so the split cannot realign, with no length field
to keep in sync. That has its own test.

FAIL-CLOSED WAS CHOSEN OVER A FALLBACK, AND THE FALLBACK IS THE INTERESTING
REJECTED ALTERNATIVE. The no_std core draws no entropy (`getrandom` has no
bare-metal backend), so the nonce arrives from outside and the slot's default
is `None`. `None` could have meant "mint the old un-bound cookie" — every
existing accept path would have kept working untouched. It means "mint no HMAC
cookie and admit no OpenSyn" instead, because a fallback is indistinguishable
from the defect: an operator watching sessions establish could not tell whether
the binding was in force. A build with no entropy now fails loudly rather than
quietly serving the replayable derivation.

THE DRAW SITS AT THE CONSTRUCTION SEAM, NOT AT EACH ACCEPT SEAM, AND THAT IS A
CORRECTION OF THE SIBLING'S SHAPE. The usrpwd/pubkey challenge nonce is
installed by `accept_and_open_session_with_auth` and by
`_with_multilink` — each seam drawing its own, each doc re-arguing that "the
SEAM, not the caller, draws it, so freshness is enforced by construction". That
argument has to be made again at every new seam, and the accept family has six
plus the router and capi paths. The cookie nonce is drawn once in
`new_session_actions`, the single AP constructor every one of them funnels
through, so a future accept path is bound by default. An initiator-role bundle
pays 8 unread bytes of entropy for it.

Two SIBLING clauses in the same entry were read the same way and are already retracted in the text (the Patch ext, R311y605); the three not acted on here are named in the carry.

PROBE D PROVES THE MCU LANE IS A WITNESS AND NOT A VEHICLE. Removing the fixture's `refresh_cookie_nonce` makes Layer C1n's `acceptor_handshake_reaches_established_and_dispatches_frame_over_lwip` FAIL: that e2e's crafted peer echoes the cookie the acceptor really minted over a real lwIP loopback, so it genuinely runs the guard on the coop/no_std profile rather than merely compiling it.

carry_forward_bullets: THE ATOM IS STILL PARTIAL AND THAT IS DELIBERATE. Its last NAMED residual is closed, but COMPLETE would need the whole-surface adversarial re-audit `scouting-active` has never had -- the same reason `attachment-bytes` and `liveliness-subscriber` stayed PARTIAL after their clauses closed. Two residuals are named in the registry as replacements: `ScoutOutcome` cannot distinguish "the survey closed with N peers" from "found one and stopped" (it reports `Discovered` whenever any locator was captured, which is true and uninformative for a survey caller), and wz drops a non-Hello scouting datagram silently at the MID filter where pico logs `_Z_ERR_MESSAGE_UNEXPECTED` -- observability only, since both keep looping.

THE FOREIGN WITNESS FOR THE SURVEY ARM NEEDS TWO RESPONDERS AND THAT IS NOW MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED. The one-router leg stays GREEN under the exit_on_first damage probe, because a single answer is reported identically by a survey and by a first-answer lookup. A pico-side responder cannot substitute: stock zenoh-pico has no scouting RESPONDER, only a scouter.

A future guard on `scout.tx.done` or `scout.timer.elapsed` would need its own EventSchema and its own inject, not a second field on this one -- the schema is named for its event.

AN ACCEPTED DIVERGENCE, STATED: wz emits ONE Scout per window where pico also emits one, but neither retransmits, so a Scout lost on the wire costs the whole window. pico has the same hole (`_z_link_send_wbuf` once, then the read loop) and this round did not widen it -- but the cycle loop it deleted was accidentally covering it, since a lost Scout was re-sent on the next cycle. A survey now fails silently where it used to retry. That is upstream's behaviour and it is the trade this round accepted.

THE `run-ci.sh` HEADER SAYS `_runci_guarded_test` "has 15 call sites in this file" AND THE SWEEP COUNTED 200. Not touched here (it sits in a shellcheck-directive paragraph whose neighbouring count already carries a "this is a MOVING count, recompute it" warning), but it is a measured stale number in a file this round edited, and it is the debt-47 shape in a script rather than in the registry.
changes_bullets: New `sources/session/hello_received_schema.scxml` (EventSchema, `uint8 exit_on_first`) and two guarded `hello.received` transitions in `sources/session/scouting.scxml`: `!== 0` -> Idle, `=== 0` -> AwaitingHello. `xtask regen` refreshed `out/wz-session-core/scouting_sm.rs` (typed `ScoutingPayload` + `ScoutingInject::raise_hello_received`); the three sibling statecharts move one line because the emit stamps a SOURCE-SET hash, not a per-file one.

`ScoutParams::exit_on_first` is a REQUIRED field, not a defaulted one, so the compiler enumerated all five construction sites and none could inherit a mode it did not choose. A survey that silently stops at the first answer and a lookup that silently waits out the window are both wrong and neither is visible from the outcome.

The inbound Hello decode moved out of `record_hello_and_emit` into the drive loop as `decode_scouted_hello`, pico's own position (`_z_scouting_message_decode` then `continue`). `pending_hello` now stages a decoded `ScoutedHello` rather than raw bytes, so the action is the HELLO arm and nothing else.

`discovered_locator` is FIRST-WINS. Under exit-on-first there is one Hello per cycle so first and last agree; under the survey arm a plain assignment let the LAST peer to answer re-point a dial target the caller may already have acted on.

`wz-capi-pico`'s copy of the scouting drive DELETED -- it delegates to `wz_capi_core::scouting::run_scout` and keeps only the `ScoutedHello` -> `HelloState` ABI mapping. Both ABIs now run ONE window over the caller's budget with `exit_on_first: false`, and the cycle loop, the per-cycle re-Scout and the zid dedup set are gone with it.

`wz-capi-core::scouting::deliver_in_upstream_order` hands the closure the LAST responder first, after the window -- the one seam where upstream's delivery contract is imitated, with the citation attached.

Round 1850.decision_summary:
THE SCOUT COULD ONLY EVER FIND ONE PEER, AND A CONSUMER WAS ALREADY PAYING FOR
IT. `scouting-active` carried one residual and it was still literally true:
`sources/session/scouting.scxml:128` targeted `Idle` on `hello.received`, and
the generated FSM assigned `ScoutingState::Idle` unconditionally, so the drive
loop -- which ends a cycle when the FSM reaches `Idle` -- returned after the
FIRST Hello. zenoh-pico's `__z_scout_loop` takes `exit_on_first` as a
PARAMETER and ships both values: the session-open implicit scout passes `true`
(`src/net/session.c:69`, it needs one dial target), the public `z_scout` survey
passes `false` (`src/net/primitives.c:81`, it reports every responder).

THE MISSING ARM WAS NOT DORMANT -- IT HAD A WORKAROUND WITH ITS OWN COST.
`wz-capi-core` and `wz-capi-pico` both re-entered whole scouting CYCLES to
reach a second peer, and said so in their own doc comments. That re-emitted a
Scout onto the group per cycle, provoked duplicate answers from every live
responder, and then needed a zid set to suppress the duplicates it had caused;
`wz-capi-pico` carried a SECOND COPY of that loop plus a "One divergence,
named" section admitting the callback could lag the wire by a cycle. A residual
that is only a note in a registry is cheap to defer; this one was running.

THE MODE RIDES THE EVENT BECAUSE THE ENGINE-FREE SURFACE HAS NO OTHER CHANNEL.
The statechart is `sce:kind="statechart"` with no script engine and no
datamodel, so a native guard can read exactly one thing: a typed
`_event.data.<field>`. A new EventSchema (`hello_received_schema.scxml`,
`uint8 exit_on_first`) gives it that field, the same NL->IR Path A lowering
`reassembly_slot.scxml`'s `more` bit already uses. The exit arm targets `Idle`;
the survey arm RE-ENTERS `AwaitingHello` and only `scout.timer.elapsed` closes
the window. That is pico's `if (!empty && exit_on_first) break;` split into the
statechart rather than into the host.

TWO FURTHER DEFECTS CAME OUT OF READING UPSTREAM, NOT OUT OF THE CLAUSE.
(1) The inbound Hello DECODE lived inside the transition action, and an action
runs AFTER its guard has already chosen the target state. So under
exit-on-first a datagram carrying the Hello MID that did not decode still ended
the window -- one malformed packet from anywhere on the untrusted multicast
group, and the scout returned having discovered nothing. pico decodes BEFORE
its MID switch and `continue`s on failure (`scout.c:71-76`), so the decode
moved to the drive loop, where pico keeps it. (2) The claim this tree had
written down -- hellos "in arrival order, as zenoh-pico's `_z_hello_slist_t`
carries them" -- is FALSE. `_z_hello_slist_push_empty` PREPENDS
(`collections/list.c:287-295`) and `_z_scout` drains from the head AFTER
`_z_scout_inner` returns (`net/primitives.c:81-90`), so a pico closure is
called after the window and sees the LAST responder first.

THAT SECOND FINDING REVERSED A DESIGN DECISION MID-ROUND. The first shape gave
the drive loop a per-Hello observer and called the capi callback at the instant
each peer was recorded -- which read as an improvement over the "lags by a
cycle" divergence being retired. Reading `_z_scout` showed the divergence's
PREMISE was wrong: upstream does not call the closure from inside its loop at
all. Per-Hello, arrival-order delivery would have been a divergence in wz's
favour, which is still a divergence. The observer was removed, the two capi
copies collapsed onto one drive in `wz-capi-core`, and the reversal now lives
at that single seam with a test.

THE RULE IS PER-ID, NOT PER-SOLICITATION, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE OF IT. A HISTORY
subscriber's own CURRENT replay is interest_id-tagged exactly as a GET's answer
is, and it must arrive. "Drop every solicited declare" would pass the headline
test and break the subscriber; it has its own test and its own damage probe, and
that probe fails only that one.

unfiltered fan RECORDED the answer as an announcement — while `liveliness` is

now, and each has its own witness because a fix applied to one registry is
invisible to the other's tests.

`make_token_id`, `hat/client/token.rs:305-317` — the R311y791 finding), so

The derivation has NO DISCRIMINATING FOREIGN WITNESS and cannot get one from a conforming peer: `initial_sn` is announced, never recomputed, so a real zenohd accepts a constant 0 as readily as a derived origin. A witness would have to be a wz-side dissector predicate over a FOREIGN session — check a real zenoh peer's announced origin against `Shake128(zid_mine || zid_other)` — which is the analyzer's oracle surface, not this atom's.

`params.initial_sn` is now a PRE-NEGOTIATION placeholder for the unicast Open path, and every production builder still writes the literal 0 into it. That is harmless (the encode seam substitutes) but it means the field's name over-promises at four call sites; a later round could either seed it from the derivation or say so at each site.

The re-seed REWINDS the TX conduits, which is correct only because an Open frame is emitted once per session incarnation ahead of every data frame. It is private to the encode seam for that reason. Nothing TESTS the rewind hazard, because nothing in the FSM can reach it.
Multicast is untouched: it has no Open body and no peer zid, so its JOIN-announced SNs still ride `params.initial_sn`.
changes_bullets: NEW `crates/wz-session-core/src/initial_sn.rs` — `derive_initial_sn(own_zid, peer_zid, sn_mask)`, a transcription of zenoh's `compute_sn` (`io/zenoh-transport/src/unicast/establishment/mod.rs:104-118`): absorb the own zid then the peer zid as WIRE bytes into `Shake128`, squeeze, read little-endian, mask by the negotiated FrameSN ring. The zid slices are exactly what zenoh hashes, because `hasher.update(&zid.to_le_bytes()[..zid.size()])` absorbs the same bytes its codec writes (`zenoh-codec/src/core/zenohid.rs:37`) and wz's `SessionInitParams::zid` holds that wire form.

`SessionLinkActions::open_params` (new, private) + `encode_open_with_role` — the Open body's `initial_sn` is now the derived value, and the same call re-seeds `outbound_frame_sn`. Resolved OUTSIDE the ext-chain closure for the R311di-pre-f5 reason `encode_init_with_role` records: it takes `remote_peer_zid` and, through `negotiated_sn_mask`, `inbound_peer_init_caps`, and a nested `R::with_mutex_mut` deadlocks the non-reentrant lwIP `critical_section`. `None` when no peer zid has landed, so a pre-handshake encode still carries the constructed value.

`crates/wz-session-core/Cargo.toml` — `codec-open-body` now pulls `dep:sha3`, rather than a feature of its own: the derivation is the Open body's own field, so a build that can emit an Open frame can always derive its origin, and one that cannot links no Keccak. The `sha3` dependency comment's "usrpwd ONLY / AP-only" clause is retired — it has two consumers now and the second reaches the MCU acceptor.

EIGHT bytes are squeezed where zenoh reads four (its `TransportSn` is a `u32`, wz's SN ring is a real `u64`). A strict extension: an XOF is a byte stream and little-endian puts the first bytes low, so for every resolution zenoh can express the masked value is bit-identical.

carry_forward_bullets: THE PARTITION IS BUILT BUT NOT DRIVEN BY wz ITSELF, and that is the exact residue this round leaves. Every existing wz spawn still goes through TokioRuntime onto the ambient runtime, so in a real node WZ_RUNTIME is inert: an operator can set it and nothing moves. The isolation is proven by test, not by a session. Closing this is a per-seam migration -- accept_loop to acc, stream_link::writer_task to tx, the read drive loop to rx, scouting/gossip to net -- and it is NOT mechanical: moving a task to another runtime takes it out of the consumer's runtime, and tokio's paused clock is PER-RUNTIME, so any test standing on tokio::time::pause auto-advance across that seam changes meaning. Each seam wants its own measurement.

The max_blocking_threads dial is tunable and currently unreachable: nothing spawns a blocking task through the pool (wz's one spawn_blocking caller, wz-replay/src/live.rs, uses the ambient runtime), so that half of "independently tunable worker_threads and max_blocking_threads" is configured but not exercised. It is honest to call it wired, not driven.

wz's only PRODUCTION sync-over-async bridge is session_glue::TokioLinkDriverAdapter, and it does not route through WzRuntime::block_in_place. Its constructor has asserted MultiThread since it was written, which is why the residual's "no guard against a consumer running wz on a current-thread scheduler" was already half false when re-measured -- the guard existed, at one construction site, for one adapter. The new guard is on the pool's bridge. Whether the adapter should become a caller of it is a question about that adapter, which the production path already avoids in favour of the non-blocking channel split.

The atom's SECOND residual is untouched and unmeasured this round: zenoh's handover is configured through the same RON string that configures the counts, and wz's equivalent is reached only through WZ_RUNTIME or a caller-built RuntimePool. No wz config file, CLI flag or demo arg reaches either.

The §5.13-runtime section body is STALE in the reverse direction (the registry is right and the prose is old): it still reads "6 atomic features all reserved (wz-runtime-tokio is unicast client-only)" and cites an R311ci audit finding 0 source cfg sites. changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/runtime_pool.rs (new): WzRuntime names the five subsystems under upstream's own spellings (app/acc/tx/rx/net) and upstream's own default worker counts (rx 2, the rest 1, 50 blocking threads throughout); RuntimePool builds each runtime lazily and names its threads wz-<name>-<n>; PartitionedRuntime implements wz_runtime_core::Runtime bound to one subsystem, so it is a drop-in for TokioRuntime at a call site that wants isolation. Nothing is rewired implicitly -- TokioRuntime still spawns onto the ambient runtime, which is what every existing consumer and every #[tokio::test] expects.

RuntimeParams::parse is the WZ_RUNTIME accept/reject set, a pure function on a string rather than a read of the process environment, so the set is testable without a global. wz spells the config as `name:key=value,...` groups separated by `;` instead of taking a RON dependency for one string. WzRuntime::block_in_place mirrors zenoh's guards at zenoh-runtime/src/lib.rs:142-162: a caller on tokio's current-thread scheduler is named instead of deadlocked, and so is one running after tokio's thread-locals are destroyed. RuntimePool::Drop shuts each runtime down on a plain thread, so a caller-owned pool can be dropped from an async context.

Round 1861.decision_summary:
The runtime-tokio atom's first residual is closed at the primitive: wz had one
ambient tokio runtime for everything, so a receive path that saturated its
workers also starved the transmit path and an operator had no dial to separate
them. wz now carries the same five isolated runtimes zenoh does -- app, acc,
tx, rx, net -- each independently tunable, plus the sync-over-async bridge's
fail-fast guards. The clause was picked by sorting all 85 PARTIAL atoms by the
age of their own reason: runtime-tokio is one of only two that cite no round at
all, so it had never been re-measured.
verification_bullets: MEASURED BEFORE FIXED, and the measurement is the clause itself made executable rather than a read of it: saturated_rx_starves_tx_on_one_shared_runtime saturates both workers of one runtime from the RX side and shows the TX side does not run inside a 750ms window. It was written and run BEFORE any implementation existed and was GREEN, which is what established the clause was still true after never having been re-measured. It stays green now, and that is deliberate -- it is the discriminator against a "partition" that quietly hands every subsystem the same runtime.

The first two drafts of that measurement were wrong in ways worth recording. Draft one signalled with tokio's blocking_send, which panics inside an async block. Draft two observed through a oneshot under a timeout, where "the value arrived" and "the sender was dropped" are the SAME Ok verdict; it reported the opposite of the truth. The third form -- an AtomicBool observed from the block_on thread with a plain sleep, no tokio timer in the loop -- is unambiguous, and a diagnostic print then showed the TX task running only AFTER the 2s saturation ended.

Four damage probes, each redding only its own claim, run with --no-fail-fast. A (RuntimePool::resolve collapsed to Application) -> the five routing tests red, with the shared-runtime measurement and every config test STILL GREEN. B (block_in_place's flavor guard inverted) -> exactly the two block_in_place tests. C (the handover-chain check inverted) -> exactly handover_chain_is_refused. carry_forward_bullets: DETECTION IS BEHIND THE RECOVERY GATE AND UPSTREAM'S IS NOT, which is a NEW divergence this round introduces while closing a larger one, and it is stated rather than left to be discovered. `AdvancedSubscriberOptions` and `declare_with_options` live behind ext-pubsub-advanced-recovery, so a subscriber that wants to be detectable must also pull the reorder buffer and the recovery query plane; zenoh keeps `.subscriber_detection()` independent of `.recovery()`. This is the SAME SHAPE the R311y91 review called M1 for history-without-retransmission. Lifting the options type to the -subscriber level needs a second `declare_with_options` arm whose bounds match the recovery-OFF `declare` -- the signature-stability invariant this module states explicitly and keeps two `declare` arms for -- so it is its own round. Two cfgs in advanced_ke.rs are pinned to the recovery gate for this reason alone and must move with it.

NOTHING CONSUMES THE TOKEN, and that is upstream's state too rather than a wz gap: `KE_SUB` is read at exactly one place in zenoh (the declaration) and `_Z_KEYEXPR_SUB` at exactly one in pico (the declaration). Both `pub use` / export it for third parties. wz declaring it therefore makes wz observable BY an external tool; it does not make wz able to observe anyone. A wz-side consumer -- a subscriber-detection liveliness subscriber, the mirror of the `@adv/pub/**` one the recovery plane already has -- is a separate capability and neither reference has it.

The eid in the token KE is minted from wz's entity counter at declare time, not read off the Subscriber handle, because wz keeps no eid there. zenoh uses `subscriber.id().eid()`, so the two agree on the KE SHAPE but a wz subscriber's token eid does not correspond to any other id the same subscriber shows elsewhere. Nothing observable depends on that today; it would matter to a consumer correlating the token with a subscriber seen another way.

The ext-pubsub-advanced-subscriber atom's subscriber-detection residual is

The control is what makes the subject assertion mean anything -- without it "zero @adv/sub frames" could equally be an observation window that catches nothing, which is the R311y807 population-is-zero class in its wire-assertion shape. It ran green before any implementation, and is KEPT after the fix, retargeted at the option-free `declare()` form that still declares no token.

TWO OF THE ROUND'S OWN TESTS WERE FALSE WITNESSES AND A DAMAGE PROBE FOUND BOTH. The teardown test first asserted "more frames after drop"; probe B, which removed the token entirely, still PASSED it, because the subscriber's own undeclare already emits a frame. It now asserts a DIFFERENCE -- a detectable subscriber's teardown carries exactly one frame more than a plain one's -- and probe B reds it. The metadata test first asserted the absence of the byte string `/room/kitchen/_`; probe C, which appended the metadata AFTER the empty chunk rather than substituting for it, produced `/_/room/kitchen` and killed NOTHING. It now reads the chunk that follows `<eid>/` positionally, and probe C reds it. A probe that judges nothing is a measurement of a missing witness (the R311y816 rule) and both were paid off in this round rather than recorded as debt.

Four damage probes, each redding only its own claim after those repairs, run with --no-fail-fast. A (the no-metadata tail spelled as a different VALID chunk, not as an empty one -- the first attempt used an empty chunk, which made the whole key expression invalid and killed two tests for the wrong reason) -> only subscriber_detection_declares_the_adv_sub_token. B (the opt-in ignored) -> the four tests that need a token, with detection_is_off_by_default still GREEN as the discriminator. C (metadata appended rather than substituted) -> only the metadata test. D (the zid bound widened past any real zid) -> only the zid refusal test.

carry_forward_bullets: A WZ-NATIVE DIVERGENCE IS INTRODUCED, NAMED HERE RATHER THAN LEFT TO BE FOUND: the volumes/<id> body is {"capability":{history,persistence}} where upstream returns the volume's CONFIG object (VolumeConfig::to_json_value). A wz volume is a registered Rust object with no config to echo -- the storage_volume module note has said so since the seam was built -- so the faithful shape would have been an empty object, which a client reads as "introspected, and empty". The capability is what a wz volume actually declares, and it is under an explicitly wz-named key rather than pretending to be upstream's. An admin client written against zenoh will parse this body and find none of the keys it expected.

THE ATOM IS STILL PARTIAL, and its remaining residuals are untouched and unmeasured this round: `report` is a hardcoded Info level where upstream's PluginReport carries per-plugin severity and messages, and with no PluginsManager the Declared state stays structurally unreachable, so a zenoh admin client cannot distinguish declared-but-failed-to-load on a wz node. Neither was attempted.

A DLOPEN'D PLUGIN PUBLISHES NO SUB-TREE, and that is a real hole rather than a design choice this round gets to make: wz DOES load plugins (plugin.rs, with real .so paths on the admin plane), and upstream's adminspace_getter is a trait method every plugin answers. Giving a wz dynamic plugin the same ability is an ABI change to wz-plugin-abi, which belongs to the §5.22 plugin family, not here. Stated so the next reader does not mistake "storage_manager publishes leaves" for "wz plugins publish leaves".

THE HOST-SIDE FRESHNESS CONTRACT IS BY CONVENTION, not by construction. The snapshot is correct because it is refreshed in the same statement group as the Started bit; nothing prevents a future host from refreshing one and not the other. The type that would make that unrepresentable -- a manager handle the handler can read directly -- is blocked by RuntimeStorageManager not being Send, which is itself load-bearing (the Volume trait carries no Send bound). Named rather than papered over.

ONLY ONE HOST FEEDS LEAVES. The library Session host and the routing-peer / router-hat demo hosts hold no storage manager and pass the static registry, so on those nodes the sub-tree is empty -- correctly, but it means the served path has exactly one production driver today.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-session-core/src/adminspace.rs: AdminPluginStatusLeaf (a suffix below the plugin's status root plus an already-rendered JSON body) and AdminPlugin::status_leaves, with a with_status_leaves builder. carry_forward_bullets: THE ATOM IS STILL PARTIAL, and its one remaining divergence is untouched and unmeasured this round: wz REBUILDS the digest from the storage snapshot every cycle where zenoh swaps a latest_updates staging map into an incremental replication log (core.rs:212-215). That is a cost and allocation question rather than a wire-visible one, and nothing was attempted on it here.

A DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE IS INTRODUCED, NAMED HERE RATHER THAN LEFT TO BE FOUND: the jitter is seeded from the replica's zid, so a wz replica's publication offsets are DETERMINISTIC and an observer who knows the zid can predict them. Upstream's thread_rng draws cannot be. The argument for it is in JitterSequence's own doc -- the property upstream states it needs is that distinct replicas differ, not that an adversary cannot follow along -- but if a later round finds a reason the unpredictability matters, that is a real change of requirement and not a bug in this code.

A RESTARTED REPLICA REPEATS ITS OWN JITTER SEQUENCE, since the seed is the zid alone with no restart-varying term. Harmless for the anti-storm property, which is across replicas, and it is what makes the schedule reproducible under test -- but it means two processes that somehow share a zid would publish in lockstep, where upstream's draws would separate them.

THE ALIGNMENT CLOCK IS READ EXACTLY ONCE, before the cycle begins, so a wall-clock STEP after start-up does not re-align the replica; the period is then held by the compensated closing delay off the monotonic clock. That is upstream's behaviour too, and it is the reason the two clocks are deliberately different here, but it is a property nothing currently tests.

THE PROPAGATION DELAY IS NOW LOAD-BEARING ON LATENCY, which it was not before: a config whose propagation delay EXCEEDS its interval (the in-tree test configs are exactly this shape, 250ms against 20ms and 100ms) now overruns every cycle, so post_publication_delay_ms returns None and the effective period becomes the delay rather than the interval. That is upstream's behaviour, and upstream logs a warning recommending a longer interval where wz currently logs nothing. A wz operator gets no signal that their configuration is self-defeating.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-session-core/src/storage_replication.rs: the schedule as FOUR pure functions on ReplicationConfig, so the arithmetic is testable with no clock at all. alignment_delay_ms(now_unix_ms) is zenoh's duration_until_next_interval (core.rs:163-190), computed in the shorter equivalent form interval - (now % interval) since last_elapsed_interval is now / interval; it returns a FULL interval on an exact boundary, which is upstream's arithmetic kept rather than smoothed. max_publication_delay_ms is interval/3 (core.rs:196) and publication_delay_ms(draw) maps an arbitrary draw into it, taking the draw as a VALUE rather than a source so the schedule stays pure. post_publication_delay_ms(cycle_work) is interval - work, with None as upstream's overrun signal (core.rs:262-272) rather than an error.

crates/wz-session-core/src/storage_replication.rs: JitterSequence, seeded per replica from its zid via the Xxh3 this module already uses, stepped by SplitMix64. Upstream draws from rand::thread_rng, and the deliberate divergence is argued from the PURPOSE upstream states -- "we do not want to create a coordinated update storm with all replicas publishing at the same time" needs distinct replicas to draw distinct sequences, and the zid is the value a fleet is already guaranteed to differ on. That is reachable in a no_std kernel with no entropy port and no failure path to invent a fallback for. The type's doc says outright that it is NOT unpredictable and must not be borrowed for anything needing that; EntropySource is the port with that contract, and its own note warns against a source that satisfies the type while defeating the purpose.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/storage_replication_service.rs: DigestPublisher::spawn is now upstream's cycle -- align, wait the propagation delay, build the frame, jitter, put, then close with the compensated remainder. The jitter sits between the build and the put, as upstream's does (core.rs:234-243): it de-correlates when the fleet TRANSMITS while the digest still describes the moment the propagation window closed, where jittering earlier would move the observation instead. The cycle is measured with clock.now_monotonic_ms, the same timeline the waits run on, which is what makes the subtraction mean anything. publish_digest_once is DELETED rather than left: placing the jitter correctly meant the cycle calls digest_frame and session.publish separately, which left that helper with no caller at all.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/timestamp_source.rs: wall_clock_unix_ms beside its NTP64 sibling -- the same SystemTime recipe in the unit an interval boundary is defined in. Kept as a sibling rather than derived through Ntp64, which would route an exact millisecond count through a fraction conversion that exists only to match uhlc. A monotonic reading cannot serve here: two replicas' monotonic epochs are their own start times, so aligning against one would de-align the fleet.

verification_bullets: MEASURED BEFORE FIXED, and the measurement was written as a test rather than read off the source. A publication_offsets_ms harness records, in the publisher's own VIRTUAL clock (tokio start_paused), the millisecond offset from spawn of each digest, taking the instant INSIDE the subscriber callback so an offset is never rounded to a polling period and waiting on a Notify rather than a poll timer so the clock jumps straight to the publisher's next wake. Against the pre-fix publisher, with interval 20ms and propagation delay 250ms, it measured exactly [20, 40] -- the configured delay was accepted, fingerprinted, and ignored. The whole run cost 0.03s of wall clock because the time is virtual.

THE FLIPPED CONTROL CARRIES ITS OWN NEGATIVE. the_publisher_waits_the_configured_propagation_delay asserts the delayed config lands in [251, 275] AND that a config differing ONLY in that parameter (delay 0) lands in [1, 25]. Either half alone is weak -- "the first digest is late" is also true of a slow publisher or a dead observation window -- so the two configurations must fall in DISJOINT windows. The bounds are the config's own: alignment is 1..=20 on the real wall clock and jitter is 0..=5.

FOUR DAMAGE PROBES, each killing exactly one test, none of them a compile failure. (1) Zeroing the propagation wait reds the propagation test AND reports 20 -- exactly the pre-fix control value, so the probe restores the measured defect rather than some other one. (2) Adding the elapsed time back onto the closing delay reds only the period test, at a 12651ms span against 10000. (3) Not advancing the JitterSequence state reds only the jitter test. (4) Inverting the alignment formula reds only the alignment test. Probes 3 and 4 ran together: 38 passed, 2 failed, so neither reached anything else.

THE PERIOD TEST IS MEASURED OVER TEN CYCLES, not one, because one interval is 1000 + (jn - jn-1) and at +/-332ms of jitter that overlaps an uncompensated cycle and would decide nothing. Over ten the jitter difference is still one draw wide while the drift has accumulated tenfold, which probe 2 confirms by landing eight jitter-widths outside the window. The probe's 12651 also corrected a claim written into this round's own comment: an uncompensated period is interval + propagation + jitter, not interval + propagation as first written.

Round 1866.decision_summary:
The vendor/sce pin moves 615cb3f6f8 -> 7f94b580f7, 69 upstream commits, and it
is not a routine refresh: the bump carries a W3C SCXML conformance fix that
changes the StatePolicy trait wz's generated statecharts implement.

Upstream split Appendix D's two entry functions apart. execute_entry_actions now
takes a `path_child: Option<Self::State>` -- `None` when the state is the entry
TARGET, so addDescendantStatesToEnter applies and a compound state takes its

carry_forward_bullets: THE `visible == true` ARM HAS NO WITNESS AND PROBE P2 PROVED IT. A put whose rename landed but whose directory fsync failed updates the mirror and still answers Err; inverting that decision fails no test, because nothing portable makes `fsync` fail after a successful `rename`. The arm is REACHED in production (an fsync can fail on a failing device) and is the one place the mirror deliberately moves under an error, so it is the arm most worth a witness and the one hardest to buy. A fault-injecting filesystem (or a `Persist` seam behind a trait so a double can answer for it) is what would close it.

THE ATOM STAYS PARTIAL. This round closed the ONE named impl residual, not the surface. `storage-backend-filesystem` still has its own coverage gap -- Layer C1bg is local-only, absent from ci.yml's layer enumeration -- so none of the three new filesystem tests run on hosted CI, and the same is true of the six kernel tests only through the C1z lane, which ci.yml also omits. COMPLETE needs a whole-surface adversarial re-audit, the same reason every other atom on this track stayed PARTIAL after its residual was paid.

NOTHING ABOVE THE KERNEL SURFACES THE REFUSAL TO AN OPERATOR OR A PEER. `apply_sample` and the aligner log at `log::error!` and continue, which is upstream's behaviour and the right one for a driver loop, but it means the ONLY signal a storage host is silently failing to persist is a log line: no admin metric, no `@/<zid>/.../storage` field, no reply-side indication to the querier who just wrote. Upstream is no better here, so this is a divergence-free gap rather than a parity one -- but it is a gap.

THE WILDCARD ANSWER IS wz's, NOT UPSTREAM's. `materialize_wildcard` sweeps every matching key and returns the first error, answering a question zenoh leaves as a TODO in `storages_mgt/service.rs:362-363`. That means there is no foreign witness for it and never can be until upstream decides; if upstream later chooses abort-on-first, wz diverges. Recorded so the next reader knows the choice was made here.

changes_bullets: crates/wz-session-core/src/storage_backend.rs: the seam gains an error channel. `StorageWriteError` is a UNIT struct and `StorageWriteResult = Result<StorageInsertionResult, StorageWriteError>`; `put` / `delete` return it. Payload-free follows the y819 `EntropyUnavailable` precedent for two reasons stated on the type: the kernel is no_std and the type rides the SUCCESS path of every MCU profile to describe a failure only an AP-side backend can produce, and no caller in this tree branches on the detail -- they all take one branch while the backend that owns the medium logs the concrete io::Error. The module doc's "no ZResult wrapper: the in-memory mutations are infallible" bullet is replaced rather than left to rot; it was the sentence the defect was licensed by.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/filesystem_storage.rs: `persist` now reports WHICH side failed, via a private `Unpersisted { visible, err }`. That split is load-bearing and is not the same as "on error, change nothing": if the rename LANDED and only the directory fsync failed, the mirror MUST move, because the mirror's contract is that it shows what a reopen would show and a reopen would read the new bytes. So `visible == false` returns early and leaves the store untouched; `visible == true` updates the mirror and still answers `Err`. `delete` looks the entry up WITHOUT removing it and only drops it once the unlink has actually happened -- it used to remove first, which made a refused unlink read back as a successful delete. `NotFound` stays a success (upstream's own `if file.exists()` rule, files_mgt.rs:198).

crates/wz-session-core/src/storage_state.rs: `process_put` / `process_delete` propagate with `?` BEFORE writing `latest`, which is the whole fix -- no version record, therefore no tombstone, therefore no replication event for a mutation the backend refused. Round 1867.decision_summary:
A durable store served a value it had failed to write, and told every peer so.

`storage-backend-filesystem` carried a NAMED residual: the `StorageBackend`
put/delete seam is infallible, so `FilesystemStorage` logged an I/O error and
updated its in-memory mirror anyway. The clause read as a bounded, in-process
honesty trade -- "a disk fault is an environmental error surfaced loudly, not a
silent lie in the in-process view". It was not bounded that way.

`StorageState::latest`, the newer-wins record the gate writes AFTER the backend
returns, is what `replication_events` and the aligner digest are derived from.
So a value this Durable store never wrote was recorded as held, advertised in
the digest, and answered into alignment queries -- and a peer that believes you
hold an event stops sending it. The failure is not "one value is lost on
restart"; it is that the mesh is told convergence was reached.

Upstream takes the opposite branch at exactly this point: on `Err` from
`storage.put`, `storages_mgt/service.rs:352-366` logs and SKIPS the
`cache_guard.insert` that feeds its replication log, and its own filesystem
backend propagates the write error with `?` (`zenoh-ref-fs/src/lib.rs:294-353`).
wz had no channel to propagate through.

The same defect had already been copied into a second backend by explicit
reference: `DynamicStore` (`storage-mgr-dynamic-volume-loading`) updates its
mirror on a rejected `store_put` "exactly as the filesystem backend does under
this infallible seam".
verification_bullets: THE DEFECT WAS MEASURED BEFORE IT WAS FIXED, AS A RESULT AND NOT AS A CITATION. Three tests were written against the OLD signature -- the error channel did not exist yet, so only the outcome claims were expressible -- and run first: 3 FAILED, 14 passed. The sharpest line is `left: Some([2]) right: Some([1])`: the store handed back the value whose write had just failed. The 14 pre-existing tests staying green in that same run is what says the fixture broke nothing.

FINAL COUNTS. C1bg filesystem_storage 17 passed / 0 failed (14 -> 17). `storage_state::tests::refused_writes` 6 passed / 0 failed. `dynamic_volume::tests` 11 passed / 0 failed over the real example `.so`. Counts are quoted because exit 0 alone is the shape that hides an empty selection.

SEVEN DAMAGE PROBES, AND SIX OF THEM KILLED ONLY THEIR OWN CLAIM. P1 (mirror updated on an unwritten put) -> the 2 value assertions, while their `is_err` halves stayed green, which is what separates the MIRROR claim from the ERROR claim. P3 (unwritten put answers Ok) -> the same 2 tests by the other half. P4 (a refused unlink reported as Deleted) -> 1. P5 (record `latest` even on Err) -> 2, and NOT the two committed-write controls, which is the measurement that the controls earn their place. P6 (record the tombstone even on Err) -> 1. P7 (DynamicStore updates its mirror on a refusal) -> 1.

PROBE P2 KILLED NOTHING, AND THAT IS THE ROUND'S HONEST RESULT. It inverted the `visible == true` arm -- rename landed, directory fsync failed -- and all 17 stayed green: no portable fixture makes fsync fail while rename succeeds, so that arm has NO witness. Recorded as a residual rather than counted as covered.

THE FAILURE FIXTURES ARE UID-INDEPENDENT ON PURPOSE. A read-only directory would be bypassed by root; instead the store directory is REMOVED (so the temp-file create is ENOENT) and, for the delete arm, the key's data file is replaced by a DIRECTORY of the same name (unlink on a directory fails for every uid). The dynamic-volume witness uses the same removal against the REAL `.so`, so its refusal comes from `write_atomically` genuinely failing rather than from a stub returning ERR.
