fourth. Unit (`payload_cbor`, 11 tests, all green). Plane (`inspect` answers
`Cbor` for one well-formed item and `NotAsDeclared` with the byte offset for
JSON under a cbor label, and `is_consistent` is asserted BOTH ways so a new
verdict arm falling through to false would red). Terminal (`wz-analyze` drives a
capture through `analyze_request` with `--payload-format demo/**=cbor` and a
`--payload-name` rename; the printed listing carries `$ = map 2 pair(s)`,
`$.t (celsius) = unsigned 21`, and `$.\i5 = text "a"`). C ABI
(`wz_dissect_pcap_fields_with_payloads`, the surface a product LINKS: the honest
capture decodes with `despite_encoding: null`, and JSON under a cbor label with
a `json` rule now decodes carrying `despite_encoding: "application/cbor"` --
the answer that was unreachable before this round, where the same capture
returned `encoding_mismatch` and nothing).
TWO DAMAGE PROBES, ON TWO DIFFERENT AXES, both discriminated by the PANIC BODY
and not by the exit code. Replacing `\i` with the bare decimal -- item 434's
naive scheme -- produced `["$", "$.5", "$.5"]` against the expected
`["$", "$.\\i5", "$.5"]`: the collision the item was registered for, reproduced
exactly. Accepting reserved additional information 28 reds both the Appendix F
leg and the two-readers-agree leg.
ONE TEST'S OWN CLAIM WAS WRONG AND THE RUN SAID SO. The `inspect` test asserted
that `{"a":1}` under a cbor label fails at the end of the payload, reasoning
that `{` is 0x7b, a text string of 27 bytes. 0x7b is major type 3 with
additional information 27, which means the LENGTH is the next eight bytes -- so
the walk stops at byte 1 reading an argument the document does not hold. The
assertion and its comment now say the real mechanism. This is item 438's shape
caught in the act: a test's claim about a format is asserted on every run and
audited by nobody.

Round 1968.decision_summary:
THE ANALYZER COULD NOT ENTER TWO THINGS IT WAS ALREADY ABLE TO OPEN, AND THE
SECOND GATE WRITTEN TO PROTECT THAT WORK FOUND A COLLISION THAT HAD BEEN LIVE
SINCE THE ROUND THAT INTRODUCED IT.

Three items, taken in the order the session was asked for: implement what the
analyzer does not do, then pay the debt that work is nearest to.

ITEM 442 -- TAG 24 IS A DOCUMENT AND IS NOW WALKED. RFC 8949 section 3.4.5.1
says the content of tag 24 is "a byte string containing an encoded CBOR data
item". That is a statement about the ENCODING, not about meaning, so walking it
invents nothing -- the argument item 433 used to open CBOR at all. The module
doc had bound this to the bignum refusal in one sentence, and that sentence was
wrong about which of the two is which: a bignum needs a reading, an embedded
document needs a walk, and this module already had one.

The three decisions the item asked for, and why each went the way it did. The
buffer is NARROWED rather than copied, so every offset the sub-walk reports is
still an offset into the capture; a row whose span means something else is
worse than an absent row. The depth counter is SHARED, so nesting through tag
24 cannot buy a fresh budget for the price of a wrapper. And a byte string that
is not a document leaves the OUTER walk good -- section 3.4.5.1 is a validity
rule, the outer encoding is well-formed whatever the bytes hold, so the partial
rows are dropped and one row says where the inner walk stopped. The indefinite
form is deliberately not re-entered: its content is the concatenation of its
chunks, so the document would exist only in a buffer this walk had to build.

ITEM 441 -- DUPLICATE MAP KEYS ARE REPORTED, NOT ENFORCED. Section 5.6 makes a
map with two equal keys invalid and nothing here looked. Comparison is on the
PATH SEGMENT, which is right twice over: section 5.6's equality is over the
generic data model rather than the encoding, so 1 in its immediate form and 1
in its one-byte form are one key though their bytes share nothing. The count
lands on the map's own row rather than raising an error, because a duplicate is
invalid CBOR that is nonetheless perfectly well-formed CBOR -- refusing it would
make `inspect` refute an `application/cbor` label over bytes that really are
CBOR, which is the disease item 433 cured.

ITEM 443 -- AND THE GATE FOUND A LIVE ONE. Item 434's namespace works because
the escape rule emits a backslash only before a `.` or a `\`, and nothing
checked that. Writing the check found the float key form emitting `\f1.5` --
an unescaped separator INSIDE a reserved segment, so `{1.5: 1}` and
`{1.0: {"5": 1}}` both reach `$.\f1.5`. Item 434's own collision, back through
the escape hatch rather than the front door, live since R311y914 with a test
asserting the broken form. That is item 438 again: the wrong premise was inside
a test's own claim.

Two gates, because one was not enough. The namespace check cannot see this
class at all -- `\f1` and `5` are both perfectly legal segments. So a second
gate compares the harm itself: two different documents must not reach the same
leaf path.

AND ITS DOCUMENT HAD NOTHING TO SPEAK ONE WITH.

Round 1970.decision_summary:
A ROW WAS REPORTING THE INTERVAL [419, 0], AND BOTH SURFACES WERE PRINTING IT.

This round set out at open-debt item 270 -- an interest declared and withdrawn
INSIDE a capture is credited with every matching byte, not with the bytes that
travelled while it was open -- and item 270 says the materials are already
there: `declared_at` / `withdrawn_at` on the declaration, `first_anchor` /
`last_anchor` on the traffic row, with only the comparison missing.

THE MATERIALS ARE THERE AND THEY ARE NOT COMPARABLE, which is a different
sentence and the one that mattered. An anchor is `PassiveFrame::stream_offset`,
and that field carries two different kinds of number: a byte offset ABSOLUTE
WITHIN ONE DIRECTION on a stream link, and the INDEX of the packet on a
datagram one. `passive.rs` pins the first in a test of its own and
`quic_datagrams`' doc states the second. Nothing on a frame says which, and
`Dissection::message_lists`' own doc has said so since R311y718.

A `ThroughputTable` row is keyed on the KEYEXPR ALONE, so it folds records from
every flow and both directions -- and it was updating one anchor pair from
whichever record arrived. One TCP flow whose two directions both carry
`shared/topic`, with direction A carrying it after 400 bytes of padding and
direction B carrying it first in its own stream, produces the pair `[419, 0]`.
That is not a span, it is not a floor, and it is not anything; and
`census_json` and `report` both emit the two numbers bare.

SO THE PREREQUISITE IS BUILT, NOT ITEM 270 ITSELF. `AnchorSpace` says what a
list's anchors MEAN, `message_lists` hands it out beside the frames because it
is the only place that knows, and a row now remembers which space its pair
belongs to: a record from another space does not move the pair, and the row
says `anchors_exact: false` instead. The interval stays true and becomes
partial, rather than staying whole and becoming false.

THE FIELD LAYER SOLVED THIS FOR ITS OWN ROWS IN R311y855 by putting
`offset_space` on the row. The rest of the planes never got it, and the
coordinate defect this workspace has now paid for three times -- R311y713's run
map, R311y855's field rows, and this -- is filed as item 452 with the
declaration and node anchors still bare.

THE GUARD BUILT ONE ROUND AGO CANNOT SEE THIS, and that is why item 379 is its

grammar, so two writers could disagree forever with every gate green.

writers produce the same bytes for the same input; the RFC's own table moved to
live beside the implementation.

THE MERGE DIRECTION IS THE RFC'S. Five short forms is what section 7 defines
and what the report module's doc had argued for, so the richer behaviour won and
the shared escaper gained them. That moves two characters' bytes on every
surface that calls it -- admin, config, REST, the census and the report -- and
nothing in the workspace pinned either spelling, which was measured rather than

Round 1976.decision_summary:
THE LAST FOUR ROUNDS WERE THIS ITEM'S EVIDENCE, WRITTEN BY THIS SESSION.

`wz_dissect.h` states the rule in prose: the ABI revision moves when a SYMBOL or
the memory rule changes, never when the JSON gains fields. Which side of that
line a key change falls on has been decided by reading, every time, and nothing
checked the reading.

R311y917 added `dropped_by_limits` to a document. R311y919 added `offset_space`
six times. Each round argued in a comment that an ADDED key is the widening the
read-by-name contract permits, and that argument is correct. What it does not
cover is a key REMOVED or RENAMED, which is a break -- and R311y919 came within
one edit of renaming `first_packet`, stopping on the same prose reading rather
than on anything that could have refused.

SO THE WHOLE KEY SET IS PINNED, NOT A RULE ABOUT ADDITIONS. A gate that only
refused removals would let the shape grow unremarked, and the growth is exactly
what a consumer pinned to a revision needs to be told about. Pinning the set
sends BOTH directions to one table, in the commit that changes the document,
where the author has to say which side of the header's line the change is on.
It is what `capi_abi_pin.py` does for the symbol set, one layer in: that pins
what a consumer links, this pins what those symbols hand back.

THE TABLE WAS MEASURED, NOT TRANSCRIBED. The first run carried an empty table
and printed the 136 keys the four planes produce, which is the same trick the
C1bz budget was re-measured with last round. A table typed from reading the
emitters would have been a third statement of the document's shape.

AND THE ROUND MEASURED SOMETHING IT DID NOT GO LOOKING FOR. All four of the most
recent hosted runs are queued or in progress; not one has completed. The
round-start step that scans for a completed red has been measuring nothing for

population of zero reading green, and it is the loop's own safety check that has
gone quiet. Filed as item 459 rather than fixed, because the owner's instruction

Round 1977.decision_summary:
THE ITEM SAID TWO COUNTERS ARE STRUCTURALLY ZERO. THEY ARE, AND THAT IS THE
SMALLER HALF.

Item 247 says `SkipCensus::ipv4_fragment` and `ipv6_fragment` are structurally
zero while two documents keep printing them. Verified rather than taken: the
whole workspace mentions `SkipReason::Ipv4Fragment` in exactly two places, and
both are the `match` arms that COUNT it. Nothing produces either.

The reason is on the variant's own doc. R311y606 changed `decapsulate` to report
every piece as `Transport::IpFragment` and leave reassembly to the consumer,
retaining the skip reason for "a consumer that does not reassemble". This
crate's consumer always reassembles: `pub mod frag` sits behind no feature at
all, so that consumer does not exist here.

WHAT THE ITEM DOES NOT SAY IS THE PART THAT HURTS. This is not "a zero is
printed". It is that THE NAME LIES. A reader looking at a capture of nothing but
IPv4 fragments sees `"ipv4_fragment": 0` and concludes there were none. The
counter that actually moved is `ip_fragment_pending`, whose name says something
narrower than what it is carrying.

SO THE STATE IS PINNED RATHER THAN THE FIELDS REMOVED. A test builds a capture
that IS a fragment, asserts `ip_fragment_pending` moved -- which is the
discriminating arm, without which a build that skipped the packet for any other

Round 1978.decision_summary:
THE COMPILER WAS ALREADY FORCING TWO OF THE THREE PLACES, AND THE HOLE WAS
EXACTLY THE ONE THE ITEM NAMED.

Item 301 says the totality of `Misbound` rests on an array the test writes by
hand: add a third variant, leave the array alone, and the gate walks a stale
set. Verified before anything was changed: the test opened with
`let all = [Misbound::Rule, Misbound::Publisher]`.

What that array was hiding is narrower than "a new variant goes unnamed".
`name`'s match is exhaustive, so a third variant cannot reach a consumer without
being given a word. What it CAN do is reach one untested -- the duplicate-word
check, which is the whole point of that test, only ever sees what the array
lists.

SO THE ARRAY IS WALKED INSTEAD OF WRITTEN. `Misbound::next` is an exhaustive
match returning the next variant, and the test derives the list by walking it.
The forcing is two-layered: a third variant MUST take an arm in `next`, and an
author who writes `Both => None` without linking it into the chain leaves the
walk one short of `NAMES`, which the length assertion compares. Neither half
alone is enough; together a variant cannot be added and go unvisited.

THE PROBES FAILED TO COMPILE TWICE, AND THAT IS HOW THE ROUND LEARNED SOMETHING.
A probe that does not build discriminates nothing, so each was fixed and re-run
-- and what stopped them was a THIRD exhaustive match, the note renderer, which
the compiler demanded an arm from before the assertion could speak. `Misbound`
therefore has three matches the compiler already guards, and the single
unguarded place was the test's own list. The item was right about the shape and
right about where.

The method is `cfg(test)`: nothing in a shipping build walks the variants, and
this workspace refuses a method with no caller -- measured, not assumed, by
leaving the attribute off and reading `method next is never used`. The forcing
therefore lands when the tests compile rather than when the crate does.

Round 1982.decision_summary:
Item 236 said the declaration dialect's discriminator rests on a premise
nobody asserted: a field-name declaration is told from a format rule by a
colon before the `=`, which bets that no key expression carries a colon.
The premise was inherited from an argv parser and never written down.

The bet is FALSE and the instance was live. The keyexpr canonizer rejects
`#`, `?`, an unbound `$` and several grammar shapes, and a colon is none of
them; this crate's pattern validation refuses an empty pattern and a
leading or trailing slash and nothing else. So a colon-bearing pattern
installed, `FormatMap::declarations` wrote it as `demo/temp:c=protobuf`,
and the reader read that back as a field name. The round trip the module
documents as its contract was broken by an ordinary character.

The repair refuses the ambiguity by name rather than resolving it. A
pattern carrying the discriminator is rejected at both install doors with
a new error that says why. That converts a silent misread into a refusal
the reader can act on -- rename the topic, or declare its parent.

What it deliberately does NOT do is make such a topic declarable. The two
spellings differ only by the colon, and the path grammar cannot help
because a path is validated as non-empty and nothing more, so the only
resolution is a delimiter no key expression may carry -- which changes the
dialect every existing declaration is written in. That is an owner's call
and is filed as its own item.

Item 448 said the reserved path-segment gate measures the CORPUS rather
than the CODE: `RESERVED_PATH_LETTERS` was a literal list inside the test
module, nothing shipping was bound to it, and a walker that began emitting
a new reserved form touched no list at all. The set assertion then said
nothing in either direction, because it compares what the corpus produced
against what was declared and the new form is in neither.

The claim was MEASURED before it was repaired: a new reserved form was put
into the walker where no corpus payload can reach it, and the gate passed
with nineteen tests green. That is the item's harm, reproduced.

The repair moves the set into shipping code as an enum whose `letter()` is
exhaustive, so a new form cannot be written without claiming a letter, and
whose chain is walked to build the set the gate compares against. Deriving
it swaps the roles of the two directions usefully: a new form is declared
the moment it can be written, so its ABSENCE from the corpus becomes the
failure -- which is the direction that used to be silent.

What this does not do is make a raw `"\\q"` literal impossible. Catching
that needs a source lint over escape literals with an exclusion list, which
is the shape item 400 warns decays into a filter bound to nothing. That is
filed rather than attempted.

signature while meaning something else entirely: it trims each flow's
OUTPUT after the whole dissection is built, so a caller asking for ten
messages still pays for the file. The header and the Rust doc say so and
nothing measured it, which item 450 filed as 438's relative -- true prose
nobody checks.

Its first candidate was a rename, which breaks a published signature. Its
third was a gate holding the sentence, and a sentence about behaviour is
held by behaviour: the two arguments leave DIFFERENT MARKS on the
document. The cap shortens it and leaves `dropped_by_limits` alone; the
preset moves that group. One test, both marks.

Two things this round measured that the item did not say.

The first assertion failed, and the fixture was why: the tap-cap capture
is many flows carrying one message each, so a per-flow output cap trims
nothing and the capped and uncapped documents came back byte-identical.
The assertion was right. "Is the implementation wrong or the assertion
wrong" needs a third question -- can the fixture reach the axis at all.

The second is sharper. A probe that wired the cap to a live-tap preset --
the exact conflation this test exists to catch -- PASSED, because the arm
asserting "the cap does not move the group" was running on a capture too
small for any ceiling to bite. Zero was true either way. An assertion that
a value does not move has to run where the value CAN move.

Round 1994.decision_summary:
The owner asked for the SCE pin to be bumped. The bump is routine -- 21
upstream commits, and all eighteen out/** changes are the template-hash
line, so no emit moved. What this round is about is what the bump exposed.

`--layer B2` failed on a build host with `unknown filter: filter
host_invoker is unknown (entry_exit_actions.rs.jinja2:462)`. It named a
template, a filter and a line number, and not one of them was the defect:
that host carried an sce-codegen built from the previous pin. `bx` prunes
`vendor/sce/target` after every remote run, so an absent or foreign oracle
is the ordinary state there rather than the exotic one.

Two questions had been asked of that binary and both were the wrong
question. EXISTENCE: Layers B and B2 each opened `[[ ! -x <bin> ]] && SKIP`,
so an absent oracle printed a pass-shaped skip -- the SKIP-green half of
open-debt item 413. MTIME: R114's freshness gate compares the binary's
mtime to the pin commit's time, which answers when it was built and never
what from. Move the pin BACKWARDS and a binary built yesterday is "newer"
than a pin committed last week; any rsync or tar that resets mtimes defeats
it the same way. It also lived in Layer B alone, with Layer B2's own comment
outsourcing the question -- "In a full run-ci, Layer B builds +
freshness-checks the binary before this lane" -- which holds for a full
sweep and for nothing else.

The question that is right is PROVENANCE: which vendor/sce state produced
this binary. build-sce.sh now records it and every consumer compares it, so
the failure that cost this round becomes a sentence naming both revisions
and the one command that repairs them.

Filed as 468 rather than folded into 413, because the mechanism differs: 413
is absence, where the lane does not run and prints green; this is staleness,
where the lane DOES run and answers about a different tree.

Round 1995.decision_summary:
The owner asked for the analyzer gap that most matters, proven by test
rather than by reading, and implemented on the spot. The instruments were
run rather than quoted: 214 atoms / 139 active / 86 PARTIAL, analyzer-plane
open debt 60, analysis-surface-parity green. From the register's own text --
not its index -- item 260 was the only entry naming a capability this reader
NAMES AND CANNOT READ.

GRETAP. R311y864 opened GRE and stopped at the ethertype, reporting
`GRE payload ethertype(s) not walked: 0x6558` and zero flows for a capture
off any cloud overlay. It stopped on purpose, and its reason is the whole
shape of this round: TEB's payload is a whole ETHERNET FRAME, and the link
layer already has TWO arms -- `strip_raweth` answers before `strip_link`
does. Handing the inner frame to `strip_link` alone would send a zenoh-pico
raweth frame INSIDE the tunnel to `NotIp`, furniture, while the identical
frame outside it reached its own arm. That is R311y863's two-doors defect
regenerated one carrier down, and half-opening the tunnel would have bought
a capability by planting a misread.

So the fix is not the TEB arm. The fix is that the link layer became ONE
door -- `enter_link` -- and the tunnel walks through it. `step_gre` is the
same shape for the same reason: the GRE step is reached from the whole-packet
door and from the reassembly door, and R311y863 measured what happens when a
step is written at one of them.

THE DEFECT WAS DEMONSTRATED BEFORE IT WAS FIXED. Three legs were written
against the old build and three failed -- `GrePayload(25944)` where a flow,
a raweth datagram and `NotIp` belonged -- while the control leg passed. That
is what says the population was reachable and the instrument could see it.

The round also paid off a red the tip was carrying. Layer C0 gate-provenance
had been failing on main since R1994 added `sce-codegen-oracle.sh` without a
citation, and the second red job was that job dying early, not a second
fault.

work, the visual axis is not this repo's, and the other half is not to be

472 said a generated config had no pre-flight validation. `zenoh_config.rs:457`
is `pub fn validate(&self) -> Vec<ConfigDefect>`, and its doc already states
its scope. The one true clause left in that item -- contradictions BETWEEN

BOTH WRONG ANSWERS CAME FROM A GREP THAT FOUND NOTHING. The register's rule --
run it before writing "blocked" or "not started" -- was QUOTED INSIDE 469's own

So the finding this round buys is not about the tap or the config. It is that
FILING a debt is a verdict: item 47 is that a register reason outlives the code
it describes, and this is its worst form, a reason that was false at birth. A
filed item becomes the next round's work; wrong, it either wastes a round or
builds a second copy of something that exists.

Round 1999.decision_summary:
Item 470 is closed: `wz-analyze --interface <name> --for <seconds>` reads a
live AF_PACKET tap, and a capability that had tests and no caller since
R311y594 now has one.

Two things had to exist first and only one of them was the crate boundary
Round 1998 moved. The other was found here: `analyze_request` built its
`Dissection` from capture bytes in exactly one place, and everything after that
point is the report. Lifting that one construction out gives
`analyze_dissection`, which is the whole of the report over a dissection
somebody else built -- and a tap is somebody else.

THE STOP RULE IS THE ITEM, not the flag. A tap has no end, so a live read that
stopped on its own would produce a report that looks complete because the TOOL
stopped rather than because the traffic did, and a short read and a quiet
network are indistinguishable on the page. `--for` is therefore REQUIRED with
`--interface` -- no default, because a default is a number the operator neither
chose nor sees -- and the report NAMES the bound that ended the read. The
kernel's own drop count goes on the same line and BEFORE the report, since a
reader who learns the tap dropped packets only below the totals has already
read the totals as a fact about the network.

Five refusals, each because the alternative is a flag that quietly changes
nothing -- the rule this parser already applies twice. A capture file together
with `--interface` (two sources, one report). `--interface` without `--for`.
`--for` without `--interface`, because a file ends by itself. And `--quic` /
`--quic-cid-len`, which are the interesting pair: QUIC recovery re-reads the
CAPTURE's own bytes, which a tap does not keep, so on a live read they would
be accepted and do nothing. Refused rather than silently ignored.

The parity gate forced the last question and the answer is a decision, not a
gap: the C ABI takes capture BYTES, which is what lets a C consumer feed a tap
it opened itself, and widening it to open sockets would move a privilege across
an FFI boundary to buy a caller something it can already do.

THE TWICE-AND-DIFF IS THE PATTERN TO REACH FOR FIRST when a plane has a self-contained upstream example. z_bytes.c asserts its own round trips, so running it on wz proves only self-consistency; linking the SAME program against the real libzenohc.so and diffing stdout is what caught the slice arrangement, and the damage probe shows every assert still passing while the output differed. A DAMAGE PROBE IS NOT OPTIONAL AND IT CHANGED A CLAIM THIS ROUND. Probing the condvar test showed it discriminated nothing, and following that back showed the module doc asserting a property the implementation does not have. Two attempts to build a discriminating test both failed to force the window, so it is written down as an unwitnessed residual instead of being implied by a green test. The general rule: when a probe leaves a test GREEN, suspect the CLAIM before suspecting the probe.

NAMED RESIDUALS, written down rather than left to be inferred from silence. (1) The condvar's unlock-then-park window is argued from the source and NOT measured; it cannot be forced through the public API without an injection point in shipped code. (2) The unstable-API arm's opaque sizes are transcribed-by-absence -- there is no second oracle on this machine -- so a consumer on that build is unchecked for the new types. (3) A FIFO channel GROWS past its capacity rather than blocking, because wz's producer is the drive thread that serves every face and blocking it on one slow C consumer would stall unrelated sessions. (4) z_get_options / z_querier_options accept and IGNORE congestion control, express, priority, locality and encoding; a program that sets them is not misled about the API and IS misled about the wire. (5) z_reply_err is exported but no example drives it, and the owned z_owned_reply_err_t is not declared at all.

Round 311y539.decision_summary: R311y539 -- the zenoh-c C ABI went from 11 to 22 of 22 linkable upstream examples, and the eight planes that moved it were mostly spellings over the shared wz-capi-core model, except for the one thing that genuinely had to be designed: the ESCAPE. A query, a sample or a reply that leaves its callback must copy itself onto the heap and re-bind the cached views at the new address, and an escaped QUERY owes two further things its dispatch cannot supply -- the face session to reply through, and a ResponseFinal that must not go out until the C side drops it, because a querier that sees the final stops listening and a broken hold produces no reply rather than a late one. The VLE codec and the scouting drive moved into wz-capi-core so one implementation serves both ABIs, since a wire-format encoder duplicated per ABI stays green against its own decoder while diverging from upstream. The footprint gate widened from 20 to 51 measured types and its export was reshaped from a struct into an array with a returned count, because a 51-entry struct whose test-side copy is one field short is a stack overwrite rather than an assertion. The strongest new witness is compiling upstream z_bytes.c once and linking it twice: it self-asserts every serialization round trip, so running it on wz proves only self-consistency, and the diff against the real libzenohc.so is what catches the slice arrangement -- a damage probe collapsing three appends into one slice leaves every assert passing and the exit code zero while printing one line where the reference prints three. A second damage probe was the round's correction: the condvar test discriminated nothing, and following that back showed this module's own doc claiming the generation counter closed the lost-wakeup window when it does not. The counter suppresses spurious wakeups, which z_ping.c needs because it waits with no predicate loop; the ordering closes the window; and the window itself is now a named unwitnessed residual rather than a property a green test implies.
verification_bullets: MEASURED, NOT CLAIMED: api-compat-c went 11 -> 22 of 22 upstream zenoh-c examples linking, reported by Layer C1cc's own coverage script on every run. The 7 ORACLE-ONLY examples stay out of the denominator. 98 distinct symbols were implemented, and the list was read off `nm -u` per example rather than chosen.

A LINK IS NOT A PASS, so six legs RUN the new planes. Five put a REAL zenoh-pico process on the far side: upstream z_queryable.c on wz answers a pico z_get and the FOREIGN process prints the payload; upstream z_get.c on wz renders a reply a pico queryable chose; z_queryable_with_channels.c on wz answers from its own thread through a fifo; z_pull.c on wz pulls a pico sample out of a ring channel; z_ping.c on wz completes four round trips against a pico z_pong.

THE FOOTPRINT GATE WIDENED 8 -> 20 -> 51 types, all measured against the INSTALLED header by a C compiler, and all 51 agree. DAMAGE PROBE: setting z_owned_query_t to 128 instead of 136 reds it with the type named; restoring it greens. The export was reshaped from a struct to a (buffer, cap) -> count array in the same commit, because a 51-entry struct whose test-side copy is one field short is a stack overwrite rather than an assertion.

THE SHARPEST WITNESS IS THE TWICE-AND-DIFF, and its damage probe is the reason it exists. upstream z_bytes.c is self-asserting (NDEBUG undefined), so running it on wz already shows the serializer and deserializer agree WITH EACH OTHER -- which is what a permutation-invariant round trip proves, and not the claim. Linking the same program against the real libzenohc.so and diffing stdout catches what the round trip cannot: DAMAGE PROBE -- collapsing the writer's appends into one slice leaves every assert PASSING and the program exiting 0, while printing `slice len: 9` where the reference prints three `slice len: 3` lines. The leg reds on exactly that.

THE RESPONSE-FINAL HOLD IS WITNESSED BY ITS OWN DAMAGE. Removing the per-escape hold makes the CHANNEL queryable leg red (20 s, no reply at all -- the querier saw the final and stopped listening) while the in-dispatch queryable leg stays GREEN. The two legs separate the two claims.

A DAMAGE PROBE CAUGHT A TEST THAT PROVED NOTHING, AND A DOC THAT WAS WRONG. The first condvar test slept so the waiter had certainly parked; dropping the generation counter left it GREEN. That exposed the module doc's claim that the counter closes the lost-wakeup window -- it does not; the ORDER (take the condvar mutex before releasing the caller's) does, and the counter suppresses SPURIOUS wakeups, which z_ping.c needs because it calls z_condvar_wait with no predicate loop. A second attempt to force the window (block the signaller on the caller's mutex) also failed to discriminate: releasing the signaller does not make it RUN first. The window is NOT witnessed and is now a NAMED RESIDUAL; what the test does cover is gross liveness plus the mutex-retaken half, which DOES discriminate (removing the re-lock reds it).

carry_forward_bullets: R311y540 = the arm nothing was measuring. Layer C1cc compares wz against the INSTALLED header, which exists for exactly one feature combination, so wz's OTHER arms were unchecked by construction — and that is where a `z_owned_bytes_t` of 40 sat from R311y498 to R311y540. The fix is to stop needing an installed header: zenoh-c GENERATES its opaque header from `build-resources/opaque-types`, a crate whose purpose is to fail compilation with the sizes, so any feature combination is measurable from one source checkout.

CALIBRATE THE GENERATED ORACLE, AND EXPECT THE TOOLCHAIN TO BE THE VARIABLE. The no-unstable arm had to reproduce the installed header before its other arms could be believed. It took two attempts: the feature list turned out not to matter, and the TOOLCHAIN did — `z_owned_task_t` is 32 under zenoh-c's pinned 1.85.0 and 24 under 1.97.0. Any future "regenerate upstream's own artifact and compare" check should pin the channel from the upstream checkout's `rust-toolchain.toml` first, not last.

THE OBSERVATION CAN BE RIGHT AND THE ATTRIBUTION WRONG, AGAIN. R311y498 measured a real 40-vs-32 difference between two zenoh-c builds and recorded it against `Z_FEATURE_UNSTABLE_API`; it is `Z_FEATURE_SHARED_MEMORY`. This is the same shape as the exclusion-carries-two-claims pattern: the half nobody re-checks is which cause the difference belongs to.

A LANE THAT REDS ONCE STILL NEEDS A RATE ON BOTH ARMS, and this round is the case where the rate said "real defect" rather than "noise": 18/20 against the reference's 20/20. The measurement also refuted the excuse that was available, since the reference did not fail at all.

WHEN A FIX MAKES A RESIDUAL TESTABLE, TEST IT. R311y539 shipped the condvar window as an unwitnessed residual after two attempts to force it failed. Both failed because the property did not hold — the implementation lost the signal. Changing the implementation made the test trivial and deterministic. A residual that resists testing is worth re-reading as a possible defect rather than a limit of the harness.

NEXT: arm the gate on hosted CI. `WZ_C1CC_OPAQUE_ARMS=1` plus a job that clones zenoh-c's SOURCE (the release archive does not carry `build-resources/opaque-types`) and installs the pinned toolchain; the generator target dirs cache the same way the zenoh-c oracle already does. Until then the four-arm check runs only where someone runs it by hand. Still open from R311y539: the 7 ORACLE-ONLY examples need an SHM-built zenoh-c INSTALL (not just the size table), and wz exports no SHM API surface.

It runs upstream's own opaque-type generator for all four feature combinations under zenoh-c's PINNED toolchain, CALIBRATES the no-shm/no-unstable arm against the installed header first, then builds each wz arm and compares it. Round 311y540.decision_summary: R311y540 -- the zenoh-c ABI arm that nothing was measuring, and the lost wakeup it was hiding next to. Layer C1cc compares wz against the INSTALLED zenoh_opaque.h, which exists for exactly one Z_FEATURE_* combination, so every other arm wz ships was unchecked by construction -- and that is where a 40-byte z_owned_bytes_t sat from R311y498 until now. Measuring it meant not needing an installed header at all: zenoh-c generates its opaque header from a crate whose whole purpose is to fail compilation with the sizes, so any feature combination is measurable from one source checkout. Calibrating that generator against the installed header took removing two variables and the second one was the surprise -- the feature list did not matter, the TOOLCHAIN did, and pinning zenoh-c's own 1.85.0 took the agreement from 61 of 62 to 62 of 62. With a validated oracle the 40 resolved: it is real, and it is the SHARED-MEMORY size, not the unstable one. R311y498 had measured a genuine difference and recorded it against the wrong axis, which also meant the axis that actually moves 8 of the 19 types wz declares had never been modelled at all. So the sizes become a two-axis table, a zenoh-c-shared-memory feature covers the layout half of the second axis, and a new script drives upstream's generator for all four combinations and compares each against a cdylib built for it -- damage-probed against the pre-y540 tree, where it names all three wrong types on the default arm and leaves the other arm green. Separately, Layer C1cc red once on the z_ping leg, and the rate rather than a retry settled it: 18 of 20 against the real libzenohc.so's 20 of 20, a wz defect with no reference-is-racy-too defence. The cause was the condvar losing a signal that arrived before its waiter -- the exact window R311y539 had shipped as a named unwitnessed residual, reachable enough to hang an unmodified upstream program. Replacing the generation counter with a pending flag closes it, takes both arms to 20 of 20, and makes the residual a deterministic test: signal with nothing waiting, then wait. Two earlier drafts of that test could never discriminate anything because the property did not hold; the fix is what made it assertable.
verification_bullets: THE ORACLE WAS CALIBRATED BEFORE IT WAS BELIEVED, and getting there took removing two variables. Upstream's generator emits `type: X, align: N, size: M` as compilation errors; its no-unstable arm must reproduce the INSTALLED `zenoh_opaque.h` or its other arms describe some other build. First run: 61 of 62. The gap was `z_owned_task_t` (32 vs 24) and it was the TOOLCHAIN, not the feature list — `zenoh/default` and the archive's exact feature list give identical tables, while zenoh-c's pinned 1.85.0 against the ambient 1.97.0 does not. Under the pin: 62 of 62, exact.

THE 40 WAS REAL AND MISATTRIBUTED. `z_owned_bytes_t` is 32 on both unstable arms and 40 with `Z_FEATURE_SHARED_MEMORY`. R311y498 measured a genuine difference and recorded it against the wrong axis; the number then sat on wz's DEFAULT arm, which Layer C1cc never selects (it reads the installed header, and `install-zenoh-c.sh` provisions the no-unstable archive), so nothing had ever compared it to anything.

THE AXIS THAT WAS WRONG IS THE BIGGER ONE. Shared-memory moves 8 of the 19 types wz declares; unstable moves 2. Checking only the unstable axis — the obvious reading of the old comment — would have left the defect in place.

DAMAGE PROBE ON THE GATE, run against the pre-y540 tree: it reds the DEFAULT arm naming all three wrong types (`z_owned_bytes_t` 40 vs 32, `z_owned_sample_t` 184 vs 216, `z_owned_reply_t` 184 vs 240) and leaves the no-unstable arm green, exit 1 against exit 0 on the fixed tree. A second probe, reverting `z_owned_bytes_t` to a single size, reds exactly the two SHM arms and leaves the two non-SHM arms green — so the gate separates the axes rather than merely noticing something.

THE CONDVAR DEFECT WAS FOUND BY A LANE GOING RED ONCE AND THEN MEASURED RATHER THAN RETRIED. Layer C1cc red on the z_ping leg, hung in its warmup. Rate over 20 runs against a real zenoh-pico `z_pong`: wz 18/20, the real `libzenohc.so` 20/20 — so "the reference is racy too" was not available. After the pending flag: wz 20/20, reference 20/20. The window R311y539 had shipped as a NAMED UNWITNESSED RESIDUAL was reachable, and it hung an unmodified upstream program.

THAT RESIDUAL IS NOW A COVERED CASE, and the fix is what made it testable. With a generation counter the property did not hold, so there was nothing to assert; with the flag the test is deterministic — signal with nothing waiting, then wait, and the wait must return. DAMAGE PROBE: reinstating the discard HANGS the test on that first line, which is the discrimination two earlier drafts of it could never get.

carry_forward_bullets: R311y541 = the second oracle, installed. `install-zenoh-c-shm.sh` builds zenoh-c from source with shared-memory + unstable, and Layer C1ce measures against it. The headline is that the number got WORSE and that is the improvement: 22 of 22 with 7 examples excluded became 21 of 29 with none excluded. A denominator that omits what you have not built is a denominator that cannot move.

BUILD THE ORACLE RATHER THAN EXCLUDING WHAT IT WOULD COVER. The 7 ORACLE-ONLY examples had been out of the denominator since R311y498 with a correct-but-permanent justification ("a property of the oracle build, not of wz"). It was true and it was also a thing that could simply be built. When an exclusion's reason is "the reference we happen to have cannot express this", check whether a different reference can be provisioned before accepting it.

READ EVERY AXIS THE ORACLE DECLARES, NOT THE ONE YOU KNEW ABOUT. `_runci_build_capi_c_for_oracle` read Z_FEATURE_UNSTABLE_API and nothing else, which was correct while one axis was known and silently wrong the moment a second oracle existed. Same for the footprint gate's advice string, which this round's damage probe caught telling a reader to build the wrong arm. A selector over a feature space needs to enumerate the space.

NEXT, and it is now the same task for two things: ARM BOTH on hosted CI. C1ce needs a job that runs `install-zenoh-c-shm.sh` (minutes, cacheable exactly like the existing zenoh-c oracle cache) plus WZ_C1CE_REQUIRE=1; the R311y540 four-arm gate needs the same job to set WZ_C1CC_OPAQUE_ARMS=1 and clone zenoh-c's SOURCE. Both are provisioning, not code.

THEN: the 8 that do not link. Two families — ze_advanced_publisher/subscriber (the wz core already has advanced pubsub; this is a spelling, like the query plane was) and the z_shm_* provider/buffer surface (genuinely its own subsystem, and the one place `zenoh-c-shared-memory` covering LAYOUT ONLY starts to bite).

Round 311y541.decision_summary: R311y541 -- the second api-compat-c oracle, built and installed, and the denominator it makes honest. Seven of upstream's 29 examples had been out of Layer C1cc's ratio since R311y498 because they do not COMPILE against the published archive's header, which is the build with neither shared-memory nor the unstable API. The justification was correct and it was also permanent: no amount of wz work moves a number whose denominator excludes the part wz has not built. So the other oracle is now built from source -- copied out of the reference clone first, because zenoh-c's CMake generates its manifest in the source tree and a reference the build mutates is not a reference -- and Layer C1ce measures against it. The result is that the headline number goes DOWN, from 22 of 22 with seven excluded to 21 of 29 with none, which is the same library measured against a corpus that no longer hides what it does not implement. The install is also the third independent confirmation of R311y540's size table: upstream's generator predicted 40 and 232 for the two types that move most, the new header declares exactly those, and the C-compiler footprint gate agrees on all 51 types -- three mechanisms, no disagreement. Two selectors had to learn that the feature space has two axes rather than one: the lane's cdylib arm selection, which read only Z_FEATURE_UNSTABLE_API and would have built the wrong library for this oracle, and the footprint gate's own failure advice, which told a reader with the SHM header to build with default features. Round 311y545.decision_summary: R311y545 -- the zenoh-c ABI's publish options stop being decoration, and measuring how they should reach the wire turned up two value defects the layout gate could never have seen. Until this round z_publisher_options_t and z_publisher_put_options_t were declared, sized, gated -- and their fields read by nothing, so a program that set an encoding, a priority, a congestion mode, an express bit or an attachment was correct about the API and wrong about the wire; wz-capi-c/src/encoding.rs said so in its own module doc, and half of what it said was already false (PublishOptions::with_encoding has existed since R233 and is foreign-proven wz->pico at R311y207). The declare path now folds encoding / congestion / priority / express into a bundle stored on the publisher, which is upstream's _declare_publisher_inner shape; the put path applies a per-put encoding override and attachment over it, taking the owned fields unconditionally as upstream documents; z_publisher_delete inherits the QoS. z_put_options_t and z_delete_options_t did not exist at all -- both entry points took a void* and neither _options_default was exported, so a program using the documented shape did not LINK, which a 29-of-29 census cannot notice because no upstream example passes them. Both are now declared field-for-field, both defaults ship, both are honoured, and both joined the footprint gate. THE TWO DEFECTS: this crate carried zenoh-PICO's enum values, and zenoh-c INVERTS both -- Z_CONGESTION_CONTROL_BLOCK is 0 and DROP is 1 where pico has them the other way round, and z_reliability_t is BEST_EFFORT 0 / RELIABLE 1 where wz had RELIABLE 0. So z_publisher_options_default wrote BLOCK where upstream writes DROP. A value nobody reads cannot be wrong, which is exactly why it survived; honouring the fields is what would have turned it into a wire divergence. Both are now gated by a new twice-and-diff leg -- one C probe, compiled once, linked against wz's cdylib AND the real libzenohc, stdout diffed over every field of all four *_options_default families -- and the reliability half runs only on Layer C1ce, because this machine's installed header defines no Z_FEATURE_UNSTABLE_API and therefore has no such field to compare. The wire half is proven by a foreign process twice over: upstream z_pub.c makes a real zenoh-pico print "with encoding: text/plain", and upstream z_pub_thr.c -- the only upstream example that populates z_publisher_options_t -- makes it print priority 1 / congestion 1 / express 1 where a dropped struct prints pico's defaults 5 / 0 / 0. Both damage-probed with attribution in both directions. The encoding id table moved to wz-capi-core as an ABI-neutral SSOT so both C ABIs read one transcription, and wz-capi-pico's oracle against the real libzenohpico now pins that shared constant instead of a copy.

And z_liveliness_get_options_default wrote timeout_ms = 0 where the real library writes 10_000; this tree already carried "the 10 s default is matched by INSPECTION, not measurement" as a named residual, and the measurement says it was not matched. Two more showed ONLY on the unstable+SHM oracle, where the field exists at all: z_get_options_t.accept_replies and z_querier_options_t.accept_replies both defaulted to ZC_REPLY_KEYEXPR_ANY (0) where upstream defaults to ReplyKeyExpr::default() = MATCHING_QUERY (1). The three request-side congestion / accept_replies sites are now NAMED constants rather than literals, which is the concrete lesson: a bare integer in an options default is a transcription with no oracle. The probe additionally covers the eight ze_advanced_* families, which agree; and its vacuity guard now reads the oracle's own zenoh_configure.h and requires one line per STRUCT -- twelve on any oracle, ten more when Z_FEATURE_UNSTABLE_API is defined -- so a family silently dropped from the probe is a failed assertion instead of a shorter diff that still compares EQUAL. Separately, a full Layer C1 run went red once on handle_inbound_non_keepalive_does_not_touch_keepalive_slot, a test in a crate this arc does not touch. It is not a flake: R311la moved the RX-activity stamp out of the KeepAlive arm onto EVERY decoded transport message for zenoh-pico `_received` parity, and the test still asserted the pre-R311la property. It seeded the slot with now_monotonic_ms() and asserted the slot still held that value; the code overwrites it with now_monotonic_ms(), so the assertion held exactly when the clock had not ticked. It read GREEN for the same reason it was WRONG -- the two numbers it compared were equal by coincidence, not by the property it named. Rewritten to seed u64::MAX, a value the monotonic clock cannot produce, and to assert the restamp lands inside the call window.

Round 311y547.decision_summary: R311y547 -- the QUERY half of the accepted-and-ignored option list, and the discovery that the wire path for the biggest item had existed all along with a literal None wired into it. `z_query_reply_options_t::encoding` was documented in this crate as "Accepted and ignored", and the reason it stayed that way is that nobody looked one layer down: `ReplyOut::reply_keyed_attached` takes an `Option<&EncodingHint>` in its third parameter and `reply_keyed_encoded` exists beside it, both carrying the reply's inner MsgPut E-flag, both landed for the storage per-version reply. `wz-capi-c`'s `flush_one` passed `None` into that slot unconditionally. So a queryable that set `text/plain` answered every querier with `zenoh/bytes`, and the fix is to thread a field through two functions rather than to build anything. The same shape on the query side: `QueryOptions::encoding` collapses with `payload` into the `QueryMetadata::value` pair that `RequestQueryBuilder::query_value` emits as ext 0x03, and `z_get_options_t::encoding` / `z_querier_get_options_t::encoding` were dropped before reaching it. All three now thread. The reply half is witnessed by a DIFFERENTIAL WITH A FOREIGN ADJUDICATOR, which is a new shape for this file: no upstream example sets a reply encoding -- `z_queryable.c` takes the defaults and touches nothing -- so an upstream driver cannot reach the field at all, and the corpus rule's objection to a wz-authored program is answered by compiling ONE source TWICE, against wz's cdylib and the real libzenohc, putting a real zenoh-pico `z_get_attachment` on the far side of BOTH, and comparing what the FOREIGN process printed. Anything wz-flavoured about the driver appears on both arms and cancels. The query-side halves get a unit test at the seam and an explicit NON-CLAIM, because no zenoh-pico example renders the encoding of a query it received -- that is established by looking rather than assumed, and it is written down so a reader does not infer a gap from silence. The leg also cost one fixture correction worth recording: the first draft barriered on the LISTENING PORT, and the REFERENCE arm came back with an empty reply set, because pico's z_get is one-shot and takes the final notification as its answer if it queries before the queryable is declared. Round 311y549.decision_summary: R311y549 -- the SSOT-sink audit the debt ledger has carried as its highest-value unaudited item, run for the FIRST of the four planes and reported as one of four rather than as four. The item's literal question -- whether SubEntry / QblEntry / the liveliness entry / the advanced-subscriber entry have "a transient clone holder with a window like face_down's", the shape that made z_undeclare_matching_listener non-deterministic at R311y535 -- is ANSWERED NEGATIVE for all four by enumeration: there is no `.clone()` of any of the four sink fields anywhere in faces.rs. Every use is `(entry.sink)()`, a call through a reference, because those four are FACTORIES (`Arc<dyn Fn() -> Box<dyn FnMut ..>>`) rather than the callback itself. MatchingSink is `Arc<dyn Fn(bool)>` -- the callback -- which is exactly why it was clonable and why face_down could snapshot it. So the y535 shape does not transfer, and that is a structural fact rather than a measurement. What the audit found INSTEAD is a sharper question the ledger item did not name: RE-ENTRANCY. `SubscriberRegistry::unregister` drops the slot IN PLACE under the observer mutex, and `Subscriber::teardown` takes that mutex; matching has a thread-local `MatchingDeliveryGuard` precisely so a retirement from inside a callback DECLINES instead of blocking on its own frame's lock, and the other four planes have no equivalent. On a straight read that is a deadlock: a C subscriber callback calling `z_undeclare_subscriber` on itself would re-take a `std::sync::Mutex` the dispatch thread already holds. It is NOT one, and the reason is a mechanism the read had to reach two crates to find: R311lh gives each subscriber a DEFERRED-FIRE CELL, so the registry-installed sink only STAGES an owned Sample and the user callback runs in the DRAIN, after the observer lock has dropped. The probe proves it rather than asserting it, and proves three more things beside the return: the handle is gravestoned, the C `drop(context)` runs, and NOTHING reaches the callback in the 500 ms after it retired itself -- the take-call-restore question the deferred cell raises, since the cell is TAKEN across the C call and a restore that resurrected an unregistered slot would deliver into a context whose drop had already run. That last assertion is CALIBRATED: with the undeclare skipped, 24 samples land in the same window, so the zero is a measurement and not a silent link. The C drop deliberately LEAKS its context, because a probe that freed it could not distinguish "no further delivery" from "a use-after-free that read garbage". Three planes remain uninstrumented and are recorded as such.
verification_bullets: THE LITERAL DEBT QUESTION IS ANSWERED BY ENUMERATION, NOT BY ARGUMENT. Every occurrence of `sink` in wz-capi-core/src/faces.rs was read: the four factory fields are constructed once and invoked as `(entry.sink)()` at five sites (face_up replay x4, declare x4); there is no clone of any of them. The R311y535 hazard needed a CLONE held across a window, and MatchingSink is the only one of the five that is a callback rather than a factory.

THE RE-ENTRANT UNDECLARE IS MEASURED, and it does not deadlock. The probe's four assertions all hold: entered (the callback fired and called undeclare), returned (no deadlock), the handle is gravestoned (the undeclare did something), the C drop(context) ran (the last Arc<CClosure> fell).

THE POST-UNDECLARE ASSERTION IS CALIBRATED. Skipping the undeclare in the callback makes the same 500 ms window deliver 24 samples, so `after == 0` in the real leg is a measurement. Without that number the assertion would pass equally on a dead link.

RATE MEASURED BEFORE THE RESULT WAS TRUSTED: 0/20 over twenty whole-runs of the probe. A single green on a timing-shaped leg is not evidence, and this one has a 20 s deadline and a 500 ms window in it.

THE MECHANISM WAS ESTABLISHED, NOT ASSUMED. `Subscriber::teardown` -> `R::with_mutex_mut(&self.observer, |o| o.subscribers.unregister(id))`, `unregister` is a `retain` that drops the slot in place, `TokioRuntime::with_mutex_mut` is a plain std Mutex (poison-recovered, not reentrant), and `dispatch_iteration_event_with` holds that mutex across the registry fan. On those four facts alone the call deadlocks; R311lh's per-subscriber deferred-fire cell is what makes the user callback run after the lock drops instead.
LANES GREEN LOCAL: 0 32s, C0, C1 53s (2189 passed / 0 failed -- 2187 at R311y546, +1 for R311y547's unit test, +1 for this probe), C2, A4.

SCOPE, STATED RATHER THAN IMPLIED: ONE of the four planes is instrumented. Queryable, liveliness-subscriber and advanced-subscriber all reference the same `deferred_fire` machinery, which is a READING and not a measurement, and each needs its own probe. They stay OPEN.

Second, deferring the query plane's drains naively DROPS every local reply: the loopback Final completes and removes the pending entry while the handler jobs are still queued. Caught by the end-to-end queryable leg reading 1 handler / 0 replies, fixed by STAGING the Final so the queue's own FIFO puts it after the handlers. The pico ABI stays Remote-only and that is now a measurement rather than an inherited pin -- Z_FEATURE_LOCAL_SUBSCRIBER and Z_FEATURE_LOCAL_QUERYABLE both default to 0 in vendor/zenoh-pico/CMakeLists.txt, which is why pico's own option structs carry no locality field. R311y557 put the face-independent local plane in `wz-capi-core`, which BOTH C ABIs share, and verified it against the zenoh-c ABI only. The pico ABI is deliberately the opposite: `Z_FEATURE_LOCAL_SUBSCRIBER` defaults to 0 in a real zenoh-pico build, so a pico session's own `z_put` must NOT reach its own subscriber, and a plane whose whole job is that delivery had just been wired underneath it. The answer is that pico is intact, and the reason is not what either comment says. THE TWO PINS ARE INDEPENDENT AND EITHER ALONE SUFFICES, measured by probing them separately: unpin the publish only and the leg stays GREEN because the subscriber's `Remote` origin filters the sample; unpin the origin only and it stays GREEN because the publish never takes the local leg at all; unpin BOTH and it REDS at `left: 1`. So the new leg pins the CONJUNCTION and says so, rather than crediting a line that is not load-bearing on its own -- and the third probe is also the first direct evidence that the plane is genuinely wired into the shared path, since removing pico's reasons to decline makes it deliver. The CALIBRATION arm is in the same test rather than beside it: "nothing arrived" is satisfied by a broken subscriber, session or harness alike, so the SAME subscriber then receives a publish from a real peer over the wire. wz-capi-pico full suite green, clippy clean.

All 212 are now defined and the gate reads 0. The instrument is deliberately store-direct on the ARTIFACT rather than on a header -- a header lists what upstream DECLARES, a `.so` lists what it DEFINES, and a linker resolves against the latter. Three things keep this from being a symbol-count exercise. The encoding constants are adjudicated by asking BOTH libraries for each accessor BY NAME and comparing the rendered string, which pins a second transcription -- (accessor name -> id) -- that the existing (string -> id) leg is blind to; a damage probe swapping one id reds exactly that accessor. The clock arithmetic is compared byte-for-byte against upstream's compiled code on inputs straddling the carry boundary, the backwards interval and the sub-second truncation. And the put options plus the delete get a twice-and-diff: one driver compiled against wz's cdylib and against the real library, both run at a real zenoh-pico `z_sub_attachment` whose printout carries encoding, KIND, priority, congestion, express and the attachment -- so the delete is judged by its wire kind rather than by an empty payload, and both damage probes were RUN. The round also retracts a claim it made itself: the two TLS drop-in legs were called unregistered debt, and they are not -- Layer E already builds the cdylib with `transport-link-tls` and its sweep runs them, so the red was the measurement's own configuration.

Round 311y560.decision_summary: R311y560 -- the hosted red that stood for 17 rounds, diagnosed by a controlled pair and fixed in the script that owns the build. `capi-c-arms` had been red since R311y542 with five candidate explanations already excluded and no reproduction here, and the cause turned out to be a single line ~2400 lines above the step it broke: the workflow-wide `CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always` at ci.yml:56. zenoh-c does not compile `opaque-types` in the ordinary sense -- its `get_opaque_type_data!` macro DELIBERATELY panics at const-eval with `'type: X, align: A, size: S'` and the build then PARSES those 97 rustc diagnostics out of stderr to emit `zenoh_opaque.h`. Forced colour wraps every one of them in ANSI escapes, the plain-text-anchored parser matches none, and it fails with "there are 0 errors in the input data, but only 97 of them were processed" -- a message that is literal rather than mysterious once the mechanism is read. Locally cargo auto-disables colour into a pipe, which is why 17 rounds of local runs said nothing. Reading "opaque-types fails to compile" as the defect was the misreading that kept it open. The evidence is three arms, all run: with the variable set the local build fails byte-for-byte as hosted does; with it unset the same command installs cleanly; and with it set against the PATCHED script it installs cleanly. The middle arm is the one that matters, because a reproduction alone was equally consistent with "a scratch-prefix build fails". The fix is `export CARGO_TERM_COLOR=never` inside `scripts/install-zenoh-c-shm.sh` rather than in the workflow, so a lane, a hand-run and any future caller are all covered and the fix travels with the thing it protects; ci.yml keeps a pointer comment so the next reader of line 56 finds the interaction. The round also corrects an asymmetry R311y559 itself shipped: `ze_advanced_publisher_delete` returned an error when no face carried the Del while its sibling `ze_advanced_publisher_put` returns `Z_OK` unconditionally, so a publisher declared before its first peer answered success to a put and failure to a delete. Upstream returns the underlying impl's result from both, so wz's best-effort fan-out is a divergence either way -- it is now ONE named divergence covering both entry points instead of two behaviours. options->source_info, again with a stated reason -- no exported constructor for

Round 311y562.decision_summary:
R311y562 -- the pico/AP metadata planes closed end to end, plus one live
ABI defect that a size check could not have seen. (1) THE AP RECOVERY
RESIDUAL. R311y561 narrowed a recovered sample's loss to encoding +
attachment "only because the ring does not retain those two"; the real
cause was one layer earlier -- AdvancedPublisher::put took a payload and
nothing else, so neither field ever existed to retain. put_with now takes
the two fields upstream's own ze_advanced_publisher_put passes through
(it OVERWRITES timestamp and source_info with the publisher's sequencing
values, advanced_publisher.c:402-407, so those two are deliberately not
parameters), CachedSample retains them, and the recovery reply replays
them. The subscriber half needed no change: its re-apply had been written
at R311y95 and was dead code for ~460 rounds because the reply could not
carry what the ring never kept -- invisible to a reader who checked only
that function. (2) THE SEAM. ReplyOut had grown one method per metadata
COMBINATION (_stamped/_encoded/_attached/_sourced/_del_sourced) and had
run out: nothing carried an attachment ALONGSIDE a timestamp, which is
exactly what both new callers hold. ReplyMeta bundles all four, so the
next field is a struct field rather than a 2^n-th method. (3) THE PICO
REPLY PLANE. z_query_reply_options_t carried encoding and timestamp as
opaque c_void with two stated reasons -- "no exported z_encoding_*" and
"the timestamp family is a follow-up round" -- both expired at R311y529
and R311y557 respectively, the same class y561 named one round earlier in
the file next door. source_info was not a field at all. All three are now
read, and closing the loop needed two things the code review would not
have found: the reply plane's own with_reply_metadata does not share the
sample plane's projection, so it dropped source_info on RECEIVE too, and
the reply-source-info codec gate had to be enabled for this ABI, whose
"OFF = pico-faithful" justification inverts the moment z_query_reply
exposes the field. (4) THE DEFECT. z_get_options_t modelled the
Z_FEATURE_UNSTABLE_API-OFF layout by reading the cmake DEFAULT rather than
the generated config -- the R311y466 trap this crate's own put-options doc
warns about -- while build-zenoh-pico-cli.sh:454 configures the reference
pico with UNSTABLE=ON and its config.h carries a bare #define. The two
missing fields sit BEFORE accept_replies, so the omission did not hide a
tail, it MOVED a field: measured on the reference header accept_replies is
at 72, wz had it at 56, which in the caller's memory is the source_info
POINTER. Every drop-in program calling z_get_options_default read its
reply-keyexpr policy out of the low half of a null pointer. lib.rs pinned
40/32/64 for reply/reply_del/get, i.e. a build nobody links, while the put
plane had modelled UNSTABLE=ON all along -- the crate was pinning two
different pico builds at once. Fixed, and pinned by OFFSET rather than
size, because a size is equally consistent with a harmless missing tail
and with a displaced field.

Round 311y563.decision_summary:
R311y563 -- the two items R311y562 wrote down as "still open" closed in the
round after, which is the point: a carry-forward is a work item, not a
description of the world. (1) THE ZENOH-C source_info FAMILY. Six option
structs on that ABI declared the field and all six carried it as an unread
c_void, with a reason that was accurate and stayed accurate for rounds --
the type was not declared by the crate. What made it stay is that the
zenoh-c shape is NOT the pico shape under another name, so "mirror the
y559 pico work" was the wrong estimate: pico's z_source_info_t is a plain
by-pointer struct filled in place, while zenoh-c's is an OWNED OPAQUE
(z_owned_source_info_t, 32 B at ALIGN 4) whose option fields are
z_moved_source_info_t* the callee CONSUMES and whose read-back needs a
distinct loaned type. So the work is the whole family -- _new / _loan /
_drop / _id / _sn / z_internal_source_info_check / _null -- plus a
z_sample_source_info without which the send half is unfalsifiable. The
alignment shaped the type: a Rust struct with a pointer field is align 8
and repr(align(4)) cannot lower it, so the handle is stored as BYTES and
read with from_ne_bytes; align 4 means a C program may legally place one
at a 4-but-not-8-aligned address, where a pointer field would be an
unaligned load that merely happens to work on x86-64. The reply plane got
its timestamp in the same pass, on the same expired-reason pattern
("accepted and ignored" while z_timestamp_t had shipped at y557), and it
was reachable only because y562 had built the ReplyMeta seam one round
earlier for the pico ABI's identical problem -- the seam paid for itself
in the next round. (2) THE LAYOUT GATE. y562 fixed the z_get_options_t
displacement and pinned the result with const assertions carrying
hand-measured numbers, and said so: still a transcription, the same class
that produced the wrong 40/32/64 pins. This round replaces the KIND of
gate. pico_abi_option_layout.rs generates a C probe, COMPILES it against
the reference build's own generated config.h (first on the include path,
so nothing restates a flag), runs it, and diffs size + field offsets
against wz's own offset_of!. No number in it is typed by a human on
either side. It carries a calibration arm -- the probe must have observed
the UNSTABLE-ON layout -- because a probe that silently compiled against
an unstable-OFF header would agree with an unstable-OFF wz and certify
the very drift it exists to catch.

Round 311y575.decision_summary: R311y575 -- the cancellation-token plane, and the 8-byte struct it was hiding behind. The debt ledger carried `cancellation_token` as ACCEPTED FOR LAYOUT AND NEVER READ on two option structs: wz shipped the token TYPE and no plane, so a C program could build a token, hand it to a get, and receive a query nothing could cancel -- with the call reporting success. Implementing it turned up two defects the residual did not name. The field is a MOVED handle upstream consumes unconditionally, so reading it as an opaque pointer leaked one token per get and left the caller struct non-null, making ownership ambiguous rather than merely leaked. And a THIRD struct carries the same field: `z_liveliness_get_options_t`, which wz declared at 8 B on the reasoning that `Z_FEATURE_UNSTABLE_API` "defaults OFF" -- the R311y466 trap that R311y562 had already paid for once on `z_get_options_t`. Measured against the reference headers the struct is 16 B with the field at offset 8, so the default writer was filling 8 of the 16 bytes a drop-in program allocates and leaving the tail as caller stack where upstream writes NULL. That defect survived the R311y565 mechanical layout gate for one reason: the gate pins the structs its own table names, and this type was not in it. So the fix has two halves, the plane and the table.

The frame: wz decodes as a PARTICIPANT that owns the session it is parsing. Consuming the same decoders as a PASSIVE dissection engine -- reading traffic the reader never joined, from a capture or a tap -- is a different contract, and ten places do not meet it. Registered as G1-G10, top priority, ahead of the zenoh/pico parity line that held the slot since 2026-08-05.

Baseline that makes the gaps readable rather than alarming: message-family coverage vs zenoh 1.5.0 is 100% -- 8 transport + 6 network + 5 zenoh + 2 scouting families (zenoh-ref commons/zenoh-protocol/src/) against 51 generated codecs in out/wz-codecs/ -- and the passive entry points already exist and take bytes only: wz-session-core/src/inbound.rs:234 parse_inbound and wz-session-core/src/network_message.rs:177 parse_frame_payload, network MID 7 of 7 at :185-217.

G1 -- no capture-side input path. wz reads from sockets, never from a capture. pcap / AF_PACKET ingest, TCP flow reassembly into a byte stream, and stream-offset to packet mapping are all absent; nothing under crates/ is a starting point. Largest of the ten.

G2 -- no passive session-context tracker. parse_inbound (inbound.rs:234) takes bytes and nothing else, but the framing is not context-free: a lowlatency session's stream prefix is a 4-byte LE u32 rather than the universal 2-byte form (wz-runtime-tokio/src/stream_link.rs:55-62,107), and compression rewrites the batch body. wz holds every one of these facts (the establishment ext id space is written down at wz-session-core/src/extlowlatency.rs:31-33) but wired into its own live session, not into an observer that infers a flow's parameters from a handshake it merely watched.

G3 -- leaf scalar field spans. Sub-codec spans are already derivable (MEASURED, see verification); what codegen does not emit is a span for a scalar field INSIDE a leaf codec. Flag bits are free -- the carrier byte's span is known and the accessors exist. Two routes, and this is the only item of the ten carrying a real design choice: a span-emitting decode in the SCE Rust template (vendor/sce, upstream) or a consumer-side field walker differentially tested against the wz codec as oracle.

G4 -- the batch parser is not best-effort. An unknown network MID absorbs the rest of the payload and BREAKS the loop (network_message.rs:217-223), and any codec error fails the whole batch. Correct for a participant, for which an unparsable frame is a framing error and a teardown; wrong for an observer, which wants every message it can read plus a typed marker for where it stopped.

G5 -- Fragment First/Drop extensions decoded but not interpreted. zenoh 1.5.0 carries ext_first (0x2) and ext_drop (0x3) on Fragment (zenoh-ref commons/zenoh-protocol/src/transport/fragment.rs:94-97). wz carries them through as generic ext entries, but the reassembler keys only on (peer, reliable, priority) plus SN consecutiveness and the M bit (wz-session-core/src/reassembly_dispatch.rs:168-196). The smallest of the ten, and the only one that is a wz-side defect rather than a missing consumer layer.
G6 -- decoded types are not consumer-shaped. InboundFrame has no Debug and no serde, so anything handing a decode to a view or a log needs a conversion layer.
G7 -- an out-of-workspace feature combination can fail the workspace deny(warnings) policy. The subset matrix CI covers is the workspace's own; a consumer choosing its own combination is outside it.

G8 -- no zenoh-format config emit or validate. WzConfig is deliberately wz's own typed config, positioned against zenoh's stringly JSON5 blob (wz-runtime-tokio/src/config.rs:6-12), so nothing that must author or pre-validate config for a stock zenoh node has a schema in wz to lean on.
G9 -- no raweth (L2) link. Absent from wz entirely; the reference is in-tree and readable at vendor/zenoh-pico/src/link/transport/udp/raweth_unix.c.

G10 -- no TLS/QUIC session-key export. tls_pipeline.rs and quic_pipeline.rs exist but nothing exports key material. Consequence beyond the observer case: wz cannot dogfood its own encrypted transport, which meets the open TLS-written-but-unwitnessed debt from R311y534.

Ordering the evidence supports: G1 and G2 gate the rest, since without input and without context there is nothing to dissect. G4 and G6 are small and unblock consumption at once. G5 is a defect and cheap. G3 carries the design choice. G8, G9 and G10 are independent capability adds, each closable alone.
