New `extfragment` reads the 0x2 First / 0x3 Drop markers and new `extpatch` reads the peer 0x7 patch level wz had emitted since R121f1 and never read -- the level being the SOLE gate on the marker rules, without which honouring them would refuse every patch-0 peer chain. G4 adds a best-effort batch walk that keeps every readable record plus a typed halt (offset + reason) while the strict participant walk is unchanged, both over ONE shared per-MID dispatch. G6 half-closes: `InboundFrame` derives `Debug` (the note forbidding it cited a codegen fact that had stopped being true); serde stays blocked on SCE derive policy in a read-only tree. G7 identifies the root the prior round deliberately left open -- `oam_body` is the only body encoder with no in-module caller, and its cfg omitted the `session-unicast` gate of its sole consumer -- and run-ci Layer C1h now names the combination. G2 adds `passive::PassiveSession`, which folds BOTH sides Init offers, follows the lowlatency 2-to-4-byte reframe AT Established rather than at Init, and refuses to claim a negotiation it did not observe. G1 adds the crate `wz-capture` -- pcap, link/IP/TCP decapsulation, and a flow reassembler repairing retransmission, reordering, overlap and sequence wrap with a stream-offset to packet map -- no_std, zero third-party deps. The end-to-end proof is a pcap built from a REAL tapped wz handshake, not from wz encoders: a tap proves the observer can frame what the LINK LAYER wrote, where a self-built fixture would stay green if the framing rule were wrong in a way the encoder shared. Two of five G5 probes found problems in the TESTS rather than the code, and both were fixed. G3, G6-serde, G8, G9 and G10 remain open and are named as such.
verification_bullets: FIVE damage probes on G5, and TWO of them found real problems rather than confirming the work. (2) removing the `process_event(FragmentDrop)` left the ENTIRE suite green -- the slot-reuse test's claim to prove the FSM arm was an OVERCLAIM, since a stranded `Receiving` and a fresh `Empty` both accept a chunk and both complete on more==0. Replaced with an engine-resting-state assertion that reds under exactly that damage. (3) the supersede fold had no observable discriminator at all, so the two folds were collapsed into ONE `abort_peer_drop` seam and a source-scan test pins the count at 1 (probed: splitting it back reds).

Probe 1 (the marker gate never runs): 6 of 11 chain-boundary tests red, and the 4 that must stay green -- both disarmed arms, the marked-start path, the observer-mirror mapping -- stayed green. Probe 4 (blind the First projector): the wire round trip over wz's OWN emitted fragment reds with "the 0x2 First marker rides fragment 0 and no other".

G5 behavioural discriminators are on BYTES, not on enums: `a_first_marker_discards_the_stranded_prefix` gives the restart a CONSECUTIVE sn, so a Router ignoring the marker delivers AAABBBCCC and only one reading it delivers BBBCCC -- and `without_the_rules_the_restart_merges_into_the_stranded_prefix` pins the wrong answer explicitly so the right one cannot pass for an unrelated reason.

G5 patch negotiation is proven over a REAL loopback handshake (`tests/fragment_markers_e2e.rs`): both peers come out with `patch_was_negotiated() == true` and level 1. The `patch_was_negotiated` assertion is what excludes a defaulted value; probe 5 (drop the negotiation callsite from drive.rs) reds both tests.

G4: 5 tests over OAM fixtures built by the real encoder (the OAM codec is ungated, so the contract is pinned in every codec-frame build). The load-bearing one runs BOTH contracts over the SAME bytes: a truncated trailing record makes the strict walk `Err` -- losing everything -- while the best-effort walk keeps the prefix and reports `CodecError { offset: <the failing record's own header>, NeedMoreBytes }`. Probe 6 (discard the prefix) and probe 7 (halt offset = 0) each red exactly one or two tests.

G6: the Debug tests assert the RENDERING carries decoded field values (`sn: 9`, `reliable: true`) off a real `parse_inbound`, and that two frames differing in one field render differently -- a Debug collapsed to a variant name would pass containment and tell a consumer nothing.

G7: `bash scripts/run-ci.sh --layer C1h` PASSES with subsets 17-18, and probed RED both ways -- reverting only the fn gate reds with E0425, reverting both gates reproduces the ORIGINAL `function oam_body is never used`. 12s lane.

G2 is proven against a TAP, not a fixture: two real wz nodes handshake over loopback TCP through a recording proxy, and the recorded streams are replayed into a `PassiveSession` that has no access to either node. A fixture built from wz's own encoders would prove a round trip and stay green if the framing rule were wrong in a way the encoder shared. Calibration first (>= 4 frames) so the `all(..)` assertions cannot pass vacuously. Probe 9 (always read a 4-byte prefix) reds both e2e tests.

G2 unit tests reach what no wz-to-wz fixture can: a session that negotiates LowLatency on both Inits reframes 2 -> 4 bytes AT Established and NOT at Init, and the same observer reads the Open under the old width and the next frame under the new one with no caller involvement. One-sided offers never reframe; a mid-session attach with no Inits does not claim a negotiation; a repeated Init on one direction does not complete the fold.

An earlier version of the oversize-prefix test asserted on the 2-byte path, where the guard is UNREACHABLE by construction (a u16 cannot exceed the u16 cap). The test name said otherwise. Rewritten onto the only reachable path -- a reframed lowlatency stream -- where it also pins that the desync is PER-DIRECTION.

G1: `cargo test -p wz-capture` = 25 tests. The pcap writer's file header is asserted BYTE BY BYTE against pcap-savefile(5), not against the reader, so the round trip cannot prove only that the two halves agree with each other. Byte-swapped files, both nanosecond magics, pcapng-by-name, snaplen flagging, and every truncation index are covered. Ethernet PADDING is pinned as not-payload (the IP total-length bound), TCP options are skipped by the data offset, and all six link types reach the IDENTICAL segment.

G1 + G2 together, end to end (`tests/pcap_dissect_e2e.rs`): a pcap built from a REAL tapped handshake -- with a three-way handshake, a byte-identical RETRANSMISSION, and a REORDERED pair -- dissects to the two tapped byte streams EXACTLY, reaches Established, and attributes every decoded message to a packet index. Probe 10 (append duplicates) and probe 11 (append in arrival order) each red it.

C2 clippy (`cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` minus the four unification excludes, `-D warnings`) is clean after every commit; `cargo fmt --all --check` clean. `cargo test -p wz-session-core --lib` 260 default / 333 with the codec+reassembly union; `cargo test -p wz-runtime-tokio` full, no failures.

NOT DONE, and named rather than implied: G3 (leaf scalar field spans) carries a design choice that was not made this round; G6's serde half is blocked on SCE's derive policy in a read-only tree; G8 (zenoh JSON5 config emit), G9 (raweth link) and G10 (TLS/QUIC key export) are untouched. HOSTED CI for this round is UNREAD.

carry_forward_bullets: R311y578a corrects R311y578's body on ONE point: that entry lists G10 among the untouched, and G10 is now CLOSED. Frozen-ledger, so the correction is this entry rather than an edit. The running score is SEVEN of ten closed -- G1, G2, G4, G5, G6-Debug, G7, G10 -- and THREE open: G3, G6-serde, G8, G9.

G10 also meets the standing R311y534 debt (TLS written but unwitnessed) as far as a key log can: wz now exports what an external dissector needs. It does NOT decrypt, and no entry should later read this as though it did.

NEXT: G9 (raweth L2 link) has an in-tree reference at vendor/zenoh-pico/src/link/transport/udp/raweth_unix.c. G8 (zenoh JSON5 config emit / validate) is an independent capability add. G3 is the one with a real design choice, and the choice is now FORCED rather than open -- vendor/sce is read-only from wz sessions, so the SCE-template route is unavailable here and a consumer-side field walker differentially tested against the wz codec is the only route left. Make that explicit before budgeting it.
LOCAL: sits atop `cb690a4b`. Six code commits plus two ledger commits on top of `e8af0d92`. Nothing pushed; hosted CI unread.
changes_bullets: New `wz-runtime-tokio/src/tls_keylog.rs` + the `transport-link-tls-keylog` feature (OFF by default). `key_log()` returns a rustls `KeyLogFile` in a build that selected the feature and `NoKeyLog` otherwise, so the four config builders install it UNCONDITIONALLY and the two builds differ in behaviour rather than in control flow -- a `#[cfg]` at each builder would be four places to forget.
Installed on all four rustls configs: `tls_config::{client_config_from_pem, server_config_from_pem}` and `quic_config::{quic_client_config_from_pem, quic_server_config_from_pem}`.

Arming takes BOTH conditions and neither alone: the cargo feature (so a production build does not contain the capability at all) AND `SSLKEYLOGFILE` naming a destination (which rustls reads itself, so wz never parses or stores the path). `keylog_supported()` / `keylog_armed()` expose the two separately, because an operator asking why a key log is empty needs to tell a feature-less build from an unset variable and the two look identical from outside.
Round 311y578a.decision_summary: R311y578a -- closes G10 (TLS / QUIC session-key export) and CORRECTS R311y578, whose frozen body lists G10 among the untouched. wz writes TLS and QUIC but could never witness one: every other transport is readable off a capture and an encrypted one is ciphertext to all of it, which is the standing R311y534 debt. New `tls_keylog` installs an NSS-format key-log sink on all four rustls config builders, armed only when the `transport-link-tls-keylog` feature is compiled in AND `SSLKEYLOGFILE` names a destination -- never by either alone, because exporting session keys makes the traffic readable to whoever holds the file and a runtime-only switch would ship that capability into every binary. Proven over a real wz-to-wz loopback TLS session driven through the PRODUCTION PEM builders: all four TLS 1.3 labels present in NSS format, and each secret logged TWICE with EQUAL values because both ends ran through wz own builders -- which is what makes them the keys to that session rather than well-formed hex. A negative arm in the same binary runs a second real handshake with the variable removed and exports nothing. Decryption is NOT implemented and is not claimed. Score: seven of ten closed, three open (G3, G6-serde, G8, G9).
verification_bullets: `tests/tls_keylog_e2e.rs` drives a REAL wz-to-wz session to Established over loopback TLS through the PRODUCTION PEM builders -- a hand-built rustls config would prove nothing about wz's own path -- and reads the exported file back.

Format asserted against the NSS key-log spec Wireshark's `tls.keylog_file` consumes: all four TLS 1.3 labels present, three whitespace-separated fields, a 64-hex-char client random, a 64- or 96-hex-char secret, lowercase hex throughout.

The assertion that makes them the keys to THIS session rather than plausible hex: BOTH ends ran through wz's builders, so each of the four secrets is logged TWICE -- once per peer -- and the two values must be EQUAL. One client random across the whole file.

NEGATIVE arm in the same binary: the same build, the same builders and a second real handshake with `SSLKEYLOGFILE` REMOVED export nothing, and the earlier log does not grow. Without it the export could have been unconditional, which is the failure the two-condition design exists to prevent. The disarmed session still reaches Established, so the gate does not break TLS.

Probe 12: replacing `config.key_log = key_log()` with a discard in BOTH tls_config builders reds the test at "the handshake exported nothing; the sink is not installed on the production builders". Restored green.
Its own test binary: `SSLKEYLOGFILE` is process-global and rustls samples it once per `KeyLogFile`, so a sibling test in the same process would race it or silently inherit it.

C2 clippy clean, plus the two feature arms (`transport-link-tls,transport-link-tls-keylog` and `transport-link-quic,transport-link-tls-keylog`) linted explicitly -- a feature the workspace lane never selects is a feature the workspace lane never lints.

NOT closed by this entry: decrypting the exported session is NOT implemented and is not claimed. The deliverable is the standard key-log FILE, which an external TLS-aware dissector consumes; a wz-side TLS record layer + HKDF is a separate piece of work.

carry_forward_bullets: G1-G10 ARE ALL CLOSED. The three that were open at R311y578a -- G3, G6-serde, G8, G9 -- are closed here. No gap in that register remains, and the G6-serde half that R311y578 called "BLOCKED on SCE" was blocked only for the codegen'd mirrors: the view model is where serde CAN land, and it is wz's own type.

DEBT THIS ROUND CREATED, registered here so it is not discovered later. (1) The `dissect` walkers are a hand-written mirror of generated decodes; the differential gate is what keeps them honest, so a codec regeneration MUST run Layer C1bn, not just Layer B2. (2) `Declare`'s nine sub-MIDs are walked, but no walker exists for the SCOUTING messages (Scout / Hello) -- they are on a different MID space the batch walk never reaches. (3) The `zenoh_config` emit covers the topology-and-transport subset only; routing / plugins / storages are omitted on purpose and a caller needing them still hand-writes JSON5. (4) `ZenohNodeConfig::validate` does not check that a `connect` endpoint is REACHABLE, only that it is well-formed. (5) raweth has no session-level wiring: the link sends and receives frames, but nothing hands a zenoh batch to it -- there is no `open_session` over `reth/`, and pico's keyexpr-to-MAC `mapping` config is deliberately unparsed.

G9's raweth is UNPROVEN against a running pico: this tree's pico build pins `Z_FEATURE_RAWETH_TRANSPORT` to 0, so `libzenohpico` has no raweth code to drive. Rebuilding pico with the feature on is the route to a real cross-impl leg, and until then the header-layout oracle is the whole of the proof. Do not read the byte match as an interop result.
NEXT: with G1-G10 closed, the priority reverts to the zenoh/pico parity + AP-full line. Note that R311y575 refuted the "the pico axis closed at y572" reading, so re-measure rather than inherit.

LOCAL: four commits on top of `933f0ef5` -- `0456f8c1` (dissect), `38c6991b` (zenoh-config), `765c5676` (raweth), `57ec0217` (Layer C1bn). Nothing pushed; hosted CI unread for all four, and for `933f0ef5` before them.
changes_bullets: G3 -- new `wz-session-core/src/dissect.rs` + the `dissect` feature: a `SpanCursor` that OWNS the generated codecs' own `SceCursor`, so the walker and the codec cannot disagree about how wide a VLE is (it is not a second VLE implementation). Walkers for the 7 network MIDs, the 5 zenoh bodies, the 9 DECLARE sub-MIDs, the shared leaves (Wireexpr / ExtEntry / Timestamp / Encoding) and the 7 transport messages, plus a best-effort batch walk mirroring `parse_frame_payload_best_effort`.

G3 -- the SCE-template route was FORCED shut, not weighed: `vendor/sce` is read-only from wz sessions, so a span-emitting `decode_spans` cannot be authored, tested or pinned from here. What makes the hand-written mirror safe is the differential gate, not care.

G3 -- `dissect` selects the WHOLE `codec-*` MID space rather than composing a subset. A build that can DECODE a MID but not DISSECT it would be a coverage hole in the layer whose job is coverage; a gate asserts the two MID sets are equal by driving both walkers over all 32 MIDs.

G6-serde -- `Field` / `Span` / `FieldValue` / `BatchDissection` are wz's OWN types, so they take the derives the codegen'd `*Owned` mirrors cannot: `Debug` + `Clone` + `PartialEq` always, `serde::Serialize` + `Deserialize` under `dissect-serde`, and `to_json` with NO serde dependency at all. `Field.name` is a `Cow<'static, str>` precisely so `Deserialize` derives -- `&'static str` has no borrow from `'de` -- while the producing path still hands in a `&'static str` and allocates nothing.

G6-serde -- `CodecError` maps to a stable variant NAME, not a discriminant, through a hand-written `serde(with)` module: the enum is `sce_forge_runtime`'s, carries no serde feature, is read-only here, and is `#[non_exhaustive]`, so a variant inserted upstream serializes as "Unrecognised" rather than silently renumbering a persisted dissection into an existing one.

G8 -- new `wz-runtime-tokio/src/zenoh_config.rs` + `zenoh-config-emit`: `ZenohNodeConfig::to_json5` renders mode / connect / listen / scouting / timestamping / transport / adminspace at the key paths read out of the reference's own `DEFAULT_CONFIG.json5`, and `from_wz` carries wz's negotiated batch_size / lease / max_links / qos onto the stock node.

G8 -- `validate` reports 8 typed defects before anything starts, including the two that are ZENOH's own enforced rules rather than wz opinions (an unknown link protocol; qos + lowlatency), and `Unreachable`, which zenoh does NOT enforce -- a node with nothing to connect to, nothing listening and scouting off starts cleanly and is alone forever.

G9 -- new `wz-session-core/src/raweth_link.rs` + `transport-link-raweth`: the 16 / 20-byte header zenoh-pico's raweth transport builds as a C struct and memcpys onto the wire. NOT a standard Ethernet header (14 bytes): pico appends its own explicit `data_length` after the ethertype, and inserts vlan_type + tag before it in the tagged form.

G9 -- byte order is deliberately NON-uniform and reproduced rather than tidied: `ethtype` / `vlan_type` / `tag` ride the HOST's order because pico memcpys the struct, while `data_length` alone goes through htons. `_ZP_ETH_TYPE_VLAN` is spelled `0x0081` for exactly that reason. An encoder that made both big-endian passes every size and offset check and no pico decodes it.

G9 -- new `wz-runtime-tokio/src/raweth_socket.rs`: `AF_PACKET` + `SIOCGIFINDEX` + `sockaddr_ll` bind behind a `RawEthIo` trait. The seam is not a test indirection -- a DPDK / XDP / TSN embedder or an MCU MAC peripheral has the same shape and no AF_PACKET -- but it is what makes the framing, the whitelist and the send/receive path drivable without `CAP_NET_RAW`. The interface-name length check runs BEFORE the socket, which is both cheaper and the only way it is reachable unprivileged.

G9 -- divergence from pico, deliberate: an interface name that does not fit IFNAMSIZ is REJECTED. pico's `strncpy(.., strlen(interface))` copies an unterminated name into the ioctl, which reads a different interface's index.

New Layer C1bn runs the whole R311y578/y578a/y579 feature set -- `wz-capture`, `dissect`, `dissect-serde`, `transport-link-raweth` on both crates, `zenoh-config-emit` -- and lints `transport-link-tls-keylog`'s own two arms. This closes R311y578's registered debt that `wz-capture` and `transport-link-tls-keylog` were in no lane at all.
Round 311y579.decision_summary: R311y579 -- closes the LAST THREE of the ten passive-dissection gaps: G3 (leaf scalar field spans), G6-serde, G8 (stock-zenoh JSON5 config emit + topology validation) and G9 (the raweth L2 link). G1-G10 are now all closed. G3 is a SpanCursor that owns the generated codecs' own SceCursor and a walker per message, kept honest not by care but by a differential gate that drives walker and codec over the same bytes and rejects any disagreement in consumed bytes, values, or whether the leaf spans tile the consumed range -- the SCE-template alternative was forced shut, since vendor/sce is read-only here. G6-serde lands on the wz-OWNED view model, which is where it can land: Field derives serde under dissect-serde and also renders JSON with no serde dependency at all, because the measured G6 failure was a consumer that could not get a decode into a log. G8 is judged by a REAL zenohd echoing every emitted value back in its resolved-config line, with both validator defects measured against that same zenohd refusing to run. G9 reproduces zenoh-pico's non-standard 16/20-byte header including its non-uniform byte order, proven byte-for-byte against pico's own structs compiled from vendor, and puts AF_PACKET behind a RawEthIo seam so the link runs end to end without CAP_NET_RAW. New Layer C1bn runs the whole feature set, closing y578's debt that wz-capture and transport-link-tls-keylog were in no lane.
verification_bullets: G3 DIFFERENTIAL GATE (22 tests, `dissect::`): every walker is driven against the GENERATED codec over the same bytes and must agree on (a) the byte count consumed, (b) the values, and (c) whether the leaf spans TILE the consumed range with no gap and no overlap. Sub-codec spans additionally RE-DECODE standalone consuming exactly their own width, which a span that merely starts in the right place fails.

G3 PROBE 1 (payload_len VLE -> u8) PASSED GREEN on the first attempt, and that was a defect in the FIXTURES, not in the code: every value in them was below 128, where a VLE is one byte and indistinguishable from a fixed byte. Fixtures were rebuilt across the continuation boundary (a 200-byte payload, a 130-byte keyexpr suffix, 150-byte query parameters, a 1e6 frame sn) and the same probe then reds at "the walker consumed 224 bytes, the codec 225".

G3 PROBE 2 (drop the Oam arm from `walk_network_record`) reds the MID-set gate at "the decoder knows [25..31] but the dissector knows [25..30]". PROBE 3 (shift every raw-bytes span one byte left, values and totals unchanged) reds EIGHT tests on the tiling alone -- the property neither the values nor the byte count can see. PROBE 4 (invert OPEN's cookie gate) reds at "the leaves end at 4 but the message ends at 7". All four restored green.
G3 -- the VLE width itself is anchored OUTSIDE both implementations by a hand-typed `[0x80, 0x01]` = 128, so the one primitive the walker and the codec share is not self-certified.

G6-serde -- the round trip goes through a REAL format (`serde_json`), not just a derive that compiled: a `Field` tree and a halted `BatchDissection` both serialize and read back EQUAL, the latter exercising the hand-written `CodecError` mapping in both directions. The no-serde arm asserts the JSON emit separately, so a build without the feature does not read as though the serde half had been checked.

G8 ORACLE: a REAL zenohd 1.5.0 is started on an emitted config and NOTHING else (no `-l`, no `--cfg`), and its own `Initial conf:` line -- the config AFTER zenoh's parser resolved it -- must carry every emitted value. Discriminating by construction: a key emitted at the WRONG path is not a parse error in zenoh, it is ignored, and the resolved line then shows zenoh's DEFAULT. Every fixture value is deliberately non-default (batch_size 4096 vs 65535, lease 8000 vs 10000, max_links 3 vs 1, qos off vs on, compression on vs off). Then `wait_for_tcp_accept_alive` proves parsed is also APPLIED.
G8 PROBE: expecting `batch_size 4097` instead of 4096 reds the lane, and zenohd's echoed line shows it tracking wz's emitted value -- so the test reads the router, not a cached string.

G8 NEGATIVE ARM, measured BEFORE the rules were written: zenohd exits on an unknown link protocol ("Unicast not supported for carrier-pigeon protocol at io/zenoh-link/src/lib.rs:183") and on qos + lowlatency ("'qos' and 'lowlatency' options are incompatible at io/zenoh-transport/src/unicast/manager.rs:265"). A positive control on the same shape comes up first, so an exit is evidence about the defect and not about the harness.

G8 -- the harness first failed for a reason worth recording: zenoh dispatches its config parser on the FILE EXTENSION and panics on a file without one (commons/zenoh-config/src/lib.rs:1286), before reading a byte. Now documented on `to_json5` itself, since nothing about the emitted content could hint at it.

G9 ORACLE: a C probe compiled against `vendor/zenoh-pico`'s REAL `raweth.h` reports sizeof / offsetof for both header structs and hex-dumps a header pico's own struct filled in. wz matches on all of it: 16 / 20 widths, offsets 12 / 14, `_ZP_ETH_TYPE_VLAN` = 129, `_ZP_MAX_ETH_FRAME_SIZE` = 1514, and the BYTES -- `010203040506 111213141516 e072 0003` plain, `... 8100 0201 e072 0003` tagged.
G9 PROBE: encoding `ethtype` big-endian instead of native leaves the SIZE/OFFSET test green and reds the BYTE test. That is the whole reason the byte compare exists, demonstrated rather than argued.

G9 -- the probe forces `Z_FEATURE_RAWETH_TRANSPORT` on AFTER pico's config.h, because THIS tree's pico build pins it to 0. Consequence recorded rather than papered over: there is no runtime pico raweth leg available here, since the built `libzenohpico` carries no raweth code. The header is compiled, not linked.

G9 -- the link itself is driven END TO END without privileges: two `RawEthLink`s over a `UnixDatagram` pair exchange real frames both directions, a whitelist rejects a foreign source AND admits the named one (positive control on a second pair), a VLAN-tagged sender reaches an UNTAGGED reader (the width is read off the frame, not off local config), and a 4-byte garbage datagram is reported `Malformed(Truncated{got:4,need:16})` rather than read past.
G9 -- `deframe` cuts to `data_length`, not to the end of the frame, proven on a 60-byte NIC-padded frame carrying 3 payload bytes: 41 pad bytes must not reach the batch decoder.

G9 -- the AF_PACKET open is checked by AGREEMENT with the kernel: the test asks for a raw packet socket by hand and requires wz's answer to match -- PermissionDenied where the kernel refuses, a socket where it does not. That has content on this unprivileged host (it catches a failure for the wrong reason) and becomes the full open path under CAP_NET_RAW. A frame leaving a real NIC is NOT proven and is not claimed.

LANES RUN BY HAND: C0 pass (13s, 0 expired blockers), C1 pass (83s), C2 pass (17s), C1bf pass (35s), C1bn pass (25s). C1bn's own guard probed: pointing it at a non-existent filter reds at "the dissect filter matched no test".

The `portability` job passed on macOS and Windows for hundreds of rounds while two defects sat in code it compiled every time. Ask of any gate: what would it do if the thing under it were broken in the ordinary way?

A FAILING STEP ABORTS THE STEPS AFTER IT. `feature-gates` runs each lane as its own step, so the reported lane is the FIRST failure, never the only one. C1y hid behind C1w, and fifteen lanes hid behind C1y for four rounds. When a job reds, the correct question is not "what failed" but "what did not get to run".

DO NOT SWEEP LANES WHILE COMMITTING. A local lane sweep and a git hook both drive cargo against `crates/target`; concurrent writers produce vanishing-object-file errors that look exactly like lane defects. Two lanes were mis-diagnosed as broken this round for that reason. Run the sweep alone, and read `crates/target/run-ci-logs/` rather than assuming the evidence is gone.

A PARTICIPANT DECODER AND AN OBSERVER DECODER FAIL DIFFERENTLY. Six of the seven tier-A items are the same shape: wz decodes traffic it negotiated, so bounds that a peer never exceeds, context it already holds, and tables it built itself were all free. changes_bullets: REGISTER, tier A (blocks the first delivery phase). A1 -- the generated codecs cap their extension chain and REJECT past it. `sources/codecs/msg_put.scxml:113` declares `max-depth="4" on-overflow="reject"`; measured across the emitted codecs the caps are msg_put 4, msg_del 4, reply 4, err 4, push 4, request 4, response 4, declare 4, interest 4, query 8, and overflow is `CodecError::TooManyElements` (`out/wz-codecs/linkstate.rs:118`). A Put carrying five extensions therefore fails to decode ENTIRELY, which is the exact opposite of the analyzer requirement that an unknown extension be a display target rather than a parse failure (`wire-spec-subset--watching-zenoh-mvp/7-2-unknown-extensions-policy`). The wz participant never hit this because it talks to peers that send what it expects; an observer of arbitrary traffic is the first consumer that can.

REGISTER, tier A. A2 -- `PassiveSession` stops at TRANSPORT frames. `passive.rs:348 next_frame()` yields an `InboundFrame` and nothing else: it does not run `parse_frame_payload` on a Frame body, does not drive a `ReassemblyDispatcher` over observed Fragments, and does not decompress a batch although `FlowContext::compression_active()` (`passive.rs:196`) computes the answer. Every part exists; none is wired on the passive side, so each consumer re-does the same three connections.

REGISTER, tier A. A3 -- `wz-capture` decapsulates TCP ONLY. `wz-capture/src/link.rs:151` returns `SkipReason::NotTcp(proto)` for everything else, so UDP is skipped by name -- and UDP is where multicast scouting, Hello/Scout, Join, and the UDP unicast link live. The named skip is the right shape; the hole is real.

REGISTER, tier A. A4 -- there is no PASSIVE keyexpr mapping table. `wireexpr_resolve.rs:1-13` is the PARTICIPANT-side resolver over a peer table the session owns. An observer needs a per-session, per-DIRECTION id -> keyexpr table rebuilt from the observed Declare / Undeclare stream, and `passive.rs` contains no reference to Declare or keyexpr at all.

REGISTER, tier A. A5 -- `FlowContext` carries four of the six negotiated values. `passive.rs:123-151` has lowlatency, compression, qos, patch (plus auth / shm / multilink offered flags) and is MISSING `resolution` and `batch_size`.

REGISTER, tier A. A6 -- no walker for the SCOUTING messages. `dissect.rs` exposes 20 walkers covering transport, network and zenoh payload; Scout and Hello live on a MID space the batch walk never reaches, so a dissection of a scouting datagram has no field spans.

REGISTER, tier A. A7 -- no C ABI over the dissection surface. `wz-capi-c` is a zenoh-c drop-in, i.e. the PARTICIPANT API; a grep for dissect / passive / capture across `wz-capi-c/src` returns zero. A [REDACTED]/C++ consumer can drive wz as an active node today and cannot call the decode core at all.

REGISTER, tier B (needed for the second delivery phase, or for operation). B1 -- no LIVE capture source. `wz-capture` ingests capture FILES; the seam is deliberately "a byte stream plus a direction" (`wz-capture/Cargo.toml:11`). The kernel half already exists elsewhere in the tree: `wz-runtime-tokio/src/raweth_socket.rs:93-95` opens `socket(AF_PACKET, SOCK_RAW, ETH_P_ALL)` and binds it to an interface for the raweth transport. What is missing is a feed loop into `Dissection::push_packet`, not a subsystem.

REGISTER, tier B. B2 -- pcapng is unread. `wz-capture/src/pcap.rs:21-24` recognises the Section Header Block only to return `PcapError::LooksLikePcapNg`. Diagnosing by name rather than misparsing is correct; pcapng remains the commonest modern capture format.

REGISTER, tier B. B3 -- IPv6 extension chains, IP fragments and checksums are unhandled. `link.rs:131-136` names `Ipv4Fragment` and `Ipv6ExtensionChain(u8)` as skips, and no IP or TCP checksum is verified anywhere, so a corrupt-but-plausible packet reassembles as though it were good.

REGISTER, tier B. B4 -- raweth has FRAMING but no session. `raweth_link.rs:75` defines `RAWETH_SCHEMA = "reth"` and no other site in the tree references that scheme: nothing opens a session over it. Compounding it, this tree's pico build pins `Z_FEATURE_RAWETH_TRANSPORT=0`, so the layout-and-bytes oracle is the whole of the proof and must not be read as an interop result.

REGISTER, tier B. B5 -- multicast runs with the fragment chain-boundary rules OFF. `multicast_dispatch.rs:1403` passes `FragmentMarkers::NONE` because a Join advertises no `0x7` patch extension and there is no per-peer Init to take a `min()` over. Upstream gates the same block on the same predicate but sources it from manager CONFIG (`io/zenoh-transport/src/multicast/rx.rs:216`); wiring that source is the closing condition.

REGISTER, tier B. B6 -- a desynchronised direction is abandoned with no resync attempt. `PassiveStall::Desynchronised` (`passive.rs:288`) is terminal for that stream. Correct while nothing in the framing permits resynchronisation, but a reader that attached mid-frame is exactly the ordinary case for a capture, and a heuristic rescan is the obvious follow-up.

CORRECTION to `[REDACTED]` section 2.2, which states that `resolution` fixes the SN field WIDTH at 8/16/32/64 bit and that a parser which does not know it "reads the Frame SN wrongly". Measured on both sides: wz writes and reads the Frame `sn` as VLE (`sources/codecs/frame.scxml:38` `sce:bit-size="vle"` -> `out/wz-codecs/frame.rs:57` `read_vle_u64()`), and zenoh writes it through the same zint path (`commons/zenoh-codec/src/transport/frame.rs:54` -> `core/zint.rs:173 uint_impl!`). `resolution` sets the wraparound MASK (`core/resolution.rs mask()`), not the field width. Parsing does not break without it; SN-GAP LOSS TRACKING does, because a wrap and a gap are indistinguishable without the modulus. That is why A5 names `resolution` as debt even though A5's own consequence is narrower than the brief claimed.

CORRECTION to the same brief, section 3(a), which recommends building the capture dissector on `StreamEnvelope` as "a resumable stream reassembler". `out/wz-codecs/stream_envelope.rs:26` declares `payload_len: u16` -- a FIXED two-byte prefix. A session that negotiated LowLatency reframes to a four-byte LE u32 prefix once Established (`passive.rs:57-64`), which `StreamEnvelope` cannot express, and one wrong boundary invalidates every later boundary in that direction. The correct base is `passive.rs`, which records the width per frame (`PassiveFrame.prefix_width`, `passive.rs:270`).

SCOPE NOTE recorded so a later round does not re-derive it. Of the analyzer requirements, six are OUTSIDE wz by design and are not registered here: the viewer and the authoring canvas (GUI), reporting, timing control, the payload sub-decoder plugin slot, and process orchestration. Aggregation layers -- Query/Reply RTT correlation, per-keyexpr throughput and traffic share -- are likewise consumer-side; `stats.rs` counts wz's OWN sessions and is not a passive aggregator.
Round 311y582.decision_summary: R311y582 -- registers, as ONE debt tier list, everything wz itself must gain before it can serve as the decode engine of a passive zenoh analyzer, measured against that project's [REDACTED] rather than against wz's own roadmap. Thirteen items: seven tier A that block the first delivery phase, six tier B that are second-phase or operational. Six of the seven tier-A items are the SAME shape -- wz decodes traffic it negotiated, so extension bounds a peer never exceeds, negotiated context it already holds, and keyexpr tables it built itself were all free, and none of them is free for a reader of traffic it never joined. The sharpest is that the generated codecs cap the extension chain at four (query eight) and REJECT past it, so a Put carrying five extensions fails to decode entirely -- the exact inverse of the requirement that an unknown extension be displayed rather than fail. Two claims in the analyzer's own capture-view brief were also measured and are WRONG, and both were corrected here rather than inherited: `resolution` does not set the SN field width (it is VLE on both sides; resolution is the wraparound mask, which matters for SN-gap loss tracking and not for parsing), and `StreamEnvelope` cannot be the dissector's base because its prefix is a fixed u16 while a LowLatency session reframes to u32. No code changed this round.
verification_bullets: This round REGISTERS and measures; it changes no code, so the verification is the measurement itself. Every claim above was read out of the tree in this session, never quoted from a note -- the External-references rule that R311y339 was written for.

The extension caps were counted per codec rather than sampled: msg_put / msg_del / reply / err / push / request / response / declare / interest all declare `HeaplessVec<ExtEntry<'a>, 4>` and query declares 8. The reject path was read at `out/wz-codecs/linkstate.rs:118` (`.map_err(|_| CodecError::TooManyElements)`), so overflow is a hard decode failure and not a truncation.

The SSOT for that cap was located, so the fix is bounded rather than speculative: `max-depth="4" on-overflow="reject"` is an `sce:tlv-chain` attribute in `sources/codecs/msg_put.scxml:113`, i.e. a declared codegen parameter, not a hand-written constant in the emit.

The SN-width correction was measured on BOTH sides before being written down. wz: `sources/codecs/frame.scxml:38` then the emitted `out/wz-codecs/frame.rs:57`. zenoh 1.5.0: `commons/zenoh-codec/src/transport/frame.rs:54` writes `sn` through the generic integer codec, and `commons/zenoh-codec/src/core/zint.rs:173`'s `uint_impl!` macro is what routes u32 to the u64 zint. A one-sided read would have proved only that wz is self-consistent.

The `StreamEnvelope` correction was measured against the prefix widths the passive tracker actually uses: `PREFIX_WIDTH_UNIVERSAL = 2` and `PREFIX_WIDTH_LOWLATENCY = 4` (`passive.rs:57-64`) versus `payload_len: u16` (`out/wz-codecs/stream_envelope.rs:26`).

The absence claims were established by grep over the tree rather than inferred from a module's name, which is the shape `feedback_an_absence_reading_is_a_cwd_claim` exists for. `RAWETH_SCHEMA = "reth"` has exactly one occurrence in the whole of `crates/` (its definition). `dissect` / `passive` / `capture` have zero occurrences under `wz-capi-c/src`. `AF_PACKET` occurs only in `raweth_socket.rs` and in `wz-capture`'s own Cargo.toml comment naming it as future work.

changes_bullets: CORRECTS R311y582's A1, which is frozen and stays as written. That entry says a chain past the cap "fails to decode ENTIRELY" with `CodecError::TooManyElements`. Measured, it does neither. The emit is `for _ in 0..MAX` pushing into a `HeaplessVec<_, MAX>`, so `TooManyElements` is UNREACHABLE, and the generator drops the `on-overflow="reject"` check on the entry-flag path -- so the loop exits on the FOR bound with the last entry's Z still set and the next field is read from chain bytes. `MsgPut::decode` returns Ok with `payload = [0x03, 0xAA, 0xBB]` where the wire held `[0xAA, 0xBB, 0xCC]`. The y582 claim came from reading `linkstate.rs:118`, which is a REPEAT construct with a separate count where the cap IS reachable, and generalising it to the ext chain. Two different constructs; only one of them errors.

The failure is INPUT-DEPENDENT, which is why a casual probe reports "it errors" and moves on. The fixture's terminating extension carries id 3 so its header byte is `0x03` -- a valid one-byte VLE that fits the bytes left. Give it id 5 and the misread asks for five bytes, four remain, and the decode fails loudly. Whether this defect is visible is a property of the peer's bytes.

NEW RULE, stated once: `ext_chain::chain_saturated(decoded, capacity, last_says_continue)`. Everything else asks it. `check_chain<const N>` is generic over the container's own capacity rather than over a restated constant, so a `max-depth` change moves the check with it and cannot leave a stale number behind.

PARTICIPANT PATH closed at `network_message::decode_one_record`, the single MID-dispatch SSOT: `check_push` / `check_request` / `check_response` / `check_declare` walk the nested zenoh-payload bodies too, because the INNER chain is the one that costs a payload. `ext_chain` is the single place that knows WHERE the chains are, so when SCE lands the generator fix this deletes in one edit instead of being hunted across the dispatch.

OBSERVER PATH closed at `dissect::walk_ext_chain_z`, which now refuses. This is the ONE place the hand-written walker deliberately does not mirror the generated decode, and it is documented as such at the site: a dissector that reproduced a silent misparse would draw a confident wrong tree, which is the single thing a dissector must never do. The divergence is bounded to saturating input, which no `agree` fixture contains, so the differential gate keeps its teeth on everything else.

CENSUS GAP FOUND AND CLOSED. R311y582 enumerated twelve messages with ext chains. carry_forward_bullets: THE ORDER IN R311y582 WAS NOT QUITE RIGHT, and the correction is cheap to state: A2 depends on A5. Fragment reassembly needs the SN ring mask, the mask is the negotiated resolution, and the resolution was A5. Half of A5 therefore landed inside A2. What is LEFT of A5 is `batch_size`: it is stored on `FlowContext` and nothing reads it, so a consumer that wants to bound a batch or flag an oversize one still does that itself.

NEXT: A4 (the passive keyexpr table) is now the sharpest remaining tier-A item, because A2 made the network records reachable and every one of them carries a `WireExpr` that is a NUMBER until a Declare stream resolves it. A6 (Scout / Hello walkers) rose in value too: A3 means scouting datagrams now arrive, and they decode as an unknown MID.

A NAMED SKIP IS HONEST ABOUT THE HOLE AND SILENT ABOUT ITS SIZE. `SkipReason::NotTcp` said, correctly, that a packet produced nothing. What it did not say is that everything multicast and everything scouting went through that one arm. When a skip reason names a NEGATIVE ("not TCP"), ask what set it actually covers before reading the dissection as complete.

ASK WHETHER A NEW TRANSPORT IS A BRANCH OR A FRAMING. UDP looked like one `match` arm and was a second framing mode with its own entry point, its own flow type and no reassembly at all. The tell was in the participant-side code the whole time (`udp_pipeline.rs:34-36`).

NOT PUSHED. Local commits `4007b45b` (A2) and `419269de` (A3) sit on `61d88f99`. Hosted has not seen the A1 regeneration either — `49cce01c` touched every entry-flag codec, so the first hosted run after this arc is the one that matters.
changes_bullets: A2 — `PassiveFrame` gains `carried`, and the tracker stops handing back a transport frame the consumer has to finish itself. A `Frame` body is decompressed when the observed session negotiated `Compression`, then walked best-effort into network records; a `Fragment` is driven through a chain router; a completed chain is walked the same way.

A2 — `Carried` names every non-batch outcome instead of collapsing to an empty batch: `Undecompressible` (lz4 refused it, or this build has no `transport-compression`), `Fragment(IngestOutcome)` (chain opened / continued / refused / aborted, which is exactly what a loss view wants), `Reassembled`, `FragmentWithoutResolution`, `Nothing`. "Carried nothing" and "carried something I could not read, and here is why" are different answers on a dissector's screen.

A2 — one chain router PER DIRECTION, keyed by the direction itself. A participant keys chains by peer zid because it faces many peers through one router; an observer faces exactly two half-sessions and may never learn either zid, so the split is structural rather than a lookup.

A5 (the half A2 needed) — `FlowContext::caps` and `sn_mask()`. Fragment reassembly compares SNs on a ring, and the ring is the negotiated `seq_num_res`, which `FlowContext` did not carry. So A2 could not be done without it.

A5 — the caps are ASSIGNED from the InitAck, not folded across both Inits. zenoh requires every InitAck size parameter to be less than or equal to the InitSyn's and rejects a peer that enlarges one (`peer_init_caps::init_ack_exceeds_advertisement`), so the acceptor's answer IS the session value. An observer has the `is_ack` bit that tells the two apart — the one thing a `&=` fold would throw away. Decoded through the existing `PeerInitCaps::from_init_body` rather than by re-splitting the packed `sn_res` byte a second time.

A5 — `sn_mask()` returns `None` before an InitAck is observed and the fragment path reports `FragmentWithoutResolution` rather than substituting a default. A mask too WIDE reads a wraparound as a gap; one too NARROW reads a gap as a wraparound. Either verdict looks decisive and is arbitrary.

A3 — `decapsulate` returns `Transport::{Tcp, Udp}` and `SkipReason::NotTcp` becomes `NotTransport`. UDP was a NAMED SKIP, which was honest that the byte stream had a hole and silent about which: scouting, multicast Join and the entire UDP unicast link all went there, so a capture of a multicast deployment produced a dissection with no messages and no error.

A3 — UDP IS A SECOND FRAMING MODE, not a protocol branch, and that is the finding that shaped the change. A datagram link carries NO length prefix: UDP preserves message boundaries, so one datagram is exactly one wire message (`wz-runtime-tokio/src/udp_pipeline.rs:34-36`). So `PassiveSession::next_datagram` is a sibling entry point to `next_frame` — no buffer to append to, no boundary to search for, no desynchronisation to recover from — while everything above the framing (the fold, the context, the `Carried` decode) is shared.

A3 — `link::Datagram` is deliberately NOT a `Segment` with the TCP fields blank, and `Dissection::datagram_flows()` sits BESIDE the TCP flows rather than inside them. A TCP flow needs a stream assembler and an offset-to-packet map and a UDP flow needs neither; folding them would mean an `Option<StreamAssembler>` that is always `None` on one side and a `stream_offset` that means two different things.

A3 — the UDP header's own `length` field is read rather than inferred from the slice. A captured frame carries Ethernet's 60-byte-minimum padding, and handing those pad bytes to the decoder turns a valid short message into a trailing-garbage parse error.
Round 311y584.decision_summary: R311y584 -- closes A2 and A3, and corrects the work order R311y582 set. A2 takes the passive observer above the transport frame: a Frame's body is decompressed when the session negotiated it and walked best-effort into network records, a Fragment is driven through a per-direction chain router, and every outcome that is not a batch is NAMED rather than collapsed to an empty one. Doing that surfaced a dependency the register missed -- fragment reassembly compares SNs on a ring whose size is the negotiated resolution, which FlowContext did not carry -- so half of A5 landed here, taken from the InitAck rather than folded across both Inits because zenoh makes the acceptor's answer the session value. A3 then found that UDP was not a protocol branch at all: a datagram link carries no length prefix, so one datagram is one whole wire message, and the fix is a second framing mode with its own entry point and its own flow type sitting beside the TCP one. Before it, SkipReason::NotTcp swallowed scouting, multicast Join and the whole UDP unicast link -- a capture of a multicast deployment dissected to no messages and no error. Two implementation shapes were rejected on measurement rather than argument (const-generic slot dimensions, whose defaults do not participate in inference; a derived Debug that would have printed capture payloads into a consumer's logs), and one new test leg found a defect in its own fixture rather than in the code.
verification_bullets: The A2 fragment leg splits ONE OAM record down the MIDDLE, so each half is individually undecodable and only the join can produce a message. A fixture split on a record boundary passes even when the join never happens, which is the shape of a test that proves the harness rather than the code.

A2 legs: a frame carries its batch decoded (2 records, no halt); handshake frames carry `Nothing` rather than acquiring a phantom empty batch; a two-fragment chain reports `Begun` then `Reassembled`; a fragment with no observed InitAck reports `FragmentWithoutResolution` and `sn_mask()` is `None`; an InitAck settles the size parameters and a SYN alone does not.

A3 legs, parser: a UDP datagram is decapsulated rather than skipped; Ethernet padding is not read as payload (the fixture asserts it really is 60 bytes first, so the leg cannot pass on an unpadded frame); both directions of one conversation share a flow key. A3 legs, WIRING: a UDP packet reaches a datagram flow, decodes, and does NOT appear in `skipped()`; two directions reach one flow. Parser tests and wiring tests are separate claims — a decapsulator that works and a dissection that never calls it look identical from the parser's own tests.

A FIXTURE DEFECT WAS FOUND BY ONE OF THOSE LEGS, and the code was right. `both_directions_reach_one_datagram_flow` first swapped only the PORTS and left the addresses alone, which is a different conversation entirely; it reported two flows and that was correct. The fixture now swaps the addresses too, and the mistake is recorded at the site.

TWO SHAPES REJECTED AFTER MEASUREMENT, not after argument. `PassiveSession` was first written with const-generic slot dimensions and defaults; a struct's const-param DEFAULT does not participate in inference, so `PassiveSession::new()` failed to resolve at every call site. Named constants replaced them. And the derived `Debug` was replaced by a hand-written one: `wz_capture::FlowDissection` derives `Debug` over a `PassiveSession`, and the chain routers hold every fragment staged so far, so the derive would have printed a capture's payloads into a consumer's logs.

NOT COVERED, and named rather than left to be discovered: multicast `Join` state is not tracked, and Scout / Hello still have no dissect walker (A6), so a scouting datagram now REACHES the observer and decodes as an unknown transport MID. The prose was the specification and the feature list was the implementation, and nothing compared them. Where a feature list has a stated intent, that intent is a testable claim.

A GROUP MUST NOT SHARE ITS LEAF'S NAME. `Field::find` is first-match-by-name, so wrapping a `locator` string in a group also called `locator` makes every consumer asking for the locator get a nested node. Cheap to fix here; it would have been a puzzling bug in a view.

changes_bullets: A4 — new `passive_keyexpr` module: per-DIRECTION `id -> keyexpr` tables, and the rule that picks between them. A participant keeps ONE table per link (the ids the peer declared, `wz-runtime-tokio/src/linkstate_forward.rs:230-237`) because the other number space is its own and it never looks anything up in it. An observer has neither and must rebuild both.

A4 — the `M` bit is encoder-perspective locality (`sources/codecs/wireexpr.scxml:38-43`): `M = 1` means the id lives in the SENDER's space, `M = 0` in the peer's. So an id seen travelling in direction D resolves against D's table when local and D.peer()'s when nonlocal. Getting this wrong is worse than not resolving at all — an unresolved id is visibly unresolved and a wrongly-resolved one is a confident lie.

A4 — `Resolved` separates three states a blank string would merge: `Literal`, `Empty` (zenoh's `WireExpr::empty()`, a message that genuinely names no key), and `Unresolved { id, owner, suffix }`, which carries enough to render `<unresolved id=17>/pose` rather than nothing. A chained declaration is FLATTENED at bind time; inserting the unresolved form would leave a second id nothing later resolves. Undeclare retires the binding.

A4 — WIRED, not merely provided. `PassiveSession` folds Declares out of the batches `carried` already walks and exposes `keyexprs()`. Leaving it as a library with no caller would repeat exactly the criticism R311y583 made of the pre-A2 context: inferred, then unused by its own crate.

A5 — `FlowContext::batch_size()` and `PassiveFrame::exceeds_negotiated_batch`, the negotiated ceiling's FIRST consumer. It had been decoded, stored and read by nothing. An oversize frame is a sender-side protocol violation, and it is FLAGGED rather than dropped: dropping is what makes a non-conforming peer invisible. Never true before an InitAck — an unknown ceiling cannot be exceeded.

A6 — `walk_scout` / `walk_hello` / `dissect_scouting_message`. A SEPARATE entry point rather than another arm on the transport walk, because the MID spaces OVERLAP: `0x01` is `Scout` on the scouting link and `Init` on a session link, and the transport dispatcher decodes scouting bytes without erroring. A separate space needs a separate door.
A6 — a byte that is not a scouting MID returns `Ok(None)`. An absence, not a failure: these bytes were not a scouting message and the caller decides what they were, mirroring `walk_network_record`.

A6 — the `dissect` feature now selects `wz-codecs/codec-scout` and `codec-hello`. Its own doc said it "selects the whole codec-* MID space on purpose" so an observer can read every message it sees; the scouting half was missing, which is the mechanical reason Scout and Hello had no walker while every transport and network MID had one.

A6 — `Hello`'s locator list is gated by `FLAG_S_HELLO_L` on the HEADER byte, not by anything in the body, so `walk_hello` takes it as a parameter. The per-locator group is named `locator_entry` rather than `locator`: `Field::find` returns the first match by name, so a group sharing its leaf's name shadows the string inside it.
Round 311y585.decision_summary: R311y585 -- closes A4, A5 and A6, leaving A7 as the only open tier-A item. A4 is the one with the real subtlety: a wire key expression is a NUMBER, and which number space it belongs to is decided by the M bit relative to the SENDER, so an observer must rebuild both spaces and pick between them per message. A participant never faces this because one of the two spaces is its own. Resolving into the wrong space is worse than not resolving at all -- an unresolved id is visibly unresolved and a wrongly-resolved one is a confident lie -- so the module separates Literal, Empty and Unresolved rather than collapsing the last two to a blank, and it is folded by the observer out of batches it already walks rather than left as a library with no caller. A5 gives the negotiated batch ceiling its first consumer, as a flagged violation rather than a drop. A6 gives the scouting MID space its own walkers and its own entry point, because that space OVERLAPS the transport one -- 0x01 is Scout there and Init here -- and the transport dispatcher decodes scouting bytes without erroring; the feature that claimed to select the whole codec-* space was also missing the scouting half, which is why those walkers had never been written.
verification_bullets: A4's central leg is the one that would be absent from a resolver written without the M rule: the SAME id, the SAME direction, two different bindings, and the M bit alone decides which. An observer that ignored it would resolve one to the other's path and report it with full confidence.

A4's other legs: a zero id resolves from its suffix alone; `WireExpr::empty()` is its own answer and not an unresolved one; a suffix composes onto the bound base; an id declared before the capture is named with its owner and suffix rather than blanked; a chained declaration flattens; an Undeclare makes a later reference unresolved again rather than stale; a declaration in one direction does not leak into the other. Plus the WIRING leg — a Declare inside a real Frame populates the tables and a later Push resolves through them.

THAT WIRING LEG CAUGHT ITS OWN FIXTURE TWICE, and the code was right both times. First `header: 0` erased the MID, so the record decoded as `Unknown` and the table stayed empty. Then, with the MID restored, the batch held TWO records: the wireexpr's suffix presence is announced by the `N` bit (`0x20`) on the PARENT header, and with it clear the encoder dropped the suffix and its bytes parsed as a second record. Both would have passed an assertion that merely matched the `Carried::Batch` arm, so the leg counts the records instead.

A5 is pinned by a CONTROL: the same frame against a session whose acceptor agreed to 65535 is not flagged, and against one that agreed to 16 it is. Without the negative arm the flag could be a constant.

A6 pins the MID-space overlap by feeding the SAME bytes to both dispatchers and asserting the transport one ACCEPTS them and calls them something else. That is the failure the separate entry point exists to prevent, and asserting it makes the reason non-obvious-to-a-later-reader into a test.

A6's `Hello` leg has its own control: identical body bytes with the header's `L` clear must stop the walk after the zid and NOT read the trailing bytes as locators. The span end is asserted, not just the field's absence.

changes_bullets: A7 — new `wz-capi-dissect` crate: the C ABI over the dissection surface. Five functions, and the memory rule is the whole contract — every string the library returns is owned by it and released with `wz_dissect_string_free`. Nothing else crosses allocated, no callbacks run, no handle outlives its call.

A7 — THE DESIGN CHOICE, and it is the substance of this item rather than any defect. A wide ABI mirroring the Rust tree (C structs for `Field` / `Span` / `FieldValue`, a tag per variant) gives C a typed tree and makes every walker wz adds an ABI change: a new `FieldValue` variant is a discriminant an already-built consumer has no case for. `dissect` gains walkers as routine — R311y585 alone added two — so that ABI would break as routine. The narrow ABI over JSON adds NODES rather than symbols, and an older consumer keeps working and sees fields it does not recognise. That is the same forward-compatibility posture zenoh's own unknown-extension policy takes.

A7 — the deciding fact was already in the tree: `dissect::to_json` exists and takes NO serde dependency, built for R311y579's G6 whose measured failure was a consumer that could not get a decode out of the library at all. The same answer applies for the same reason.

A7 — its OWN crate, not an addition to `wz-capi-c`. That crate's entire contract is "a zenoh-c drop-in": every symbol in it answers to an upstream header, and the census lanes read it that way. A wz-specific dissection ABI living there would mean a consumer could not tell which half it was linking, and a zenoh-c symbol census would start reporting symbols zenoh-c never had.

A7 — the pcap entry point returns a per-flow SUMMARY, not the whole field tree. A capture holds an unbounded number of messages and one string carrying all of them is a shape that works for a test and fails for a session; a consumer walks the flows, then expands the messages it wants. The skipped-packet count is IN the summary: a consumer that cannot see it reads a dissection with holes as a complete one.
A7 — `wz_dissect_abi_version` is a SYMBOL and memory-rule revision, not a JSON-shape one, and the header says so. Freezing the JSON shape would reintroduce exactly the coupling this design avoids.
Round 311y586.decision_summary: R311y586 -- closes A7 and with it the whole of tier A. A7 was the one item that was a DESIGN CHOICE rather than a defect, and the choice is between two ABIs that are not equally durable: a wide one mirroring the Rust field tree, which makes every walker wz adds an ABI break for consumers already built, and a narrow one over a self-describing document, where a new walker adds nodes and an older consumer keeps working. wz took the second, and the deciding fact was already in the tree -- dissect::to_json exists with no serde dependency, built for the G6 failure of a consumer that could not get a decode out of the library at all. It lives in its own crate rather than in wz-capi-c, whose entire contract is answering to zenoh-c's header. Real C compiled against the header, linked the cdylib, and printed the KeepAlive field tree before freeing it through the library's own free; the header was checked as C and as C++ because the consumer this exists for is [REDACTED]. The seven tier-A items R311y582 registered are now all closed, and the highest-value next action is not code: eight unpushed commits have regenerated every entry-flag codec, widened a feature, and added a workspace member, and none of that has met hosted CI.
verification_bullets: REAL C LINKED THE CDYLIB AND READ THE TREE. `gcc` compiled a consumer against `include/wz_dissect.h`, linked `libwz_capi_dissect.so`, and printed `{"name":"KeepAlive","start":0,"end":1,"kind":"nested","fields":[...` before freeing through the library's own free. Exit 0. The Rust-side tests prove the walkers; only this proves the BOUNDARY, which is the only thing this crate adds.

The header was syntax-checked as BOTH C and C++ (`gcc -fsyntax-only` and `g++ -x c++`), because the consumer this exists for is [REDACTED] and a header that only compiles as C would be found at integration time rather than here.

The ABI legs, driven through raw pointers rather than by calling the Rust functions directly: a transport message crosses as JSON; undecodable bytes return `WZ_DISSECT_ERR_DECODE` rather than UNWINDING, which is the leg that matters most since a panic across `extern "C"` is undefined behaviour; null arguments are refused before any dereference, on both entry points and on the out-pointer; freeing null is a no-op so a consumer's cleanup needs no guard of its own; a pcapng file is `WZ_DISSECT_ERR_BAD_CAPTURE` and hands back NO string.

`CString::new` is checked rather than unwrapped. `to_json` escapes control characters so an interior NUL should not occur — but an unwrap there would convert a walker bug into a panic across the FFI boundary, and an error code is the only correct answer at that seam.

changes_bullets: THE OBSERVER HAD NO CLOCK, so its reassembly deadline was `u64::MAX` and nothing swept. `PassiveSession::with_reassembly_window` + `observe_at(now_ms)` make it enforceable, and the instant is an INPUT rather than something read off the host: a pcap packet carries when it was seen and a live tap knows when it arrived, which also makes a replayed file deterministic and keeps a 100x replay from expiring chains that never expired. `new()` still has an unreachable deadline, so no existing consumer acquired an expiry by upgrading.

`wz-capture` NEVER ENABLED `reassembly`. Building `-p wz-capture` alone, a Fragment stayed opaque -- the capture front end could not do the per-channel reassembly the client's spec asks for. Invisible in a workspace build because `wz-runtime-tokio` turns the same feature on and cargo unifies it back. Now default-on, with the no-default arm kept and both built.

THE LIVE SOURCE (B1) EXISTS: `wz-runtime-tokio::live_capture` -- `LiveTap` over the `AfPacketSocket` R311y579 built for the raweth LINK, a `PacketSource` seam so the FEED LOOP is provable without privilege, and `pump` into the same `Dissection` a pcap file feeds. Placed here and not in `wz-capture` because that crate is `no_std` with zero third-party dependencies on purpose.

THE INSTANT IS `SCM_TIMESTAMP`, not a host clock read after `recvmsg`. Timing the READER would show scheduling delay as network delay and would expire chains that were never late. `SO_TIMESTAMP` failing at open is a hard failure rather than a silent fallback.

THE TAP READ 476 OF 20 000 AND SAID NOTHING. Measured, not modelled: the kernel default receive buffer (208 KiB) dropped 99.7 % of a single-process loopback burst. Asking for 8 MiB via `SO_RCVBUF` changed NOTHING because `net.core.rmem_max` clamps it; `SO_RCVBUFFORCE` took it to 18 725 read at 60 123 pkt/s -- a 31x defect that one setsockopt closed, behind a sentence that said performance was out of scope.

DROPS ARE VISIBLE (`PACKET_STATISTICS`). Not a performance feature: a packet the kernel discarded leaves a hole indistinguishable from one the network made, so SN-gap loss tracking would report the analyst's own machine as network loss. `wz_capture::SkippedPacket` states that rule one layer up and the tap was breaking it one layer down. The read-and-clear semantics are documented rather than hidden behind an accumulator that would break a second caller silently.

FIVE ACCUMULATIONS GREW WITHOUT BOUND once a source stopped ending -- the retained byte stream of every connection (much the largest), the run map, decoded frames, the skipped list, and the flow table. `DissectionLimits` bounds all five and `DissectionDrops` counts what each bound cost. Defaults are all `None`, which is the FILE behaviour unchanged; `for_live_tap()` is a starting point and says it is not a tuned one. The flow table is the one that cannot be trimmed in place, so past the cap the least recently active is evicted.

TWO DEFECTS TRIMMING INTRODUCED, both caught by the tests written for them. (1) The delivery slice indexed a RETAINED tail with an ABSOLUTE offset, which diverge the moment trimming starts and would have fed the observer plausible-looking wrong bytes. (2) Run offsets were recorded as `stream.len()`, i.e. relative, so `retain` comparing them against an absolute base emptied the whole run map. Both are now absolute, and a trimmed offset is UNANSWERABLE rather than answered by the nearest surviving run.

Round 311y595.decision_summary: R311y595 -- the dissect field-name census. A census inverts it: an addition DEMANDS the codec's name, a rename reds twice over, and a gap is carried by name with a reason that the gate forces out once the gap closes. carry_forward_bullets: R311y599 = the first step of the MCU pool remodel: `wz-link-lwip::rx_pool` gives the four MCU buffer-pool emits their first LIFECYCLE consumer, and with it the freelist-accounting gate the tree has never had.

WHY THIS ORDER: the user asked whether a structure supporting both a CPU filler and a DMA filler is possible. It is, and it is already declared rather than hypothetical -- SCE models `rx_dispatch: isr_to_pool` vs `worker_tick` as two policies over ONE pool (`vendor/sce/sce-build/src/mesh/deploy.rs:797-806`, conditional default IsrToPool when burst_pps is declared), and `deploy/ap_mcu_pair.yaml` already uses both in one file (mcu_node lines 58/67 isr_to_pool, ap_node lines 174/183 worker_tick). So the correct shape is ONE seam with N adapters, not two modes inside wz; and the copy adapter must be the one that runs in CI so the seam is never dead code.

BLOCKER FOUND, and it is for SCE not for wz: a descriptor-ring adapter cannot be built on the emitted arm path, because nothing can produce the ADDRESS of an armed-but-unfilled slot. `Slot<DmaArmedRx>` has only `dma_start_rx` and the inherited `idx()`; `read`/`write` exist only on `Slot<CpuMut>` and `Slot<CpuRef>`; the pool's `storage` field is private. A MAC's buffer-request callback needs a `*mut u8` at arm time. Measured at vendor/sce ef4c2fe4d5. This is the next hand-off to SCE and it gates step 3, not step 1.

TARGET IS REAL, which changes the calculus recorded in earlier rounds: the intended board is an Infineon KIT_T2G-B-H_LITE (TRAVEO T2G CYT4BF, dual Cortex-M7), with a working lwIP port and a hardware-validated UDP round trip. Its driver contract is an EXACT match for the FSM's arm/complete pair -- `cy_ethif.c:1727` asks the application for a buffer via an `rxgetbuff` callback, and CEDI `readRxBuf` (cedi.h:2131-2153) documents itself as "swaps out the buffer and replaces it with a new one", i.e. a buffer SWAP not a copy. So arming is genuinely reachable on this target once the address gap above is closed. The M7 D-cache also makes SCE's post-RX cache-invalidate emit meaningful for the first time, which requires flipping a wz pool to `cache-policy: maintain`.

DESIGN DECISION recorded so it is not relitigated: bind the future T2G adapter BELOW Infineon's ECM, to the stable `Cy_ETHIF_` PDL layer, rather than forking ECM. ECM already occupies the callback slot (`eth_internal.c:332-336` registers both rxframecb and rxgetbuff, one slot per instance), so the two cannot coexist; forking a vendor SDK recurs at every release, and ECM's value to wz is only PHY / link bring-up since wz has its own stack.

NEXT: convert `LwipUdpSocket` to a borrow-and-return receive so the seam has a production caller. `try_recv` returning an owned `Datagram<N>` is exactly what slot ownership cannot preserve, so the conversion is an API change across six files; the planned shape is an additive closure-style `recv_with` that fits the existing call sites (they use the payload immediately and inside one RefCell borrow) rather than a Drop guard, which the `Rc<RefCell<SessionRxSocket>>` in wz-session-lwip would fight.

BOARD IS IMMINENT, not hypothetical (user, this session), which reorders the queue: the SCE armed-slot ADDRESS gap is the only item with external lead time, so it goes upstream FIRST and in parallel with wz-local work. Everything else here is wz-local and can move at wz's pace; that one cannot.

HONEST GROUNDS for this commit, recorded because the obvious two are both wrong: it is NOT performance and NOT parity. Measured -- stock zenoh has zero DMA / descriptor-ring / slot-pool occurrences across io/ and zenoh-buffers, and zenoh-pico has exactly one (serial circular mode, a different shape), so this is a SUPERSET with no reference to diff against; and at the deploy's own declared rates (burst_pps 50 scout / 200 session / 20 serial) eliminating one 1500-byte memcpy is on the order of 0.04% of a 300 MHz M7. An earlier claim in this session that the DMA path is "faster and lower power on MCU" was made WITHOUT measuring and is retracted. The real justification is determinism (arena fixed before the first packet, no allocation under load, burst absorbed by the ring) plus the one thing this commit actually delivers: the pool FSM had zero consumers and therefore zero gates, and SCE shipped a defect into it that wz could not see.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-link-lwip/src/rx_pool.rs (new): the `RxSlots` trait plus an `impl_rx_slots!` macro instantiating it over each SCE-generated MCU buffer-pool emit. The trait is reserve / buf / bytes / release / free_count / slot_idx, with the emit's own phantom-typed `Slot<CpuMut>` as the associated type so the generator's compile-time lifecycle rules survive being seen through the trait. This gives the four `out/wz-link-lwip/*_pool_mcu.rs` emits their FIRST lifecycle consumer; until now `rx_sockets` read only their SLOT_COUNT / SLOT_SIZE constants and the seven-state FSM had zero callers tree-wide on the MCU tier.

The seam is cut at "the reader does not learn how the bytes arrived". A CPU filler copies out of an lwIP pbuf; a descriptor-ring MAC writes the slot directly; both end at a slot holding bytes, borrowed then returned. That is what lets one session tier sit above both without branching on which it got.

The unicast session impl carries the SAME cfg as the module it names (`not(buffer-pool-session-rx-slim)` for `session_rx_pool_mcu`, the feature for `session_rx_pool_mcu_minimal`), because lib.rs compiles exactly one of the two. The tests alias whichever is active rather than cfg-ing themselves out, so the slim lane exercises the seam instead of reporting green on nothing.

Scope stated so it is not stretched: this is the pool-facing half only. It does NOT model arming, and the module says why in its own docs — a MAC's buffer-request callback needs the ADDRESS of an armed-but-unfilled slot, and the emitted `Slot<DmaArmedRx>` carries only `idx()` while the pool's `storage` is private. carry_forward_bullets: R311y600 = the CPU-fill adapter over the R311y599 seam: `PooledUdpRx<P, Q>` receives into pool slots and lends them through `recv_with`. Step 1 of the MCU pool remodel is now complete on the RECEIVE side — trait, adapter, and the gates that make both honest.

WHAT THIS IS AND IS NOT, restated because both obvious readings are wrong: it is NOT a performance change (same one copy, and at burst_pps 50/200/20 the copy was never the cost) and it is NOT parity (neither stock zenoh nor zenoh-pico has a slot-pool shape at all — measured zero occurrences in zenoh `io/` + `zenoh-buffers`, one in pico and that one is serial circular DMA). It is the substitutability: the session tier above `recv_with` cannot tell a CPU filler from a peripheral one, which is the only reason a T2G adapter can be dropped in later without touching anything above it.

NEXT, in the order that respects lead time. (1) The SCE hand-off is WRITTEN and is the only item with external lead time: `claudedocs/wz-forge-handoff-armed-slot-address.md` on the SCE machine asks for a narrow address accessor on `Slot<DmaArmedRx>`, without which no descriptor-ring adapter can be built at all. ⚠ That file is under SCE's gitignored `claudedocs/`, so it exists on that machine only. (2) Convert the six `try_recv` call sites to `recv_with` so the adapter has production callers — until then its only consumers are its own tests, which is the trap this repo keeps paying for. Its driver contract matches the FSM exactly — `cy_ethif.c:1727` requests a buffer from the application via `rxgetbuff`, and CEDI `readRxBuf` (cedi.h:2131-2153) documents a buffer SWAP rather than a copy. Flipping a wz pool to `cache-policy: maintain` at that point makes SCE's post-RX invalidate emit meaningful for the first time; every wz pool is `cache-policy: none` today and the reason is recorded at `sources/network/session_rx_pool_mcu.scxml:32-43`.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-link-lwip/src/rx_pool.rs: `PooledUdpRx<P: RxSlots, const Q: usize>` — the CPU-fill adapter, an lwIP UDP socket whose received bytes land in pool slots instead of an inline `heapless::Vec` per queue entry. Its recv thunk reserves a slot BEFORE copying (a drained pool is back-pressure and the datagram is dropped counted, never partially staged), copies the pbuf into the slot, and enqueues `Received{slot,len,src_addr,src_port}`.

`recv_with(|bytes, addr, port| ..)` is the read side, and the closure rather than a return value is the seam: bytes live in a pool slot, so returning them by value would be a copy and returning them by reference would leave the caller holding a slot. The slot is back on the freelist before the call returns, on every path. This is the shape a descriptor-ring adapter will also expose, so the session tier above never learns which filler it got.
`Q` is asserted `<= P::SLOT_COUNT` at bind. A queue deeper than the pool can fill would never reach its declared depth, and failing at startup is better than a permanent silent under-run.

The enqueue-failure path RELEASES the slot it could not queue. Without it a burst permanently shrinks the freelist and the socket eventually goes silent with no error anywhere — and a drop COUNTER cannot see it, because the count rises identically either way. `free_slots()` and `rx_drop_count()` are both public so a deploy can watch the two together and tell a drained pool from a full queue.

Six tests: the trait's five (dims agreement with the socket tier, one full cycle read back through the emit's own `slot_state`, the freelist returning to full over three rounds, slot non-aliasing, per-pool dims) plus two on the adapter (loopback round trip asserting the slot is OUT while queued and BACK after `recv_with`, and the overflow leak guard).
Round 311y600.decision_summary: R311y600 -- PooledUdpRx, the CPU-fill adapter over the R311y599 RxSlots seam. An lwIP UDP socket that stages received datagrams into SCE-generated pool slots and lends them through a recv_with closure, returning the slot before the call returns on every path. The closure is the seam rather than a returned value because bytes living in a slot cannot be handed out by value without a copy nor by reference without the caller holding a slot. Reserve happens BEFORE the copy so a drained pool is counted back-pressure, and the enqueue-failure path releases the slot it could not queue -- a leak that a drop COUNTER cannot see, since the count rises identically whether or not the slot came back, which is why the guard asserts free_slots instead. Two damage probes confirm both guards fire, and probe 1 reddens exactly one test while the other six stay green. Explicitly NOT a performance change and NOT parity: the copy count is unchanged and neither stock zenoh nor pico has this shape. What it buys is substitutability -- the tier above recv_with cannot tell a CPU filler from a peripheral one, which is what lets the T2G adapter drop in later.

A probe that only its own leg can see, which is what distinguishes a real guard from a test that fails because the crate stopped building.

DAMAGE PROBE 2 (the read-side leak): replacing `recv_with`'s `pool.release(received.slot)` with `core::mem::forget` reddens `pooled_socket_loopback_round_trip` and the overflow test's final drain assertion, and leaves the four pure-trait tests green.
Both probes were reverted from a pre-damage copy and the revert verified by grepping the marker to zero occurrences rather than assumed.

The overflow test's arithmetic is derived, not guessed: `heapless::spsc::Queue<T, Q>` holds `Q - 1`, so `Q = 2` with four datagrams sent gives one queued and three refused, and the test asserts `rx_drop_count() == 3` alongside `free_slots() == SLOT_COUNT - 1`. Asserting only the drop count would pass on the leaking build.
